Coverage score follows the facts sheet (single-site family, <= 8 names), not the record's 40-name claim.

skeptic: The equity-relevant event (a line down) is disclosed by 8-K within four business days, so the only tradable residual is undisclosed partial run-rate drops; with seven names and rare events the record's own feasibility gate (median >20 cloud-free detections per site-quarter) may stop the project. Archive fetch and polygon definitions are unverified. Coverage claim of ~40 names contradicts the facts-sheet family cap; scored on the cap.

verifier.changes: C lowered from the panel median 3 to 2. Evidence: the anchor for 2 is "sold by several vendors". TESTED HERE (one vendor search plus two page fetches) found satellite thermal plant-activity monitoring sold by at least five vendors, not two: Earth-i SAVANT (copper and nickel smelters, daily, history to early 2016, ESA release names hedge funds and CTAs as clients), SatVu (high-resolution thermal pitched at trading and investment with a steel activity offering), LaGrand (thermal-IR steel plant monitoring, procurement customers, claims a plant shutdown detected before media), plus the Wood Mackenzie Genscape and Kayrros names already in the record. The exact mechanism (VIIRS Nightfire nightly profiles at named mills) is published: Elvidge et al. Remote Sensing 2023 and the Payne Institute steel-flaring commentary report VNF profiles for more than 1,000 steel mills with COVID and Ukraine disruption examples, and a 2025 Elvidge deck profiles U.S. Steel Granite City. The record's claimed edge (sub-$5B single-site names that vendors skip) is REASONED only, and for the seven retained tickers the on/off state is 8-K disclosed, so "more granular in a way that matters" is not shown. All other criteria stay at the panel median. A stays 5: FIRMS area CSV is structured, the MAP_KEY is verified in the facts sheet, and TESTED HERE the FIRMS download page states VIIRS S-NPP 375 m coverage from 20 January 2012 and the API docs list VIIRS_SNPP_SP (standard processing) as a date-addressable product, so archive access through the same keyed API is confirmed; the one new fact (S-NPP production ceased 2 November 2026, so the record's VIIRS_SNPP_NRT URL returns no new data) is fixed by a product-name swap to NOAA-20/21. L stays 4: EDGAR Item 2.02 dates computed TESTED HERE give 17 to 35 day leads for Q1-Q3 across the seven names and the hypothesis fixes measurement at T-20. S stays 2 (record's own vet and red team; additionally REASONED that CENX potlines, OLN chlor-alkali, LXU ammonia and TROX pigment reactors are enclosed processes that are weak 375 m IR emitters, so the mechanism really covers CLF, SXC and EXP). U stays 1 (seven names, facts sheet family cap). H stays 4: TESTED HERE CMR shows VNP14IMG and VNP46A2 granules from 2012-01-19, but the FIRMS FAQ states standard "ML" files lag 2-3 months and the download page says NRT is replaced by standard data with about a 5 month lag, and NRT geolocation and granule completeness differ from standard, so a backtest on standard data versus live NRT is a real but minor look-ahead caveat; the 2012-2017 history is S-NPP only while live collection must now be NOAA-20/21. G stays 5.
verifier.refutation: This signal should not be in the top ten because almost every path to a tradeable, backtestable edge is blocked. (1) Universe: the facts sheet caps it at seven named tickers, so at most 28 earnings events a year, and the hypothesis further restricts to quarters where a more-than-15% site-days drop was NOT disclosed by 8-K or press before T-20; the record's own red team expects 10 to 20 usable quarters in the whole 2019-2025 window, which cannot distinguish a real coefficient from polygon overfitting. (2) The equity-relevant event is disclosed: a line down at CLF, SXC or CENX is an 8-K or press release within days and sits in consensus by T-1, so the undisclosed residual is a partial run-rate that a 375 m thresholded active-fire detection (near-binary per overpass) cannot resolve. (3) The mechanism physically covers only three of the seven names (CLF blast furnaces and EAFs, SXC coke ovens, EXP kilns); CENX aluminium potlines, OLN chlor-alkali cells, LXU ammonia reformers and TROX pigment reactors are enclosed processes that are weak IR emitters at VIIRS resolution (REASONED), so effective coverage is three names. (4) It is not uncrowded: VNF per-mill profiles for 1,000-plus steel mills including a US mill are published by Elvidge and the Payne Institute, the nightly data behind them is freely distributed by EOG, and Earth-i, SatVu, LaGrand, Kayrros and Wood Mackenzie sell plant thermal activity to traders; whatever edge remains is the REASONED claim that nobody bothers with sub-$5B single-site names. (5) Data continuity is worse than the record states: S-NPP FIRMS production ceased 2 November 2026, so the record's primary URL now returns nothing new, the 2012-2017 history is S-NPP only, and live collection must move to NOAA-20/21 with different overpass times; the backtest archive is standard processing that replaces NRT with a 2-5 month lag and differs in geolocation and granule completeness; and the Black Marble secondary is 9 days behind, not 1-2. (6) The lead time is genuine but ordinary (17 to 35 days) and the hypothesis fixes T-20, no better than several higher-coverage physical signals. A signal with one-percent coverage, a near-binary noisy residual, published mechanism, vendor competition, and a sensor transition in the month it would go live does not belong above signals that trade dozens of names each quarter.
verifier.release_schedule_check: Source side (TESTED HERE): the FIRMS FAQ at https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/data/tools/firms/faq states VIIRS 375 m NRT latency under 3 hours, so the last night of the quarter is in the area CSV by day +1 and a conservative cloud-screened full-quarter site-days count is final by day +1 to +3; the Black Marble secondary (VNP46A2 standard) is 9 days behind per CMR, so a Black Marble-based reading is final about day +10. Release side (TESTED HERE from data.sec.gov submissions JSON, last ten 8-K Item 2.02 filings per name, days after calendar quarter end): CLF 19-23 for Q1-Q3 and 34-55 for Q4 (median 34); OLN 27-31 (median 30; one 8-day pre-announcement, one 73); SXC 27-31, Q4 48 (median 30); LXU 28-31, Q4 56-65 (median 29); EXP 29-30, fiscal Q4 49-50 (median 30); CENX 31-39, Q4 50-51 (median 37); TROX 25-37, Q4 44-50 (median 37). Lead = release lag minus 3: CLF 16-20 days (Q1-Q3), OLN/SXC/LXU/EXP 24-28, CENX/TROX 22-36, with Q4 prints 31-62. Across the seven names the median lead is about 27 days, straddling the 27/28 boundary; the hypothesis fixes measurement at T-20, inside the 14-27 band, so L=4. Note the record's primary product name is now stale: S-NPP FIRMS production ceased 2 November 2026, so live collection must use VIIRS_NOAA20_NRT or VIIRS_NOAA21_NRT (same format, same latency).
verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: Vendor search (TESTED HERE, one WebSearch plus page fetches): Earth-i SAVANT sells daily smelter activity indices (copper ~70%, nickel ~80% of world capacity, infrared and visible bands, history to early 2016; the ESA business news release names hedge funds, banks, CTAs and traders as customers); SatVu markets high-resolution thermal imagery for trading and investment with a steel activity product and a planned Dunkirk steel case study; LaGrand (Switzerland) sells thermal-IR steel plant monitoring to procurement buyers and claims it detected a steel plant shutdown before the media; Wood Mackenzie Genscape and Kayrros (already in the record) cover refineries; no vendor found selling per-ticker site-days for the seven retained US names, and no result for RS Metrics or SpaceKnow in this search. Literature: Elvidge et al. 2013 Remote Sensing (VIIRS Nightfire algorithm, steel mills named as detected sources); Elvidge et al. 2023 Remote Sensing 15(19) 4760 (daily global IR-emitter program, nightly and monthly profiles 'suitable for analyzing industrial production, identifying disruption events, and tracking recovery'); Payne Institute commentary (Elvidge, Zhizhin, Taber, Bazilian, 2022) on VNF profiles for more than 1,000 steel mills with COVID and Ukraine disruption examples; a 2025 Elvidge deck (search snippet; PDF now 404) with a VNF profile of U.S. Steel Granite City; a 2017 Remote Sensing of Environment paper identifying industrial heat sources from VNF time series; a February 2026 preprint finding SWIR/MIR fire products capture steelmaking activity as high-temperature anomalies. Net: the mechanism is published at the single-mill level with US examples and the nightly VNF data behind it is freely distributed by EOG (unreachable from this container only), and plant thermal activity is sold by several vendors; the specific sub-$5B per-ticker version is not sold but its edge is REASONED, not shown.

rows.name: State WARN notices as a plant-closure and restructuring nowcast

justifications.text: A: five state pages are DATA but need HTML, xlsx and PDF parsing (CA prior years are PDFs; IL monthly xlsx; NY legacy HTML); LaborCurrent key is verified in the facts sheet but the evaluation tier is 30-day delayed, 10 calls/day, 10 records/call, 90 days of history, so it is not the backtest source the record claims; Texas blocked from the container; L: the record's own measurement is the quarter's aggregate notified headcount at T-1 (lead_time_days 1); S: record cut to 2 because unmatched-to-8-K notices are immaterial by construction and the IJPE 2022 study finds closures positive and layoff-only flat (sign ambiguity); C: LaborCurrent sells the 8-K-cross-referenced, ticker-mapped version to funds at $49-499/mo, WARNTracker and LayoffData aggregate (record 2); U: only CA, NY, IL, WA, FL are reachable under terms from the container, so the record's ~40%/500 names overstates reachable coverage and qualifying events are 10-30 per quarter; H: FL list 2017-2026, IL archive visible, CA prior years as PDFs give 5+ years for three states, NY only 2023-2025, WA unknown, notice dates recorded so point-in-time is sound but reconstruction from PDFs is required; G: state government pages are public (5) but LaborCurrent's evaluation-tier terms are unread and LayoffData robots disallows /api/ and /search/ (mild flag).
justifications.lead: Quarter aggregate is final at T-1 -> 1 day -> L=1. Individual notices precede the layoff by 60 days and the company's own disclosure by 0-60 days, but the hypothesis measures at T-1, so the full-quarter reading has no lead over the release.

justifications.text: A: five state WARN pages are DATA but need xlsx/HTML/PDF parsing, Texas is blocked from the container, and the verified LaborCurrent key is an evaluation tier (30-day delayed, 10 calls/day, 10 records/call, 90 days history per the facts sheet) so live national coverage needs the $49/mo tier; L: the record freezes the per-ticker count at T-1, so the full reading is final one day before the release (anchor 1); S: Phase 1 lowered signal_noise to 2 because unmatched notices are by construction the ones management deemed immaterial (no Item 2.05 8-K), the literature finds closures positive and layoffs flat so the sign is split, and a suit-cluster-like distress loading is already in short interest; C: LaborCurrent sells the 8-K-cross-referenced ticker-mapped version to funds at $49-499/mo, WARNTracker and LayoffData aggregate, journalists watch the state pages (several vendors, anchor 2); U: the record's ~40%/500 names assumed national coverage, but reachable-under-terms coverage today is five states plus a 30-day-delayed national tier, which the facts-sheet principle for N28/N29 says to score honestly, putting it in the 5-19% band with only 10-30 qualifying events per quarter; H: FL 2017+, IL archive, CA prior years as PDFs, NY 2023+, WA unknown, and the LaborCurrent evaluation tier holds only 90 days (contradicting the record's 'historical' claim), so the backtest must be reconstructed from state archives (anchor 3); G: state government public records, legal_risk 1 in the record, LayoffData robots flag applies only to a dropped fallback.
justifications.lead: Event stream, not a quarter aggregate: a notice is public 1-7 days after filing and 0-60 days before the layoff date. The record's hypothesis counts notices filed in the 75 days before the release and freezes at T-1, so release day minus T-1 = 1 day. Freezing at T-5 would cost almost no information (notices accrue slowly) and would lift L to 2, but that is not what the record specifies.

justifications.text: A: five state pages are DATA but need xlsx/PDF/HTML parsing, Texas is blocked from the container, and the LaborCurrent evaluation key verified in the facts sheet is 30-day delayed, 10 calls/day, 10 records/call, 90 days of history, which cannot serve either a live T-1 read or a backtest, while live national coverage needs $49/month, so 3; L: the quarter's notified headcount is final at T-1 by the record's own measurement window, so 1; S: vet lowered to 2: closures earn positive returns per the 2022 IJPE study (sign ambiguity) and notices without an 8-K Item 2.05 are immaterial by construction; C: LaborCurrent sells the 8-K-cross-referenced, ticker-mapped version to funds and WARNTracker, LayoffData, Apify and layofftracker also sell or publish it, so 2; U: the ~40% (500 names) figure is REASONED and counts states not reachable; the five reachable states cover roughly 30% of US employment and give only partial per-ticker series, so 3 on what is reachable under terms; H: FL 2017+, IL archive, CA prior years only as PDFs, NY 2023+ on legacy pages, WA unknown, LaborCurrent eval 90 days: reconstructed per state, so 3; G: state government pages are public, mild flags are LaborCurrent terms unread and LayoffData robots disallowing /api/ and /search/, so 4.
justifications.lead: Notices arrive continuously; the per-company quarterly aggregate is final only at T-1 (record: 'final at T-1'). Lead over the earnings release = 1 day. The 0-60 day lead the record cites is over the layoff date, not the release.

concerns: data-engineer: The facts sheet contradicts the record: LaborCurrent's $0 tier holds 90 days of history at 10 records per call, so the national backtest must come from state archives (PDF parsing) or the $49/mo tier after grading. Texas (largest manufacturing state) is unreachable from the container. Subsidiary-name resolution to tickers is the real engineering cost. Expect a few dozen qualifying events per year, so this is an overlay, not a standalone series.

quant-pm: The facts sheet's description of the LaborCurrent evaluation tier (90 days of history, 100 records/day, 30-day delay) means it serves neither the backtest the record assigned to it nor a live T-1 read; the record should be corrected. Residual information after the 8-K cross-check is small by construction and sign-ambiguous; the record itself calls this an overlay with a few dozen events per year. Texas, the largest manufacturing state, is unreachable without the paid tier.

skeptic: The record's claim that the $0 LaborCurrent tier is 'enough for the backtest' is contradicted by the facts sheet (90 days of history, 100 records/day); the backtest must be rebuilt from state PDFs. Expected sample is a few dozen qualifying events per year across the universe, with sign uncertain inside a 2-10 day window; any hit likely loads on the distress factor already in short interest.

rows.name: ATS open-requisition count and wording shifts

justifications.text: A: Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and SmartRecruiters are documented keyless JSON APIs with probe_status DATA; the Workday POST endpoint returned 200 with jobPostings (TESTED HERE in record) but is undocumented; iCIMS is per-tenant HTML; L: final reading at T-2 per measurement_window; S: record cut to 2 because QTD posting changes are dominated by sector/seasonal hiring cycles and a disappearing req cannot be signed as pull versus fill until several quarters of median time-to-fill exist; C: LinkUp, Revelio Labs, Lightcast, Thinknum and Textkernel sell company-level posting counts to many funds (record 2), req-level pull/fill granularity is the only differentiator and is unproven; U: 250-320 names (19-25%) on documented APIs per record, count unverified and likely skewed to software, Workday doubling excluded pending per-tenant terms; H: every ATS API returns current postings only (TESTED HERE in record), Wayback denied by network policy, Common Crawl CDX unreliable, so zero history and daily archiving must start now; G: the record does not state that the four documented APIs' terms were read, Workday and iCIMS are AMBER per tenant, so terms are unread or ambiguous.
justifications.lead: Daily snapshots through T-2; reading final 2 trading days before release -> L=2. Postings have no quarter-end concept, so there is no earlier 'full-quarter' point.

justifications.text: A: Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and SmartRecruiters are documented keyless JSON APIs probed DATA; the Workday POST endpoint (TESTED HERE in record) and iCIMS HTML are AMBER and excluded from this score; L: final reading at T-2 per the record (2-6 day band); S: Phase 1 signal_noise 2 because a raw count decline is unsigned without req-level pull-versus-fill classification, which needs a time-to-fill baseline that does not exist yet, and sector hiring cycles, year-end freezes and the economy-wide AI headcount restraint dominate the series; C: LinkUp, Revelio, Lightcast, Thinknum and Textkernel sell company-level posting counts to many funds and Gutierrez et al. (Management Science 2020) published the effect, so sold by several vendors (2); the wording/pull-fill angle is a variant, not a new series; U: the record's 250-320 names (19-25%) on the four open APIs is REASONED, not enumerated, skews to software/internet, and straddles the 260-name boundary, so scored conservatively in the 5-19% band; H: zero history, APIs expose current postings only (TESTED HERE in record), Wayback is denied by network policy, no backfill mechanism exists (anchor 1); G: documented public job-board APIs with an intended-use/attribution flavour (mild flag, 4); Workday undocumented and iCIMS per-tenant terms would be 3 if included.
justifications.lead: Daily snapshots run from fiscal-quarter start to T-2; the reading is final 2 days before the release (release day minus 2 = 2 days). No quarter-end dependency.

justifications.text: A: Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and SmartRecruiters are documented keyless JSON APIs probed DATA in Phase 0, which meets the 5 anchor for the data the signal uses (current postings); L: final reading at T-2 per the record, so 2; S: vet lowered to 2: QTD posting declines are dominated by sector hiring cycles and year-end freezes, a disappearing req is unsigned (pulled vs filled) until median time-to-fill is known, which needs history that does not exist; C: LinkUp, Revelio, Lightcast, Thinknum and Textkernel sell company-level posting counts and Gutierrez et al. (Management Science 2020) is published, the mid-cap and req-level gap is REASONED, so 2 (1 is arguable); U: the 250-320 names on documented APIs is REASONED and unverified, those platforms skew to tech, the Workday leg that would double coverage is undocumented and terms-AMBER, so 65-250 is the evidenced band, 3; H: zero history, Wayback blocked, no backfill at all, facts sheet lists S19-type forward collection, so 1; G: terms of the documented APIs are unread in the record, Workday is an undocumented internal endpoint with per-tenant terms, iCIMS is AMBER, so 3.
justifications.lead: Daily snapshots from fiscal-quarter start; signal uses the final 8 weeks and is final at T-2 (record). Lead over the release = 2 days.

concerns: data-engineer: No backtest is possible today; go/no-go only after ~3 quarters of snapshots. Pull-vs-fill signing requires an estimated median time-to-fill per board, which itself needs history. Tenant mapping to the ~1,300-name universe must be built by hand and the 250-320 figure should be verified before relying on U=4. ATS API terms (Greenhouse Job Board API, Lever Postings API) should be read and filed before scaling daily polling.

quant-pm: No backtest is possible for at least three quarters of archiving, and the pull-versus-fill sign rule cannot be calibrated until a median time-to-fill per board exists, so the first several quarters produce an unsigned count. The vendors already hold multi-year history for the same companies, so by the time this version is testable the mid-cap residual may be gone. The margin/opex channel is the right target but the 20-25% coverage claim should be enumerated before Phase 3.

skeptic: No Phase 1 backtest is possible; go/no-go only after ~3 quarters of archived snapshots, and for the first several quarters the pull-vs-fill classification cannot be computed. Job-postings data is among the most widely sold alt-data categories, so the residual for mid-caps may be below round-trip costs. The Workday POST endpoint should not be counted toward coverage until per-tenant terms are read.

rows.name: Supplier-first disclosures flagging customer cuts

justifications.text: A: EDGAR daily index, XBRL frames and Notes datasets are DATA and structured, but the event itself is 8-K Item 2.02 exhibit text that must be parsed and classified from HTML, efts full-text search is intermittent (403 in Phase 0, 200 in Phase 1), and API Ninjas transcripts are premium-only per the facts sheet (free key cannot reach them); L: supplier reports 3-25 days before the customer, typical ~10 per record; S: mechanical when a >=10% named customer is cited, but share-loss, pricing and inventory-correction confounders and text ambiguity (record 3); C: FactSet Supply Chain and Bloomberg SPLC sell relationship maps, sell-side does this for mega-cap chains, event classification for thin-coverage mid-caps is not sold (record 3); U: ~120-150 names (~10%) after the <=10-analyst filter; H: 8-K daily index from 2004, XBRL ConcentrationRiskPercentage1 frames from ~2009, filing timestamps exact so point-in-time is clean; G: SEC data is clearly public, but transcript legs (API Ninjas redistribution unclear, Fool ToS) and the Nasdaq calendar robots flag are mild flags; use EDGAR-derived dates per the facts sheet.
justifications.lead: Event is final the day the supplier files its 8-K Item 2.02. Supplier-to-customer release gap 3-25 calendar days per the hypothesis window; typical ~10 days -> band 7-13 -> L=3. Note the supplier filing is public on day 0, so part of the lead may be consumed by same-day repricing of the customer.

justifications.text: A: EDGAR daily index, XBRL frames and Notes datasets are free and structured (DATA) but the event is 8-K Item 2.02 press-release text requiring HTML/text classification, EFTS is intermittent (403 in Phase 0, 200 once), and the facts sheet says the API Ninjas free key cannot reach transcripts, so the transcript leg is unavailable (4); L: the reading is final on the supplier's report date, 3-25 calendar days before the customer's release (median ~10-12, nominally band 3), discounted one notch because the reading is itself a public filing and the record's own press cases (Lumentum/Apple) show same-day repricing in the customer, with the earnings-window residual reasoned not shown; S: Phase 1 held signal_noise at 3 because when the event fires (customer named at >=10% of supplier revenue with explicit attribution) the mechanism is near-mechanical, but share-loss confounding, text ambiguity and small n (10-30 events per quarter) remain; C: FactSet Supply Chain and Bloomberg SPLC sell the map, sell-side does this for mega-cap chains, Cohen-Frazzini is published with arXiv 2301.11394 showing post-2004 decay, but the dated event classification for thinly covered mid-cap customers is not sold (3); U: record's ~10% (120-150 names) after the >=10% named-customer and <=10-analyst filters (5-19% band); H: 8-K index from 2004 and XBRL concentration data from 2009 give 5+ years point-in-time by filing date, minor caveat that the 'consensus moved <1%' filter needs daily consensus vintages that are not free historically; G: SEC data are public domain, but the record keeps a Nasdaq calendar leg with a robots flag and a transcript leg with unclear redistribution terms (mild flags, 4).
justifications.lead: Supplier files 8-K Item 2.02 on its own report day (day 0); the in-universe customer reports 3-25 calendar days later (record: typically 5-25; hypothesis window 3-25). The reading is final on day 0, so the nominal lead is 3-25 days, median ~10-12. Because the reading is a public filing that can be priced in the customer the same day, scored 2 rather than 3.

justifications.text: A: EDGAR daily index, XBRL frames and DERA notes datasets are DATA but the event text is 8-K HTML needing parsing, EDGAR full-text search is intermittent (403 in Phase 0, 200 once), API Ninjas transcripts are premium-only per the facts sheet (free key cannot reach them) so the transcript leg is absent, and the Nasdaq calendar is robots-flagged (treated absent, EDGAR dates instead), so 4; L: the event is final on the supplier's release day and the hypothesis admits gaps of 3-25 days before the customer's release, median ~10, so 3; S: 8-K press-release text rarely attributes a cut to a named customer (naming happens on calls, now unavailable), share-loss vs end-demand ambiguity remains, the record's own cases (Lumentum/Apple) repriced the customer the same day, and arXiv 2301.11394 finds customer momentum insignificant post-2004, so 2; C: FactSet Supply Chain and Bloomberg SPLC maps are widely used, sell-side does this for mega-caps, the supplier-customer link literature is heavily published (Cohen-Frazzini and successors), the mid-cap residual is REASONED, so 2; U: 120-150 thinly covered customers is REASONED and ConcentrationRisk members often lack the customer name, so 3 at the low end of its band; H: 8-K text 2004+ and XBRL 2009+ are point-in-time by filing date, but the 'consensus moved <1%' filter needs daily consensus history that is not free historically and transcripts are unavailable, so 4; G: SEC data is public, mild flags are the Nasdaq robots disallow and transcript redistribution ambiguity, so 4.
justifications.lead: Reading is final the day the supplier files its 8-K Item 2.02. The hypothesis keeps only events 3-25 calendar days before the customer's release; the record's typical gap is 5-25 days, median about 10. Lead = 3 to 25 days, central ~10, so 3.

concerns: data-engineer: The arXiv 2301.11394 result that customer momentum is insignificant post-2004 and the Lumentum/Apple same-day case cap the residual. efts.sec.gov intermittency means the keyword screen needs the Notes-dataset fallback built from day one. ConcentrationRisk members often lack the customer name, so the supplier-customer map still needs 10-K text parsing. Transcripts: the API Ninjas free tier does not serve them, so flagged calls must be read manually.

quant-pm: The 'already diffused' filter (customer consensus moved <1% since the supplier filing) cannot be backtested without historical daily consensus vintages, so the historical test would run unfiltered and the live version filtered, which is a design inconsistency. Transcripts are unavailable on the free API Ninjas tier per the facts sheet, so the record's 'read the handful of flagged calls' step is manual only. Use EDGAR-derived dates rather than the Nasdaq calendar per the facts sheet.

skeptic: The transcript leg the vet relied on (API Ninjas free tier) is not available per the facts sheet, so classifiable events per quarter will be fewer than the 10-30 claimed and the clean-attribution filter is harder to apply from press releases alone. The customer often reprices on the supplier's release day, leaving an earnings-window residual that is reasoned, not shown.

rows.name: AIS vessel calls at single-company bulk, LNG and fertilizer terminals

justifications.text: A: aisstream.io websocket subscription confirmed in the facts sheet (free key via GitHub), NOAA MarineCadastre daily zips are DATA, Census trade API key verified; live stream must be self-archived; L: live count final the day after quarter end, CNR/MOS/NFE/CMP report 30-45 days after quarter end, record cut lead to 15 for draft-inference cleaning; S: a loaded departure from a verifiably exclusive berth is a shipment count, a direct physical measure of tons (major driver) one step from revenue, with draft-based partial-load noise and price as the separable confounder; C: Kpler, Vortexa, Spire, AXSMarine and MarineTraffic sell cargo and vessel tracking and count these cargoes (record 2); U: 8-12 names with verifiable exclusive berths (12 or fewer -> under 1%); H: NOAA archive 2010 through 2024 (15 years) free and immutable, but 2025 folder is 404 (TESTED HERE in record) so live history starts from zero; G: aisstream has no terms page (facts sheet: none exists), commercial status unknown, so terms are ambiguous; NOAA and Census are public.
justifications.lead: Live feed: quarter count final at quarter end + 1 day. Releases: CNR ~30-35 days, MOS ~35-40, NFE ~40-45 after quarter end. Minus ~5-10 days of draft/load cleaning -> 15-30 day lead; record 15 -> band 14-27 -> L=4. Backtest-only NOAA archive lags ~11+ months and gives no live lead.

justifications.text: A: aisstream.io websocket subscription confirmed with a verified key in the facts sheet (structured JSON, free) and NOAA MarineCadastre daily zips are DATA, so both live and backtest feeds are reachable by code; L: the live call count is final ~day +1 and draft-based load cleaning by ~day +5, with CNR/MOS/NFE/EE reporting ~day +30-38 and CMP ~day +40, so the arithmetic gives 25-35 days, but the record's own hypothesis haircuts to 15 days for cleaning and the Census month-3 anchor lands after most prints, so scored on the record's 15 (band 4); S: at a verified exclusive berth a loaded departure is a shipment, a direct measure of tons (a major driver) one step from revenue, but price dominates coal/LNG revenue, FSRU throughput is largely contracted, Mosaic publishes monthly sales volumes, and draft inference is noisy for partial loads (record signal_noise 3); C: Kpler, Vortexa, Spire, AXSMarine and MarineTraffic sell cargo and vessel tracking to most energy desks (several vendors, 2); U: five named tickers after the exclusivity pruning (CNR, MOS, NFE, EE, CMP), facts-sheet single-site family, under 12 names (1); H: NOAA archive 2010-2024 gives 5+ years free point-in-time, minor caveat that the 2025 folder is 404 (TESTED HERE in record) so live history starts from zero and the backtest and live sources differ; G: facts sheet confirms no aisstream terms page exists, so commercial status is unknown (terms unread/ambiguous, 3); NOAA leg is clean.
justifications.lead: Quarter ends day 0; the live AIS call count is final day +1 and draft-weighted load inference cleaned by ~day +5. CNR, MOS, NFE and EE report ~day +30-38 (early November for a September quarter) and CMP (September FY) ~day +40. Lead = 30-40 minus 5 = 25-35 days. The record states 15 days (its own cleaning haircut), and the Census port-level export release for month 3 lands ~day +35-42, i.e. after most releases, so the vessel count is the only pre-print read of month 3.

justifications.text: A: NOAA MarineCadastre daily zips are DATA for 2010-2024 and the aisstream.io websocket key is verified in the facts sheet, but the free archive stops at 2024 (2025 folder 404, TESTED in record), the live feed is websocket-only with no catch-up so it must run continuously from day one, and terrestrial coverage at the specific berths is unverified, so 4; L: call count final at Q+1 day, record cuts to T-15 for draft-based cleaning, named names report Q+25 (CNR) to Q+50 (NFE), so 4; S: a loaded departure from an exclusive-use berth is a clean shipment count one step from revenue, but tons times price with price dominating, partial-load draft inference and unverified berth exclusivity are moderate confounders, so 3; C: Kpler, Vortexa, AXSMarine, Spire, MarineTraffic and VesselFinder sell cargo and vessel tracking and the record concedes LNG and crude flows are crowdedness 1-2, so 2; U: five named names (CNR, MOS, NFE, EE, CMP) with HCC/AMR conditional, inside the facts-sheet single-site family cap of eight, so 1; H: 15 years of free NOAA history for backtests but it ends in 2024 with no free 2025-26 data, so the live series cannot be stitched to the archive without a gap, 4; G: aisstream terms page absent (facts sheet legal amber for S04), NOAA and Census public, so 3.
justifications.lead: Quarter's loaded-departure count final at Q+1 day with a live feed; record measures at T-15 after draft cleaning. Releases: CNR ~Q+25-30, MOS ~Q+35-40, EE ~Q+35-40, CMP (Sep FY) ~Q+40, NFE ~Q+40-50. Raw lead 24-49 days, usable lead 15 days by the record's own design, so 4. MOS publishes monthly sales volumes and Census port exports land ~5-6 weeks after month end, so the lead over public disclosure of months 1-2 is near zero for that leg.

concerns: data-engineer: Backtest (NOAA/USCG NAIS 2010-2024) and live (aisstream terrestrial) are different sources with a ~2-year hole between them, so thresholds calibrated on the archive cannot be validated against the live feed before trading. Daily NOAA zips are large; filter to berth polygons on ingest. aisstream terms do not exist, which is a legal ambiguity, not a clearance. Census port-level exports anchor two of three months, leaving one month of residual.

quant-pm: The legal status of the live feed is unverified and no terms page exists; a backtest on the NOAA archive would validate a signal that cannot be traded until aisstream's commercial use is confirmed or a paid feed is bought. Revenue is tons times price and price is not observed here. Mosaic's monthly volume releases make MOS redundant, leaving four names. The berth-exclusivity verification from 10-K/permit text is unstarted.

skeptic: Live history starts from zero today and the archive-to-live gap (2025 to present) has no free source. The commercial terms of aisstream are unread. For LNG (NFE, EE) and coal (CNR) the cargo counts are already sold to energy desks by Kpler and peers; the genuinely under-covered legs are salt and phosphate at two names. Price, not volume, drives the revenue surprise for most of these.

rows.name: Federal docket feeds: supplier suits, liens, product liability

justifications.text: A: PACER CM/ECF RSS feeds are DATA (XML, no account, 7 courts tested 200 in record) but carry only caption and entry type; nature-of-suit codes require PACER Case Locator (account not created, $0.10/page) or CourtListener. TESTED HERE: CourtListener v4 search without a token returns HTTP 401 'Authentication credentials were not provided', so the free account the facts sheet lists as not created is required -> free key not yet obtained; L: quarter filing count is final at T-1 (lead_time_days 1); S: suit clusters are a lagging distress proxy already in short interest and spreads, RSS has no nature-of-suit field (record 2); C: UniCourt, Thomson Reuters Court Wire (Eikon), Docket Alarm and Lex Machina sell litigation alerts including 'portfolio company sued' to investors (record 2); U: ~60 actionable sub-$3B names (13-60 band) though searchable universe-wide; H: RSS is rolling recent entries with no archive, backfill only through PCL (account plus fee-metered, waived under $30/quarter) or partial RECAP via CourtListener (token required, TESTED HERE 401) -> forward collection with a partial, not-yet-obtained backfill; G: official uscourts.gov RSS and public court records, no scraping conflict.
justifications.lead: Filing count measured at T-1 -> 1 day -> L=1. Individual suits precede the release by 0-90 days but the hypothesis aggregates the trailing 90 days at T-1.

justifications.text: A: seven PACER CM/ECF RSS feeds return XML keylessly (TESTED HERE in record), but the feeds carry no nature-of-suit field, so classification needs CourtListener or PACER Case Locator accounts, which the facts sheet lists as not created (free key not yet obtained, 4), and cand failed; L: the record freezes the 90-day suit count at T-1, so the full reading is final one day before the release (anchor 1); S: Phase 1 lowered signal_noise to 2 because a suit cluster is a lagging distress proxy already carried by short interest and spreads, most collection suits sit in state courts outside the free feeds, and the bulk of federal docket activity is employment/securities/patent noise; C: UniCourt, Trellis, Docket Alarm, Lex Machina and Thomson Reuters Court Wire (portfolio-company-sued alerts in Eikon) sell docket analytics to investors (several vendors, 2); U: the record's own 'actionable in ~5% (about 60 sub-$3B names)' is below the 65-name floor of the 5-19% band (2); H: RSS is rolling-only with no archive, and the backtest must be reconstructed name by name through PACER Case Locator party searches (account not created, $0.10/page with an unverified sub-$30/quarter waiver) or partial RECAP, i.e. reconstruction (3); G: official judiciary RSS feeds (uscourts.gov 'Feed the Need'), CourtListener free, PACER terms clean (5).
justifications.lead: Event stream: a complaint appears in the court's RSS within minutes of docketing. The record's hypothesis counts suits in the 90 days before the release versus the prior 90 days and measures at T-1, so release day minus T-1 = 1 day. Freezing the window at T-5 would change little but is not what the record specifies.

justifications.text: A: seven district RSS feeds are DATA and keyless but carry only caption and entry type with no nature-of-suit field and are rolling-only, cand failed to connect and ~25% of districts have no feed, while the classification and history legs need a PACER account (not created per facts sheet, $0.10/page with a conditional waiver) or a CourtListener token (not created), and state courts where most collection suits sit are absent, so 3; L: filing count final at T-1 per the record, so 1; S: vet lowered to 2: a suit cluster lags and proxies the distress factor already in short interest and spreads, and the free RSS cannot filter by NOS; C: UniCourt, Trellis, Docket Alarm, Lex Machina and Thomson Reuters Court Wire in Eikon sell 'portfolio company sued' alerts to investors, so 2; U: about 60 actionable sub-$3B names claimed, the top of the 13-60 band, federal-only, so 2; H: RSS has no archive, history must be reconstructed through PCL party-name searches (account not created, waiver conditional) or the partial RECAP archive, so 3; G: official PACER RSS (uscourts.gov 'Feed the Need') and CourtListener are public with no scraping conflict, 5.
justifications.lead: Suits arrive continuously; the 90-day count is final at T-1 (record). Lead over the release = 1 day.

concerns: data-engineer: Start the RSS archive now or lose the data; cand feed unreachable (000) and only ~50% of district courts publish full feeds. Most collection suits sit in state courts outside every free feed. PACER fees are waived under $30/quarter but the PCL party-name backfill for ~60 names and Exhibit 21 subsidiaries must be budgeted in pages. Any backtest will be driven by a handful of distress episodes.

quant-pm: By the time suppliers sue in federal court the distress is usually priced; the hypothesis controls for short interest but the residual is likely a handful of Hertz/JetBlue-type episodes. State courts, where most collection suits sit, are outside the free feeds. Both accounts needed for classification and backtest (PACER, CourtListener) are not yet created; the per-page PCL cost arithmetic (~300 pages per quarter for ~60 names) is reasoned, not tested.

skeptic: The free feeds cannot produce the signal's own filter (NOS 190/195/365/367) without an unobtained PACER or CourtListener account, and the RSS archive starts today. Most collection suits are in state courts outside every free source. The actionable sample is a few dozen names, so any backtest is driven by a handful of distress episodes.

rows.name: HS-code import nowcast (Census) for import-dependent hardgoods

justifications.text: A: Census international trade API key verified in the facts sheet, JSON, monthly HS-10 by origin country with value and quantity; ImportYeti 403 (blocked) and Panjiva paid are both excluded; L: month-2 FT-900 lands ~5 weeks after month end, i.e. ~5-8 days after quarter end, and releases follow 25-45 days after quarter end, record 14; S: HS lines pool many importers, only 2 of 3 months, sign ambiguity between import build as overhang versus demand (record 2); C: Panjiva, ImportGenius and Datamyne sell bills of lading and sell-side consumer analysts watch the same Census tables, HS-10 ticker mapping is the only edge (record 2); U: 15-25 names with verified HTS-10 dominance; H: monthly series back to 2013 via the API (per probe) gives 12+ years, but the API serves the current revised vintage (monthly and annual revisions) rather than originally published values, a minor look-ahead caveat; G: official Census API, clearly public.
justifications.lead: Months 1-2 reading final when the month-2 FT-900 posts: ~35-40 days after month 2 end = ~5-8 days after quarter end. Typical release 25-45 days after quarter end -> 17-40 day lead for the two-month reading; month 3 arrives after the release. Record 14 -> band 14-27 -> L=4 (discounted for the missing month and shutdown delays).

justifications.text: A: Census international trade API key verified in the facts sheet, structured JSON, monthly HS-10 by origin with value and quantity (5); L: only months 1-2 of the quarter are available pre-print (month 2 lands ~day +4 to +11 after quarter end against releases at day +25 to +45, a 14-41 day lead that would be band 4), but the full-quarter reading never exists before the print because month 3 lands after the announcement, so one notch off (3); S: Phase 1 signal_noise 2 because HS lines pool many importers, tariff pull-forwards broke the import-to-sales link in 2025, port congestion and FOB timing shift months, and the vet reframed it as an inventory/gross-margin proxy rather than a revenue nowcast (indirect, heavy confounders); C: Panjiva, ImportGenius and Datamyne sell bill-of-lading data that appears in sell-side previews for large importers, Panjiva publishes HS 9503 toy research, and consumer analysts watch the same Census tables (commonly used, 2); U: 15-25 names after restricting to verified HTS-10 dominance (1-4% band, 2); H: monthly API series from 2013 (per probe) gives 5+ years, minor look-ahead caveat from Census annual revisions of preliminary trade data (4); G: official government API with a free key, ImportYeti (403) dropped, Datamyne pages used only for manual dominance checks (5).
justifications.lead: Calendar quarter Jan-Mar: the February FT-900 detail lands ~5-6 weeks after Feb 28, i.e. ~Apr 4-11 (day +4 to +11 after quarter end). Covered importers report ~day +25 to +45 (late April to mid May). Months-1-2 lead = 25-45 minus 4-11 = 14 to 41 days (record states 14). The March release lands ~May 5-12, after most prints, so the full-quarter reading is never available pre-print; scored 3 for the missing third month.

justifications.text: A: Census international trade API key verified in the facts sheet, JSON, monthly HS-10 by origin country back to 2013 per the Phase 0 probe, 5; L: TESTED HERE the FT-900 index lists September 2026 as the latest release on 2026-11-11 (October not yet out), confirming the ~5-week lag, so month-2 data lands ~Q+5 days (17-33 days before releases) but month 3 lands ~Q+35-38, after most releases: strict full-quarter wording gives 1, the signal as defined gives 4, scored 3 for a two-thirds reading plus shutdown-delay risk; S: vet lowered to 2: HS lines pool many importers, the series lags retailer commentary and port volumes, and tariff pull-forwards broke the import-to-sales link in 2025; C: Panjiva, ImportGenius and Descartes Datamyne sell bill-of-lading data at scale and sell-side consumer analysts use the same Census tables, the HS-10 mid-cap mapping edge is REASONED, so 2; U: 15-25 names after restricting to verifiable HTS-10 dominance, so 2; H: 2013+ via the API but the API serves annually revised vintages rather than first prints, a minor look-ahead caveat, so 4; G: official Census API, Panjiva/Datamyne pages used only to verify dominance, ImportYeti blocked and dropped, 5.
justifications.lead: FT-900 for month M lands ~35-38 days after month end (TESTED HERE: September 2026 is the latest release available on November 11). Calendar Q1: February data ~April 3-7, March data ~May 5-8. Releases for the named categories: toys Q+22-35, powersports Q+22, footwear Q+30-38, coolers/grills/small appliances Q+37-40. Months-1-2 reading: 17-33 days of lead; full-quarter reading: -15 to +3 days, i.e. after most releases.

concerns: data-engineer: Only two of three months are ever available before the release, so the 'full-quarter reading' never exists pre-print. Revisions: store each monthly API pull as its own vintage from now so the live series is point-in-time even if the backtest is not. Federal shutdowns delayed 2025 releases. HTS-10 dominance verification relies on Datamyne/Panjiva public pages (UNPROBED) and 10-K sourcing text.

quant-pm: The series is a category aggregate; for the 15-25 names that dominate a line the same table is on sell-side consumer analysts' screens and Panjiva publishes the mapping, so the residual that survives to the earnings window arrives after retailer commentary and port volumes. Federal shutdowns delay FT-900 releases and can erase the lead. The dominance verification per HTS-10 line relies on vendor marketing pages, not a data feed.

skeptic: The full quarter is never observable before most releases; the record's lead of 14 applies to a two-month reading only. Federal shutdowns delay FT-900 releases (the record notes this). Coverage of 15-25 names rests on a dominance check against vendor marketing pages rather than data.

rows.name: Index rebalance and forced-flow overlay around earnings dates

justifications.text: A: press.spglobal.com index-change releases are 200 (HTML tables to parse), FTSE Russell add/delete lists are PDFs, Wikipedia change table is HTML, SSGA MDY holdings xlsx is DATA with a redistribution clause, Yahoo chart API is undocumented; spglobal.com/spdji is 403 from the container; L: ad-hoc S&P changes announced ~5 business days before effective date, quarterly rebalances ~17 days (Jun 5 -> Jun 22, 2026), Russell preliminary lists ~28 days before (Nov 13 -> Dec 11, 2026), record lead_time_days 5; S: Greenwood-Sammon and Chang-Hong-Liskovich show the effect sits at announcement and is shrinking, and the target is exit slippage/realized variance, not return (record 2); C: every index-arb desk and systematic fund models these flows and sell-side publishes predicted lists (record 1); U: 5-10% of names (65-130) carry an index event inside T-5..T+5 in a given quarter; the filter applies to all names but is informative only for that slice; H: S&P press releases with announcement dates seen back to at least 2020, Russell PDFs by year, Wikipedia table has effective dates only and is editable (not point-in-time), SSGA holdings current day only -> five-plus years with reconstruction caveats; G: public press releases and PDFs, SSGA internal-use clause, Yahoo undocumented endpoint, Wikipedia CC BY-SA attribution (mild flags).
justifications.lead: Flag is final at the index announcement. S&P ad-hoc: ~5 business days before effective; S&P quarterly: ~17 calendar days; Russell: ~28 days. The reading is a calendar flag, not a quarter total; record 5 days -> band 2-6 -> L=2.

justifications.text: A: press.spglobal.com releases (200, TESTED HERE in record) and FTSE Russell PDFs are free but need HTML/PDF parsing, the SSGA xlsx is structured but current-day only, the spglobal.com/spdji page is 403 (4); L: ad-hoc S&P replacements are announced 2-5 business days before the effective date and the record's stated lead is 5 days (band 2), although scheduled rebalances (~17 days' notice) and Russell preliminary lists (~4 weeks) give more; S: the record itself reclassifies this from signal to exit/sizing rule with 'no predictable sign of the abnormal return', and Greenwood-Sammon and Chang-Hong-Liskovich show the effective-date effect has disappeared, so as a predictor of the earnings move it is weak (1); C: the record states crowdedness 1, index-arb desks and every systematic fund model these flows and sell-side strategists publish predicted add/delete lists (1); U: a calendar check applied to every in-universe earnings event (~100% per the record), with a 5-10% fire rate (5); H: Wikipedia S&P 400 change table is multi-year and S&P press releases with announcement dates go back to at least 2020, giving 5+ years with a minor caveat that realized passive-weight changes (SSGA holdings) are current-day only (4); G: SSGA xlsx carries an internal-use redistribution clause, Yahoo chart API is an undocumented endpoint, Wikipedia needs attribution (mild flags, 4).
justifications.lead: The flag concerns an earnings date within T-5..T+5 of an index effective date. Scheduled S&P rebalance changes are announced ~17 days before the effective date (record: Jun 5 to Jun 22, 2026; Mar 6 to Mar 23, 2026), so the flag is final 12-22 days before an earnings date inside the window; ad-hoc replacements give 2-5 business days; Russell preliminary lists ~4 weeks (Nov 13 for the Dec 11, 2026 reconstitution). The record states 5 days, the ad-hoc case, which is the one that matters most.

justifications.text: A: press.spglobal.com releases (200), LSEG PDFs, Wikipedia change tables and the SSGA xlsx are all free but need HTML/PDF parsing, the spglobal.com/spdji page is bot-blocked, so 4; L: the record's own lead is 5 days, the vet's dated examples show quarterly rebalance changes announced ~17 days before effective dates and Russell preliminary lists ~4 weeks out, but quarterly rebalances fall on third Fridays of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec when calendar-quarter reporters rarely have earnings, so the overlaps that actually occur come mostly from ad-hoc S&P replacements announced 3-5 business days ahead, 2; S: the record disavows alpha ('no claim of differentiation', 'adds no alpha'), Greenwood-Sammon and Chang-Hong-Liskovich show the index effect has disappeared or occurs at announcement, so as a predictor of the target it is 1; C: record's own crowdedness 1, modelled by every index-arb desk and systematic fund; U: ~100% as a calendar but only 5-10% of events have an index event inside T-5..T+5, so 3; H: history must be reconstructed from Wikipedia change tables and year-by-year LSEG PDFs with SSGA holdings current-day only, so 3; G: SSGA xlsx internal-use clause, Yahoo chart API undocumented, Wikipedia attribution, so 4.
justifications.lead: Ad-hoc S&P additions/deletions: announced ~3-5 business days before the effective date (record). Quarterly rebalance: announced ~17 days before (vet: June 5 for June 22, March 6 for March 23). Russell: preliminary lists ~28 days before (Nov 13 for Dec 11). Earnings dates rarely sit within T-5..T+5 of a third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, so the binding case is ad-hoc with 3-5 days; record's own figure is 5.

concerns: data-engineer: This is an exit/sizing rule, not a signal; its value is measured in slippage, which the record says itself. SSGA daily holdings must be archived from now (current day only) if realized weight changes are wanted. Announcement timestamps must be reconstructed from press releases, not from Wikipedia, for any point-in-time test. Yahoo chart endpoint is undocumented and can change without notice.

quant-pm: Not a signal: no alpha claimed, no directional content, and the record's own literature says the effect now occurs at announcement, not at the effective date. Its only value is as a sizing/exit rule measured by slippage and realized variance, which the ranking should treat separately from the fundamental signals; the high U and H scores should not pull it up the list. The SSGA redistribution clause is acceptable for internal use only.

skeptic: This is an exit-slippage and sizing filter, not a signal; it does not predict the surprise or the abnormal return and the record says so. Scoring it on the seven criteria flatters it on U and A. Its value, if any, is measured in realized variance and fills, and the red team notes extra rebalance volume may improve fills rather than hurt them.

rows.name: Weekly rail carloads by commodity (intermodal and coal near-identities)

justifications.text: A: AAR weekly releases are DATA but HTML with a curl UA requirement, BNSF weekly reports are PDFs, Norfolk Southern weekly reports are 200 (xlsx and PDFs), STB EP724 is weekly xlsx, UP and CSX are 403 from the container. TESTED HERE: eia.gov/coal/production/weekly/ is 200 and links xls/weekly_production.xlsx -> all legs need HTML/PDF/xlsx parsing; L: the quarter's last AAR week posts the Wednesday after week end (<=7-10 days after quarter end), carrier reports a few days later; JBHT reports ~day 15, HUBG ~day 25, BTU/CNR/AMR/HCC days 25-40, record 15; S: for the retained names the public weekly series is close to reported volume (BNSF and NS intermodal units for JBHT/HUBG, AAR coal carloads for the coal names) but it is a system total with share drift and price dominating revenue, so a proxy with a clear mechanism; C: AAR weekly carloads are quoted by every transport and coal analyst (record 1); U: ~35 names (~2.7%); H: AAR archive is '~52 pages of releases' (depth not quantified), BNSF from Feb 2025 (<1 yr), NS PDFs 2023-2026 (~3 yrs), STB 2014+ REASONED. TESTED HERE: the EIA weekly_production.xlsx is a single-week snapshot (49 rows, week ended 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-31), not the multi-year file the record REASONED, so history must be reconstructed from archived releases -> 3; G: AAR is a trade association (press totals free, detailed tables paid, UA requirement), carrier IR pages and STB/EIA are public (mild flag).
justifications.lead: Last week of the quarter available ~5-10 days after quarter end (AAR Wednesday release; BNSF/NS a few days after week end). Releases: JBHT ~15 days after quarter end (lead ~5-8), HUBG ~25 (lead ~17), BTU/CNR ~30 (lead ~22), AMR/HCC ~35-40 (lead ~28). Median ~20 days; record 15 -> band 14-27 -> L=4, with JBHT alone at L=2-3.

justifications.text: A: AAR weekly releases (HTML, curl UA required), BNSF PDFs, Norfolk Southern xlsx/PDFs (200, TESTED HERE in record) and STB EP724 are free but need PDF/HTML parsing, UP and CSX return 403 from the container, and the EIA weekly coal page returns 200 (TESTED HERE) (4); L: the quarter's last AAR week posts ~day +5 and carrier reports ~day +7, against JBHT ~day +15 (lead ~8-10), HUBG ~day +28 (~21) and BTU/CNR/AMR/HCC ~day +30-40 (23-35), record states 15 (band 4); S: Phase 1 signal_noise 2 because the series are carrier or national totals rather than the shipper's own loads, share drifts, price dominates revenue, and the record itself expects a small coefficient and reclassifies the output as a consensus anchor; C: record crowdedness 1, AAR weekly carloads are the most-watched freight series and are quoted by every sell-side transport and coal analyst (1); U: the vet kept only six named tickers with a near-identity series (JBHT, HUBG, BTU, CNR, AMR, HCC), under 12 names (1); H: AAR weekly releases including intermodal run multiple years (Phase 0 saw ~52 pages) and EIA/STB are multi-year, giving 5+ years for the coal leg, with the caveat that carrier-specific intermodal reports start only 2023 (NS) and Feb 2025 (BNSF) (4); G: trade-association press releases and carrier IR pages are public, STB/EIA are government, record legal_risk 1 (5).
justifications.lead: Calendar quarter ends day 0 for all six names. AAR posts the final week on the first Wednesday after it (~day +5); BNSF and Norfolk Southern weekly reports follow (~day +7). JBHT reports ~day +15 (lead ~8-10 days), HUBG ~day +28 (lead ~21), BTU/CNR/AMR/HCC ~day +30-40 (lead 23-35). The record states 15 days and the hypothesis measures at 10 trading days before release.

justifications.text: A: AAR weekly releases are free HTML (TESTED HERE: the record's URL now 301s to /resource-finder/, releases live at /aar_news/weekly-rail-traffic-data/), BNSF weekly reports are PDFs, NS xlsx/PDFs 200, but UP and CSX return 403 from the container (HUBG's UP leg is blocked) and the EIA weekly coal API path is unprobed (page 200 TESTED HERE), so partly blocked plus PDF parsing, 3; L: TESTED HERE 'Week Ending November 7, 2026' was posted by Wednesday November 11, confirming the Wednesday-for-prior-week cadence, so the quarter's last week is available ~Q+4-5 days; JBHT reports ~Q+15 (lead ~10), HUBG ~Q+28-30, BTU/CNR ~Q+25-35, AMR/HCC ~Q+35-40, hypothesis measures at 10 trading days (~14 calendar) before release, majority band 4; S: vet 2: a national commodity total is an industry aggregate, company share drifts and price dominates revenue, record expects a small coefficient; C: record's own 1, AAR weekly data are in every transport and coal model; U: after the vet only six names (JBHT, HUBG, BTU, CNR, AMR, HCC) have a near-identity series, 12 or fewer, so 1 despite the row's ~35 claim; H: BNSF weekly PDFs only from February 2025 and NS 2023-2026, the identity series are the short ones, AAR and EIA deeper, so 3; G: AAR requires a browser UA, corporate IR page terms unread, STB and EIA public, so 4.
justifications.lead: AAR releases the week ending Saturday on the following Wednesday (TESTED HERE: week ending Nov 7 posted by Nov 11). Quarter's final week available ~Q+4-5 days. JBHT ~Q+15 gives ~10 days (3); HUBG ~Q+28-30, BTU ~Q+30-35, CNR ~Q+25-35, AMR/HCC ~Q+35-40 give 20-36 days (4-5). Record's 15 and the T-10-trading-day measurement sit in band 4.

concerns: data-engineer: The coal leg's multi-year history is not in the EIA weekly xlsx (current week only); it must be rebuilt from archived EIA weekly pages or AAR releases, and the AAR archive depth should be counted before claiming more than 1-3 years. UP and CSX weekly reports are blocked from the container, so HUBG's UP-side intermodal is missing. PDF parsing of BNSF reports is brittle. The record itself expects a near-zero coefficient; treat as a consensus anchor feature.

quant-pm: The record concedes the coefficient should be small because the same weekly numbers are in every transport and coal model; this row's value is as a consensus anchor for S07/S04-type physical signals, not a trade. JBHT, the largest name, reports so early that the lead is a week. The 'near-identity' between carrier intermodal loads and JBHT/HUBG volumes is REASONED, not shown.

skeptic: The record itself reclassifies this as a consensus anchor for other signals rather than a trade; the residual after consensus revisions is expected near zero. Two of the four Class I carrier pages are blocked from the container, and the carrier-level identity series (BNSF, NS) have under two years of history. The row's coverage field (~35 names) is stale relative to its own vet.

rows.name: Summed federal contract obligations (FPDS/USAspending)

justifications.text: A: USAspending spending_by_transaction and spending_by_award are keyless JSON (TESTED HERE 200 in record, CACI civilian actions visible 6 days after signing), FPDS ATOM 200, LDA.gov API 200; SAM.gov 404 with DEMO_KEY is a patch for the DoD gap only; L: civilian obligations near-final 7-10 days after quarter end, CACI/BAH report ~22-30 days after, ICF/PSN/MMS/TTEK/SAIC ~30-40 days, record 15, DoD leg withheld 90 days (TESTED HERE in record: Kratos and KBR DoD actions 97-111 days old); S: obligations mostly fund existing IDIQ task orders and lag recognition, lumpy, Sep-30 surge dominates variance (record 3); C: Quiver Quantitative ($30/mo), GovWin IQ, Bloomberg Government and Apify actors map the same feed to tickers (record 2); U: ~50 names with >30% federal revenue (~3.8%); H: FY2008+ via API (REASONED), FPDS FY2004+, but a naive historical pull includes DoD actions that were invisible for 90 days and backdated modifications/deobligations, and last-modified filtering is REASONED not verified -> five-plus years with a look-ahead caveat; G: official government APIs, keyless, clearly public.
justifications.lead: Civilian obligations near-final at quarter end + 7-10 days (6-day visibility lag tested). Releases: CACI ~22-25 days after quarter end (lead ~12-15), BAH ~25-30 (lead ~17), ICF/PSN/MMS/TTEK ~30-40 (lead ~22-30). Record 15 -> band 14-27 -> L=4. DoD obligations for the quarter's last ~8 weeks are not visible at any release.

justifications.text: A: USAspending spending_by_transaction and spending_by_award are keyless JSON APIs returning 200 (TESTED HERE in record), FPDS ATOM works for simple queries, LDA.gov API 200 (5); L: civilian obligations are visible within ~6 days (CACI actions dated 2026-11-05 seen 2026-11-11 in record) so the civilian sum is near-final ~day +7-10, against CACI/BAH ~day +22-25 (lead 12-18), ICF/PSN ~day +30-38 (20-30) and MMS/TTEK ~day +40-50 (30-40), record states 15 (band 4); S: Phase 1 signal_noise 3, summed obligations are a direct read of bookings/book-to-bill which drive backlog guidance, but obligations mostly fund existing IDIQ task orders, are lumpy around the Sep-30 federal year-end, and DoD actions are withheld 90 days (clear mechanism, moderate confounders); C: Quiver Quantitative sells ticker-mapped USAspending data at $30/mo, GovWin IQ and Bloomberg Government sell contract intelligence, Apify actors replicate it, and CESifo/Bank of Lithuania papers cover award effects (several vendors, 2); U: ~50 names with >30% federal revenue, civilian-heavy first test 15-20 names (1-4% band, 2); H: FY2008+ via API gives 5+ years, minor look-ahead caveat that the historical database contains DoD actions that were invisible at the time and later record modifications, which the backtest must emulate from signed dates (4); G: official government API, keyless, public domain (5).
justifications.lead: Quarter ends day 0; civilian-agency actions reach USAspending within ~6 days (record TESTED HERE), so the civilian quarterly sum is near-final ~day +7-10. CACI (June FY) and BAH (March FY) report ~day +22-25 (lead 12-18 days); ICF and PSN ~day +30-38 (lead 20-30); MMS and TTEK (September FY) ~day +40-50 (lead 30-40). Record states 15 and the hypothesis measures 10 days before release. DoD obligations signed within 90 days of T-1 are never visible pre-print (DFARS PGI 204.6), so the defence portion of the quarter is structurally incomplete.

justifications.text: A: USAspending spending_by_transaction and spending_by_award are keyless JSON probed 200 in the record, FPDS ATOM and LDA.gov also 200, 5; L: a single CACI civilian transaction visible with a 6-day lag shows visibility not completeness, the record calls civilian totals 'near-final' at Q+7-10 (REASONED), DoD is blanked for 90 days, and the hypothesis itself measures at T-10, so 3 even though CACI/BAH (Q+22-25) and later reporters (Q+30-40) would allow 12-30 days; S: civilian obligations are one step from bookings and revenue with the Sep-30 surge and IDIQ funding of existing work as moderate confounders, the cited award event studies support a mechanism, so 3; C: Quiver Quant sells ticker-mapped contract data for $30/month, GovWin IQ, Bloomberg Government and Apify actors also sell it, defence analysts track awards, so 2; U: ~50 names with over 30% federal revenue, civilian-heavy first subset 15-20, so 2; H: FY2008+ via the API with point-in-time approximated from action and last-modified dates (REASONED), a minor look-ahead caveat, so 4; G: official government APIs, 5.
justifications.lead: Civilian actions post within ~3 business days to FPDS and load to USAspending daily (one observed 6-day lag); record treats the civilian quarter as near-final at Q+7-10. Releases: CACI ~Q+22-25, BAH ~Q+25, ICF ~Q+30-35, SAIC ~Q+35-40, MMS/TTEK/PSN ~Q+35-40. Potential lead 12-30 days, but the hypothesis measures at T-10 and DoD obligations are withheld 90 days, so scored 3.

concerns: data-engineer: Point-in-time reconstruction is the main engineering risk: verify that USAspending exposes a last-modified or load date per transaction, otherwise the backtest sees DoD actions and modifications the market could not. UEI hierarchy roll-up including subsidiaries must be built and versioned. SAM.gov award notices need a real api.data.gov/SAM key to test (DEMO_KEY 404). Quiver already sells the ticker-mapped series for $30/mo, so the edge is only in the fiscal-quarter alignment and lag model.

quant-pm: A $30/month retail vendor already maps the same feed to tickers, so the residual edge is only fiscal-quarter alignment, UEI roll-up and the lag model; the test should include Quiver-style raw sums as a control. The DoD 90-day withholding blanks most of the quarter for defence-heavy names, limiting the real test to ~15-20 civilian-heavy tickers. The SAM.gov award-notice patch is unverified (404 with DEMO_KEY).

skeptic: Completeness of civilian obligations at Q+7-10 is asserted from one transaction's lag, not from a reconciliation of totals across vintages; late FPDS reporting is common. For defence-heavy names most of the quarter is invisible at the release. A $30/month retail vendor already maps the same feed to tickers, so the edge is the fiscal-quarter alignment and UEI roll-up only.

verifier.changes: S lowered from 3 to 2 (TESTED HERE, 2026-11-11). I ran the signal as specified (civilian-agency obligations, Jul-Sep 2026 vs Jul-Sep 2025, USAspending spending_over_time with a 17-agency civilian filter, keyword recipient match) for the three names whose Q3-2026 prints are already out. Booz Allen: civilian obligations +8% YoY ($1,622M vs $1,498M) while BAH reported Civil+Commercial revenue -15% ($702M vs $827M) and total revenue -3.9% on Oct 23. ICF: civilian obligations -5% ($180M vs $190M) while ICF reported revenue +1.1% and awards +4.5% on Nov 5. CACI: civilian obligations +9% ($1,133M vs $1,037M) and revenue +8.2% on Oct 21, a match, but CACI is DoD-dominated so the civilian sum is not the driver. Two of three live sign checks disagree with the print. Mechanism confounders are also heavier than 'moderate': September alone is 61% (CACI), 61% (BAH) and 75% (ICF) of the quarter's civilian obligations, i.e. year-end funding of next-year work, not the quarter's revenue; and October 2025 (shutdown) civilian obligations are negative for CACI (-$2.8M) and ICF (-$0.2M), so the YoY base for the Dec-2026 quarter is distorted. Caveat: n=3 with name matching rather than the UEI roll-up the record proposes, so this is evidence of sign ambiguity, not a backtest. A kept at 5 (all keyless endpoints 200 TESTED HERE). L kept at 4: official schedule puts civilian data on USAspending within 5 days, so the Sep-30 quarter is near-final ~Oct 7; verified release dates give leads of 14 (CACI Oct 21), 16 (BAH Oct 23), 22 (PSN Oct 29), 29 (ICF Nov 5) days; DoD leg is never final (CACI DoD latest visible action 2026-08-03 on 2026-11-11, 100 days), which I treat under S rather than double-count in L. C kept at 2: additional vendors found (GovChime, Bureauify, Sweetspot) and Quiver's USAspending-sourced company tracker confirmed, but still no vendor sells the fiscal-quarter-aligned UEI sum. H kept at 4: API search floor is 2007-10-01 (TESTED HERE 422 for FY2002), Award Data Archive lists only the latest full and delta files dated 2026-11-06 (no vintages), so point-in-time must be emulated from action_date plus the deterministic 90-day DoD rule; still 5+ years with a caveat. U 2 and G 5 unchanged.
verifier.refutation: The panel scored the mechanism on reasoning; the first live out-of-sample check contradicts it. For the only quarter where both the data and the prints exist (Jul-Sep 2026), the signal as specified (civilian obligations, same quarter a year earlier) was wrong-signed for two of three names: Booz Allen's civilian obligations rose 8% while its Civil revenue fell 15% and total revenue fell 3.9%; ICF's civilian obligations fell 5% while revenue and awards rose. The one match (CACI, +9% vs +8.2%) is a name whose revenue is dominated by the DoD leg the signal cannot see. The structural reasons are visible in the same probes: 61-75% of a Sep quarter's civilian obligations land in September, the federal year-end sweep that funds next year's option periods, so the sum measures funding timing, not the quarter's work; obligations on cost-plus IDIQ task orders are incremental funding of work already in consensus; the 90-day DoD withholding blanks roughly 85% of the quarter for the defence-heavy half of the 50-name universe, so the 'full-quarter reading' never exists before the print for those names; the October 2025 shutdown makes the next YoY base negative; and recipient resolution by UEI hierarchy is still unbuilt. Meanwhile the raw feed is nightly, free and already ticker-mapped by a $30 retail vendor and tracked by GovCon sell-side, so whatever residual exists is likely absorbed by the company's own pre-announced awards and the analyst-revision factor. Add that the usable universe is ~15-20 civilian-heavy names (U=2) and that history must be emulated rather than observed (no USAspending vintages exist), and a signal with A=5 and G=5 but S=2 is an easy-to-collect proxy that has not yet shown it points the right way, which is a weaker claim than rank 5 of 59 implies.
verifier.release_schedule_check: Official lag: USAspending 'About the Data' (https://www.usaspending.gov/data/about-the-data-download.pdf, last updated Oct 6, 2026) states FPDS contract data are generally on USAspending.gov within five days of the action (three business days to FPDS per FAR 4.604, next-morning transfer, published the day after), with DoD and USACE delayed 90 days (also https://www.fpds.gov/common/html/dodDataAvailability.html and DFARS PGI 204.604(2)). Arithmetic for the quarter ended 2026-09-30: a Sep 30 civilian action is due in FPDS by Oct 5 and published by Oct 7, so the civilian sum is near-final at about Q+7 (TESTED HERE 6-day visibility for CACI GSA/DOJ actions). Verified releases: CACI Oct 21 (lead 14 days), Booz Allen Oct 23 (16), Parsons Oct 29 (22), ICF Nov 5 (29). Tetra Tech and Maximus (September fiscal year-ends) report mid-to-late November (REASONED from prior-year pattern, lead ~35-45), SAIC early December for its Oct-31 quarter (REASONED, ~30). That supports L=4 for the civilian leg. The DoD leg: at the hypothesis's T-10 measurement (Oct 11 for CACI) only DoD actions signed before ~Jul 13 are visible, i.e. under two weeks of a 13-week quarter; TESTED HERE the newest DoD action for CACI visible on Nov 11 is dated Aug 3. For defence-heavy names (CACI, BAH National Security, SAIC, LDOS, KBR, KTOS) the full-quarter reading is never final before the print.
verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: Vendors: Quiver Quantitative government-contracts tracker (USAspending-sourced, company-level; record says $30/mo API), GovWin IQ, Bloomberg Government, plus newly found GovChime (spending-trends analytics, states USAspending receives a nightly FPDS refresh), Bureauify (federal contracting reports, 'updated daily'), Sweetspot federal capture intelligence, and the Apify actors already in the record. Several vendors sell the feed; none found selling the fiscal-quarter-aligned UEI-rollup sum, so C stays 2 rather than 1. Literature: award-announcement event studies are plentiful and mixed: Elayan, Pukthuanthong and Roll (2006) positive abnormal returns and volume; Ferris and Rayfield (J. Corp. Accounting and Finance 2024) reaction scales with award size; Larson and Picou (IPPA) market-model event study on federal/military awards; Samunderu and Yordanova (pharma, federal spending open data) find limited impact; CESifo WP 7534 and Bank of Lithuania (2026) in the record find effects only for competitive awards. No paper or dataset was found that tests summed quarterly obligations as a nowcast of contractor revenue or book-to-bill, which is both the edge and the reason the mechanism is unvalidated.

rows.name: Wikipedia pageviews and Google Trends for single-product consumer small caps

justifications.text: A: Wikimedia Pageviews API is DATA, keyless JSON, CC0 (primary series per the vet); the Google Trends cross-check is partly blocked from the container: pytrends 429s under volume and a single GET to trends.google.com/trends/explore returned 429 (TESTED HERE in record), manual CSV export is browser-only; L: final reading at T-2 per measurement_window; S: pageviews and search interest are attention measures that respond to news, marketing and controversy rather than purchases (record 2; borderline sentiment-like); C: Google Trends charts appear in every sell-side consumer preview (crowded at 1), but the Wikipedia-pageview construction is not sold or charted (record 2); U: ~35 names with an unambiguous brand article or topic entity; H: Wikimedia daily pageviews from 2015-07 (10+ years) and immutable so point-in-time is exact, Trends 2004+ but non-reproducible normalization; G: Wikimedia CC0 is clean but the Trends leg is an unofficial endpoint with a robots flag, listed as legal amber for S23 in the facts sheet -> ambiguous overall.
justifications.lead: QTD mean through T-2 (Trends lags 1-2 days; pageviews daily) -> 2 days -> L=2. No earlier full-quarter point exists because the window runs to the release.

justifications.text: A: the vet made Wikimedia pageviews (keyless JSON, CC0, DATA) the primary, which alone would be 5, but the Google Trends cross-check is an unofficial endpoint that returned 429 on a single GET from the container (TESTED HERE in record), i.e. partly blocked, so 4; L: final reading at T-2 per the record (band 2); S: Phase 1 signal_noise 2 because attention responds to news, campaigns and controversy rather than purchases, the vet had to add an attention-shock exclusion filter, and the pre-announcement drift is expected to carry most of it (indirect proxy, heavy confounders), with Da-Engelberg-Gao's 'In Search of Fundamentals' as the supportive prior; C: the record says every sell-side consumer analyst and most PMs chart Google Trends for these brands in previews and it is in consensus for the obvious names, five papers are listed, and TickerTrends/AltIndex package it (commonly used, 2; the Trends leg alone would be 1 and the pageview substitute carries the same information); U: ~35 names with an unambiguous brand entity (1-4% band, 2); H: Wikimedia daily pageviews since 2015-07 are unrevised point-in-time data, 10+ years free (5), Trends normalization drift affects only the cross-check; G: facts sheet lists S23 as legal amber for Google Trends via pytrends (unofficial endpoint, robots flag), while the primary pageviews are CC0, so terms ambiguous (3); dropping the Trends leg entirely would make it 5.
justifications.lead: The QTD mean of daily pageviews runs from fiscal-quarter start to T-2 (pageviews post with ~1-day lag, Trends 1-2 days); the reading is final 2 days before the release (release day minus 2 = 2 days).

justifications.text: A: Wikimedia pageviews (the vet's primary) returned 200 TESTED HERE with a descriptive User-Agent but 429 with a generic one from this shared IP, and the Google Trends leg is 429 on a single GET with pytrends unofficial, so one leg is effectively blocked from the container, 4; L: final reading at T-2 per the record, so 2; S: vet 2: attention responds to campaigns, news and controversy rather than purchases, Da-Engelberg-Gao's revenue-surprise result is for few-product firms on 2004-2008 data; C: Google Trends charts are in every sell-side consumer preview, the search-volume literature is heavily published, and Man Group warns these signals vanish, so 1 ('heavily sold or published; assume priced in') rather than the record's 2; U: ~35 names with unambiguous brand terms or topic entities, so 2; H: TESTED HERE Wikimedia per-article daily counts served from 2015-07-01 for Crocs, CC0 and point-in-time, so 5 for the primary series (Trends history is non-reproducible and would be 3); G: Trends via pytrends conflicts with Google's terms and robots (facts sheet lists S23 as legal amber), Wikimedia is CC0, so 3 with Trends kept as a cross-check.
justifications.lead: QTD mean from fiscal-quarter start to T-2 (Trends lags 1-2 days; Wikimedia daily counts are available next day). Lead over the release = 2 days.

concerns: data-engineer: Trends is effectively unusable from this IP (429 on one request), so the signal is a Wikipedia-pageview signal in practice; the record should say so. Pageview spikes need the z>3 event exclusion to be coded and its news-matching step is manual. Da-Engelberg-Gao's pricing result predates the chart becoming a standard analyst tool; test net of T-20 to T-2 drift as the vet requires.

quant-pm: The pageview series is testable now and cheap, but the record's own expectation is that for these single-brand names the chart is on every screen and the T-20 to T-2 drift already carries it; the hypothesis correctly nets out that drift, which is the whole test. The Trends leg is rate-limited from this container at one request and sits in legal amber; recommend running the backtest on pageviews only and deciding on Trends afterwards. Keyword/entity choice is the largest source of backtest bias per the cited Journal of Investment Strategies paper.

skeptic: The T-20 to T-2 drift control the vet added is the right test and is likely to show the information is already in price for the obvious names. Wikimedia's rate limits bite on generic clients from this shared IP (TESTED HERE 429), so the collector must send a descriptive User-Agent and pace requests. If the Trends leg is dropped entirely G rises to 5 and A to 5; if Trends were primary G would be 2.

rows.name: Taiwan dedicated-OEM monthly revenue as a sell-in nowcast for US brands

justifications.text: A: TWSE OpenAPI t187ap05_L and TPEx OpenAPI mopsfin_t187ap05_O are DATA (JSON; TPEx threw a transient 520 before 200; TWSE file refreshes ~1 week after the 10th), but the MOPS history interface is blocked from the container. TESTED HERE: /nas/t21/sii/t21sc03_115_9_0.html and /nas/t21/otc/t21sc03_110_6_0.html return HTTP 200 with a 947-byte WAF page 'FOR SECURITY REASONS, THIS PAGE CAN NOT BE ACCESSED' (datacenter IP block); /nas/t21/sii/t21sc03_110_6_0.html is 404 -> live feed 5, history partly blocked 3, blended 4; L: TPEx month-3 print by the 10th same day, TWSE OpenAPI ~17th (record TESTED HERE: September file dated 10-17 still served on 11-11), GOLF/MODG report ~35-40 days after quarter end and FOXF ~30-35, record 15; S: Fusheng/AIM also supply TaylorMade, Ping and Mizuno, Giant/Merida sell own brands, FX and FOB timing blur the pair (record 2); C: Taiwan sell-side covers every supplier, Bloomberg/FactSet carry the monthly series and GOLF/MODG/FOXF analysts can read the 10th-of-month prints (record 3; the critic did not flag N07 for crowdedness); U: 3-4 names (~0.3%); H: OpenAPI endpoints are current-month snapshots, MOPS archive blocked (TESTED HERE), no history in hand and the facts sheet rules N07 forward-collection-only with H of 1 or 2 -> 1 because no backfill is verified; G: official exchange open-data APIs (Taiwan OGDL permits commercial use per the record, REASONED, licence text unread) plus the Nasdaq calendar/consensus robots flag (use EDGAR dates).
