justifications.lead: Taiwan issuers publish month M revenue by the 10th of M+1. TPEx OpenAPI refreshes the same day; TWSE OpenAPI ~1 week later (record: September data still served on November 11). Same-quarter window: month-3 print at Q+10 to Q+17; GOLF ~Q+35-40, MODG ~Q+35-42, FOXF ~Q+32-37, so 18-30 days. The vet's one-month-lagged window (three months ending one month before the brand's quarter end) would make the last needed print land ~Q-20, i.e. 55+ days of lead, but the lag is uncalibrated and the backfill to calibrate it does not exist in the container.

concerns: data-engineer: MOPS is IP-blocked from this container (reported, not worked around), so the 5 years of monthly prints the vet requires cannot be assembled here; possible routes are company IR pages or aggregator pages, both unverified. Start archiving both OpenAPI files daily now with retry logic (TPEx 520). TWSE OpenAPI lag means month-3 data for TWSE names may arrive only ~1 week before FOXF reports. Three to four names gives a test with almost no statistical power.

quant-pm: No backtest exists until MOPS monthly history is re-derived (the record itself says no trading until five years of prints and per-pair lags are assembled); the aggregator pages prove the history exists but the container could not reach the query interface. With three or four names the test has almost no power, and the supplier-to-segment mapping (club heads to Titleist clubs, not Acushnet balls; Giant/Merida to Fox's bike segment) means even a correct read covers a minority of each brand's revenue. Replace the Nasdaq consensus and calendar endpoints (robots flag) with EDGAR dates and the verified FMP key.

skeptic: No backtest is possible until monthly prints are assembled from MOPS or company IR pages and per-pair lags calibrated; the record says at least five years are needed. With three to four names the test has almost no power. The 'gap versus consensus' construction depends on a daily consensus archive that starts today. Attribution noise (multi-brand suppliers) is the dominant failure mode.

justifications.text: A: ECHO effluent-chart REST returns JSON (TESTED HERE 200, 1.18 MB, 110 flow value rows for 2026) and CAMPD API answered 200 with DEMO_KEY in the record; api.data.gov key verified in the facts sheet; NOAA NCEI DATA; L: full-quarter DMR flow is final 19 days after quarter end (TESTED HERE: ValueReceivedDate minus period end = 19 days on all six flow outfalls for every 2026 period, median 19, n=55) and covered names release ~day 24-38, so lead 5-19 days, median ~10; CAMPD quarterly lands ~day 41, after nearly all releases; S: self-reported flow is physical but tracks heat rejection (weather), turnarounds (already disclosed) and outfall mix more than sales, few names are single-site and commodity-chemical quarters are set by spreads (record red team) -> heavy confounders; C: compliance datasets that no vendor converts to equity signals (record; IIR/Genscape sell outages, not flow run-rates), not in sell-side previews; U: facts sheet places S07 in the single-site family where each row covers eight or fewer names, so the record's REASONED 30-40 does not survive the dominant-site filter; H: ECHO DMR values 2007+ with ValueReceivedDate for stamping and CAMPD 1995+, minor caveat that ValueReceivedDate is regulator receipt not ECHO publication and the lag is verified for one Texas permit; G: EPA official REST APIs.

skeptic: The measurement_window text is internally contradictory (candidate says a 4-5 month DMR lag, vet says 19 days; my Louisiana tests side with the vet). Only one permit is mapped and it is not a universe name. Cooling-water flow at once-through sites is often set by pump configuration rather than throughput, so the process-vs-cooling outfall classification is load-bearing and undone. Coverage claim ignores the facts-sheet family cap. Overlaps N03 NPDES leg.

rows.name: Clustered open-market insider buying (Form 4)

justifications.text: A: SEC Form 3/4/5 structured quarterly data sets, EDGAR submissions API and the Form 4 atom feed are all DATA in the record; the SEC User-Agent string is 'not yet set, trivial' per the facts sheet; OpenInsider is unreachable (TLS reset TESTED HERE by vetter) but the record says SEC bulk data replicates it; L: record's vet change (4): blackouts start 2-4 weeks before quarter end and releases come 3-6 weeks after, so the last qualifying buy is 40-50 days before the release and Form 4 posts within 2 business days; S: record signal_noise 2, decades-old factor whose event-window residual is likely mean reversion; C: Verity/InsiderScore, 2iQ and Quiver sell it, OpenInsider screens it free, Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski and Lakonishok-Lee publish it (record crowdedness 1); U: record ~100% Form 4 eligibility but qualifying clusters are 'a few dozen events per quarter', so full coverage discounted one notch; H: data sets 2006q1 through 2026q3 with point-in-time filing dates from the EDGAR daily index (record); G: SEC public data, jet leg with OpenSky non-commercial terms dropped.

justifications.text: A: SEC structured Form 3/4/5 quarterly zips (2006q1-2026q3), EDGAR atom feed and submissions API are all DATA in the record; only the trivial SEC User-Agent is outstanding; OpenInsider unreachable from the container but not needed; L: last qualifying open-market buy precedes the 2-4 week pre-quarter-end blackout and posts within 2 business days, so the reading is fixed 33-70 days before the release (record 40-50) -> 28+ days, though the reading is itself a public filing priced on its filing day so the lead is over the print only; S: insider clusters are informed but the earnings-window residual after 40+ days of public drift is an indirect proxy confounded with value/contrarian (record red team; CMP literature is monthly drift, not earnings-day surprise); C: Verity/InsiderScore, 2iQ (FactSet, WRDS), Quiver Quant and free OpenInsider screens plus decades of papers -> heavily sold and published; U: Form 4 panel covers all ~1,300 names but qualifying clusters (3+ officers, >$250k, non-10b5-1) are REASONED at a few dozen events a quarter, ~100-150 distinct names a year (8-12%); H: 2006q1-2026q3 structured data with point-in-time filing dates from the EDGAR daily index; G: SEC official; the jet leg (OpenSky non-commercial, ADS-B Exchange paid) was dropped.
justifications.lead: For a Sep-30 quarter: blackout starts Sep 2-16 (2-4 weeks before quarter end, REASONED in record); last qualifying buy posts on Form 4 by ~Sep 18 (2 business days). Releases 3-6 weeks after quarter end = Oct 21 to Nov 11. Lead = Oct 21 - Sep 18 = 33 days (minimum) to Nov 11 - Sep 2 = 70 days (maximum); record states 40-50 days. Caveat: the cluster is public on the Form 4 posting day, so its informational lead over the market is 0 days; the 33-70 days is lead over the earnings print only.

justifications.text: A: SEC Form 3/4/5 structured quarterly zips 2006q1-2026q3, EDGAR atom feed and submissions API all probe DATA, only a declared User-Agent needed (facts sheet: trivial); L: a Form 4 posts within two business days of the trade and is itself the public disclosure, the record's 40-day figure is lead to the earnings date not over disclosure, and the red team notes the drift is captured in the days after posting, so the anchor's filing clause applies; S: insiders buy for value and contrarian reasons and by T-1 what remains is mean reversion (record S=2, red team); C: 2iQ, Verity/InsiderScore and Quiver sell it, OpenInsider screens it free, decades of literature (Lakonishok-Lee 2001, Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski 2012), record C=1; U: eligibility is universal but qualifying clusters (3+ officers, >$250k, non-10b5-1) are REASONED at a few dozen events per quarter, the 13-60 band; H: 2006q1-2026q3 structured datasets with point-in-time filing dates from the EDGAR daily index; G: SEC public data, jet leg (OpenSky non-commercial, paid ADS-B Exchange) dropped
justifications.lead: Last qualifying buy falls before the blackout (2-4 weeks before quarter end, REASONED); releases come 3-6 weeks after quarter end, so 35-70 days separate the last buy from the print. But the Form 4 is public within 2 business days of the trade, so the lead over public disclosure is 0-2 days and the anchor's 'filing priced on the filing day' clause gives 1.

concerns: data-engineer: Heavily arbitraged factor; the record itself says to drop it if earnings-window conditioning adds nothing over the generic cluster screen. Coverage score reflects data eligibility, not event frequency: expect only a few dozen tradable events per quarter.

quant-pm: The Phase 1 vet itself reframes this as a conditioning overlay and control variable, not a standalone trade; differentiation from vendor screens is cost only and the record says to drop the earnings-window conditioning if it adds nothing over the generic cluster screen. Expect the drift to be captured in the days after the Form 4 posts, weeks before T-1.

skeptic: By its own vet this is a conditioning overlay and control variable, not a standalone trade; the cluster-screen edge is arbitraged in liquid mid-caps; OpenInsider is unreachable from the container (TLS reset) but the SEC bulk data replicates it.

verifier.changes: L: 5 -> 1. The L anchor reads '1 = 0 to 1 day, or the lead is over a filing that is itself priced on the filing day.' The S18 reading IS a Form 4 filing: the cluster becomes known to us and to every vendor/screener on the same EDGAR posting (TESTED HERE: atom feed updates continuously; trade-to-filing lag median 2 days, p90 4 days across 8,070 open-market purchase rows in the 2025q2 data set). Two of the three panel scorers (quant-pm, skeptic) wrote this caveat in their own justifications, and the skeptic scored it 1; the panel median of 5 only survived because two scorers measured lead to the earnings print instead of lead over public disclosure, which is the opposite of what the anchor says and inconsistent with the facts-sheet treatment of N27/N39 ('filing-day news whose earnings-window residual is reasoned, not shown'). The 33-70 day gap to the print is real but is exactly the case the anchor's filing clause was written to exclude. U: 3 -> 2. TESTED HERE on the full 2025q2 Form 3/4/5 data set (50,861 submissions, all EDGAR filers): applying the record's own rule (transaction code P, acquired, Form 4, non-10b5-1, 3+ distinct officers, >$250k, trade date inside the quarter) yields 28 issuer-clusters in the quarter across the entire filer population. SIC lookup via the submissions API: 15 are in excluded sectors (10 financial/REIT/bank, 4 pharma/biotech, plus Organon SIC 2834), 3 more are closed-end funds/BDCs with no SIC (KYN, NCDL, BBDC), and 1-2 are below $500M (ARQ). That leaves roughly 8-9 in-universe clusters in a quarter that was unusually buy-heavy (April 2025 selloff), i.e. ~35 distinct names a year at most, ~25 once the 'every buy 28+ days before quarter end' condition is applied (20 of 28 clusters passed it). That is the 13-60 band (2), not the 65-250 band (3) the panel reasoned without counting. Relaxing officers to 'any insider' gives 177 clusters/quarter population-wide, but the record's hypothesis is officers only. A, S, C, H, G: kept. A=5 confirmed (every SEC endpoint DATA with a declared User-Agent; FILING_DATE is native in SUBMISSION.tsv so no daily-index reconstruction is needed). One housekeeping flag for A: the zip path changed mid-2026 (2006q1-2026q1 under /files/structureddata/..., 2026q2+ under /files/datastandardsinnovation/...; each quarter exists at exactly one path), so a fetcher must use the landing-page hrefs. H=5 confirmed (2006q1 zip 200, 17.3MB; continuity 2025q3 through 2026q3 all 200). C=1 confirmed (FactSet 2iQ, WRDS 2iQ and Quiver insider pages all 200). G=5 confirmed (SEC data, jet leg dropped).
verifier.refutation: S18 should not be in the top ten because its one claimed edge, a 40-50 day lead, is lead over the earnings print, not lead over public disclosure, and the scoring anchor explicitly assigns 1 to a reading that is a public filing priced on its filing day. Every Form 4 in the cluster is on EDGAR within two business days (observed median 2, TESTED HERE), is ingested the same day by 2iQ, Verity, Quiver and at least five free screens found in one search, and the practitioner evidence says coordinated cluster buying is priced by the day before disclosure. The 33-70 days between the last buy and the print is therefore time for the market to absorb the information, not time in which we hold it alone; by T-1 the cluster is an old, widely published fact and the residual the program would trade is, per the record's own red team, a value/contrarian proxy. Second, coverage was reasoned, not counted: counting the record's own cluster rule on the full 2025q2 data set gives 28 clusters in the entire EDGAR filer population, of which 18 are financials, REITs, BDCs or biotech that the program excludes, leaving roughly 8-9 in-universe clusters per quarter in a heavy-buying quarter, about 25-35 tradeable names a year, often fewer after the 28-days-before-quarter-end condition; the 65-250-name band the panel used is not supported. Third, the blackout premise is leaky: 24% of officer open-market buys land inside the final four weeks of the quarter, so the 'reading is final at blackout start' logic fails for a quarter of events, and there is no public blackout calendar to know which. Fourth, the record itself concedes that the only differentiation from vendors is cost and an untested conditioning twist, and that if the twist adds nothing in backtest the signal should be dropped. With L=1 and U=2 the weighted score falls from 3.60 to about 2.70; even with the panel's generous L=5 the honest U alone takes it to 3.50. The case for keeping it is that it is free, deep (2006+), structured and legally clean, which makes it a good control variable and conditioning overlay, exactly what vet change (5) already reframed it as. A control variable is not a top-ten signal.
verifier.release_schedule_check: Source schedule (TESTED HERE): https://www.sec.gov/data-research/sec-markets-data/insider-transactions-data-sets states the structured data sets are 'updated quarterly' with a cutoff of 5:30PM ET on the last business day of the quarter; observed last-modified stamps are 7-9 days after quarter end (2026q3 posted 07 Oct 2026, 2026q2 09 Jul, 2026q1 07 Apr, 2025q4 07 Jan) with one late post (2025q3 on 18 Nov 2025, 49 days). That quarterly file is only the backtest path; the live path is the EDGAR atom feed/daily index, which posts each Form 4 within the SOX 403 two-business-day deadline (rule effective 29 Aug 2002; observed median lag 2 days, p90 4 days). Earnings timing of covered names (TESTED HERE, submissions API, first 8-K item 2.02 after the 30 Sep 2025 quarter end for 12 mid-caps WDFC HELE ESE KAI MTX AIN NPO ALG TNC ENS FELE WTS): +9 (HELE, off-cycle fiscal quarter), +22, +23, +28, +28, +28, +34, +35, +36, +36, +37, +51; median +34 days. Lead arithmetic to the print: blackout start 14-28 days before quarter end (REASONED, and not universal: TESTED HERE 24% of officer non-10b5-1 open-market buys in Q2-2025 were executed inside the last 27 days before quarter end, 9% inside the last 13), plus 2 business days to post, gives the reading final at QE-12 to QE-26; release at QE+22 to QE+51 (median +34); so the last qualifying buy is public 34-77 days before the print, typically ~46, consistent with the record's 40-50. Lead over public disclosure, which is what the L anchor scores: 0 days, because the Form 4 is the disclosure and the cluster is visible to every vendor and free screener on the posting day; under the anchor's filing clause this is a 1.
verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: One web search (insider cluster buying, earnings surprise, Form 4, opportunistic purchases, InsiderScore, 2iQ) returned no peer-reviewed paper that tests cluster buying against the earnings-announcement return specifically; the hits were practitioner pieces: an Interactive Brokers summary of the academic evidence (purchases informative, sales not, coordinated buying stronger), a Substack analysis arguing coordinated cluster buying is largely priced by the day before disclosure while large single purchases move prices on the disclosure day, and a crowd of free cluster-buy screens (arkolith.com monthly cluster lists, insiderscreener.com, vcpscanner.com, falsifylab 'Form 4 Watch', heygotrade how-to). That is direct evidence the screen is commoditised down to the retail-newsletter level. Vendor URLs from the record re-probed TESTED HERE: FactSet 2iQ listing 200, WRDS 2iQ 200, Quiver Quant insiders 200 (Verity 403 from this IP). Literature already in the record stands: Cohen, Malloy and Pomorski JF 2012 (opportunistic vs routine; 82 bp/month, a monthly-drift result, not an earnings-day result) and Lakonishok and Lee RFS 2001. Nothing found changes C=1 or S=2.

rows.name: Complaint-spike precursor to recalls and warranty charges

justifications.text: A: NHTSA complaints and recalls APIs are DATA keyless; the openFDA device/event (MAUDE) source is listed UNPROBED in data_sources but TESTED HERE 2026-11-11: HTTP 200, meta.last_updated 2026-11-04, 3,948 results for brand 'inspire', and the openFDA key is verified in the facts sheet; CPSC Incident endpoint 404 and already dropped; L: record measurement window ends 3 trading days before earnings (lead_time_days 3); S: record signal_noise 2, most spikes never become recalls and accruals often land a quarter later; C: Kumar et al. publish the NHTSA complaint-return link and plaintiff firms mine the same data, no vendor packages complaint velocity (record crowdedness 3); U: record ~3% (35-40 names); H: NHTSA multi-decade by model year and MAUDE from 1991 (both REASONED in record, 26.8M records TESTED by vetter) with filed/received dates, but the posting lag (days for NHTSA, 1-2 weeks for MAUDE) is REASONED so backtests carry a minor look-ahead caveat; G: US government APIs, keyless.
justifications.lead: Rolling 90-day complaint window ends T-3; reading final 3 trading days before the release -> 3 days.

justifications.text: A: NHTSA complaints and recalls APIs keyless DATA, openFDA MAUDE 200 in the record (26.8M records, last_updated 2026-11-04) with the openFDA key verified, CPSC recalls DATA; the CPSC incident endpoint is 404 and was dropped; L: the record measures a rolling 90-day window ending 3 trading days before the print, so the reading is final 3 days before (2-6 day band); the data would allow a quarter-end window final ~14 days after quarter end (MAUDE 1-2 week lag) but that is not the spec; S: complaint spike -> recall probability -> ASC 450 accrual is an indirect chain: most spikes never become recalls, accruals often land in a later quarter and the literature (Kumar et al.) puts the abnormal return after the recall announcement, not at the print; C: no vendor packages complaint velocity, but the NHTSA-complaint-return link and MAUDE recall-prediction are published (three papers in record) and plaintiff firms mine the same feeds, so the series is known and ours differs only by issuer-level mapping; U: 35-40 names REASONED, ~3%; H: NHTSA dateComplaintFiled multi-decade and MAUDE date_received since 1991, but both are receipt dates so point-in-time needs an assumed publication lag (minor look-ahead caveat); G: government APIs, no scraping; App Store RSS is a public feed.
justifications.lead: As specified: reading taken at T-3 trading days -> lead 3 calendar-ish days (record lead_time_days 3). Data-permitted alternative (not the record's spec): Q3 ends Sep 30; NHTSA complaints post within days and MAUDE within 1-2 weeks, so a fiscal-quarter window is final ~Oct 14; covered names release ~day 25-40 (HOG/PII/WGO/THO ~Oct 25-Nov 5; INSP/PEN/IRTC/TNDM/GKOS ~Oct 30-Nov 10, REASONED) -> 11-27 days. justifications.text: A: NHTSA complaints API is keyless JSON (DATA; TESTED HERE 200 for Rivian R1S 2025 and Tesla Model 3 2023), openFDA MAUDE answered 200 with 26.8M records (record TESTED), CPSC recalls 200, the CPSC incidents endpoint is 404 and dropped; L: the reading is taken 3 trading days before earnings (record) and NHTSA posts within ~2 days (TESTED HERE: complaint filed 2026-11-09 visible 2026-11-11), MAUDE 1-2 weeks, anchor 2-6 days; S: most spikes never become recalls, accruals often land in a later quarter and the RQFA literature puts the return after the recall announcement (record S=2); C: Kumar et al. publish the NHTSA-complaint-return link and plaintiff firms mine the same data, no vendor packages complaint velocity as an earnings signal (UNKNOWN), record C=3; U: record claims 35-40 names REASONED, but off-road powersports (Polaris, BRP) are CPSC not NHTSA products and the CPSC incident channel is dead (TESTED HERE: Harley Street Glide 2024 returned 0 complaints, Winnebago View 2024 returned 1), 13-60 still plausible with device makers; H: NHTSA dateComplaintFiled is multi-decade and MAUDE date_received runs from 1991 (REASONED) with a conservative publication-lag assumption, records can be edited or removed (minor look-ahead caveat); G: government APIs are clean but the App Store customer-reviews RSS (undocumented Apple endpoint) remains in the source list
justifications.lead: Rolling 90-day window ends T-3 trading days. NHTSA complaints appear within ~2 days of filing (TESTED HERE); MAUDE refreshes roughly weekly with receipts through 2026-10-30 as of 2026-11-04 (record TESTED). The reading is final 3 days before the release → anchor 2.

concerns: data-engineer: Point-in-time backtests must add a conservative publication lag on top of dateComplaintFiled and date_received; NHTSA records can be edited after filing. Issuer-level aggregation across models/brands is the engineering work and the mapping is unverified for most of the 35-40 names.

quant-pm: Reverse causality (media stories and class-action solicitation drive complaint surges) is handled only by a 60-day exclusion; device-brand-to-company mapping is manual; issuer-level 2x spikes are rare so the hypothesis may have few events. A quarter-end-window redesign would raise L to 4 at the cost of missing post-quarter recall decisions.

skeptic: Reverse causality from media-driven complaint surges; device-brand to issuer mapping unverified; powersports coverage overstated because ATVs and side-by-sides are outside NHTSA; the App Store review leg reuses the mechanism the facts sheet flags for N33/S21.

skeptic: The 25%-of-closings coverage gate is unmet for every pilot name on today's evidence; the vendor and literature check was never performed (search budget exhausted); the entity matcher is not built; Dallas update cadence unknown.

verifier.changes: S: 3 -> 2. TESTED HERE backtest: I parsed the twelve most recent glore<MMYY>.pdf files (each embeds the same month for the prior five years, giving a 2021-2026 monthly port table) and pulled CLF's 'Steel Products (net tons)' row from nine earnings 8-K exhibits on EDGAR. CLF-mapped ports (Silver Bay + Marquette) quarterly YoY vs CLF reported steel-shipment YoY, 2024Q1-2026Q3: ports +36.6/+44.3/-9.3/-7.3/-33.3/-17.3/+6.5/+18.2/+7.2/+18.7/+5.0 percent vs shipments -3.5/-5.1/-6.5/-5.2/+5.1/+7.5/+4.9/-1.5/-0.8/-6.2/+3.0 percent: sign agreement in 4 of 11 quarters (all-port total: 6 of 11), with port swings 5-10x the shipment moves. The port split tracks pellet production and inventory decisions (Northshore idle 2022 and restart 2023, the 2024 pellet-inventory build, the 2025 Minorca/Hibtac idlings, Stelco supply from Nov 2024) that CLF pre-announces, not the quarter's steel shipments or fixed-cost absorption. That is the anchor for 2 (indirect proxy with sign ambiguity or heavy confounders), not 3 (clear mechanism, moderate confounders). G: 4 -> 2. TESTED HERE https://lcaships.com/terms/ (200): 'Permission is granted to temporarily download one copy of the materials ... for personal, non-commercial transitory viewing only ... you may not: modify or copy the materials; use the materials for any commercial purpose ... you must destroy any downloaded materials'. All three scorers wrote 'terms unread'; they are explicit and carry a non-commercial clause and a no-copy clause, which is anchor 2 under the program's 'no scraping against terms of service' line. robots.txt allows crawling with Crawl-delay 10, and the PDFs are press releases that trade press republishes, so this is not anchor 1. A kept at 4: PDF is one page and pdftotext -layout parses the table cleanly; WP REST API gives structured post dates; still PDF parsing. L kept at 4 with a caveat: the panel's '~3 days after month end' is one data point; the measured posting lag since 2020 ranges 1-25 days (7-9 days through 2025, 1-2 days in 2026) and the per-quarter lead has a 25-quarter median of 15 and a last-12-quarter median of ~20 (min 12), so the 14-27 band holds on the median but 4 of the last 12 quarters fell in the 7-13 band and CLF pre-announcements produced leads of 0 and -1 in 2022Q3 and 2023Q1. C kept at 3: no vendor and no sell-side evidence found, but Skillings' May 2026 piece republished port-level tonnage (Marquette, Cleveland), so even the port split is in trade press; I could not evidence anchor 2's 'commonly used by sell-side'. U kept at 1. H kept at 5: original as-published monthly PDFs with real upload timestamps from Oct 2020 (glore1220 served from /2021/01/) to Oct 2026, 6+ years, plus archive PDFs back to at least Sep 2019 (re-uploaded 2020-09-29) and post records back to Jan 2011; one 'Revised' PDF (glore1123-Revised, Feb 2024) shows revisions exist, a minor caveat.
verifier.refutation: This signal should not be in the top ten for three independent reasons. (1) It does not measure what it claims to. The record targets steel shipments and fixed-cost absorption, but the port-level series tracks pellet production and inventory policy, which CLF pre-announces (Northshore idle 2022, restart 2023, the 2024 pellet-inventory build, the 2025 Minorca/Hibtac idlings to burn down that inventory, Stelco supply after Nov 2024). Tested against CLF's own reported steel tonnage, the CLF-mapped ports got the sign right in 4 of 11 quarters and the all-port total in 6 of 11, with port swings of 20-45 percent against shipment moves of 1-7 percent; a coin would do as well. Steel earnings are set by HRC and auto-contract pricing in any case, and the record itself has already demoted the row to 'a single-name sanity check ... not traded on its own', which is not what a top-ten slot is for. (2) It is a single name with four events a year, so even a true 1-2 point edge on shipments cannot be validated or sized: 25 usable quarters exist and the panel's own H score (6 years) buys about 24 events. (3) The legal line is not clean. The site's Terms and Conditions, which no scorer read, grant 'personal, non-commercial transitory viewing only', forbid copying the materials or using them 'for any commercial purpose', and require destroying downloads; the program's own rule is no scraping against terms of service. The PDFs are press releases that trade press republishes, so a reasonable reading says they are meant for distribution, but that is an argument, not a clean terms page. Added to this, the lead the panel priced as a reliable 17-22 days was 12-13 days in three of the last eight quarters and 0 or -1 in 2022Q3 and 2023Q1 because CLF pre-announces, and the posting lag was 7-25 days in every year before 2026. The data is real, free, parseable and six years deep, which is why it scores well on A and H; but a top-ten signal needs an edge, and the backtest says this one has none over consensus beyond what CLF has already told the market about its mines.
verifier.release_schedule_check: No official release calendar exists. The LCA site has no schedule page (https://lcaships.com/publications/ 200 and the 'Cargo Reports: Reports 2011-2026' menu list reports but state no lag; a web search for a stated schedule found none). The lag was therefore measured TESTED HERE from WP REST post timestamps (https://lcaships.com/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?categories=32) cross-checked against PDF Last-Modified headers, against CLF's 8-K Item 2.02 filing dates from https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000764065.json. Quarter-end (month-3) report post date -> CLF release -> lead: 2020Q3 Oct 8 -> Oct 23 = 15; 2020Q4 Jan 14 -> Jan 25 = 11; 2021Q1 Apr 15 -> Apr 22 = 7; 2021Q2 Jul 21 -> Jul 22 = 1; 2021Q3 Oct 13 -> Oct 22 = 9; 2021Q4 Jan 18 -> Feb 11 = 24; 2022Q1 Apr 13 -> Apr 22 = 9; 2022Q2 Jul 14 -> Jul 22 = 8; 2022Q3 Oct 25 -> Oct 25 = 0; 2022Q4 Jan 11 -> Feb 13 = 33; 2023Q1 Apr 12 -> Apr 11 (preliminary results 8-K) = -1; 2023Q2 Jul 7 -> Jul 24 = 17; 2023Q3 Oct 10 -> Oct 23 = 13; 2023Q4 Jan 2 -> Jan 29 = 27; 2024Q1 Apr 2 -> Apr 22 = 20; 2024Q2 Jul 9 -> Jul 22 = 13; 2024Q3 Oct 2 -> Nov 4 = 33; 2024Q4 Jan 7 -> Feb 3 (preliminary) = 27; 2025Q1 Apr 8 -> May 7 = 29; 2025Q2 Jul 9 -> Jul 21 = 12; 2025Q3 Oct 7 -> Oct 20 = 13; 2025Q4 Jan 8 -> Feb 9 = 32; 2026Q1 Apr 1 -> Apr 20 = 19; 2026Q2 Jul 2 -> Jul 23 = 21; 2026Q3 Oct 2 -> Oct 19 = 17. Median of all 25 quarters = 15 days (matches the record); median of the last 12 = ~20 days, min 12, 4 of 12 in the 7-13 band. Post dates before 2020Q3 are migration artifacts (lag 0 or negative) and were excluded. Q3 specifically (the panel's worked example): 17 days in 2026, 13 in 2025, 33 in 2024, 13 in 2023, 0 in 2022, 9 in 2021. The lead sits in the 14-27 band on the median, but it is not the stable '3 days after month end, 17-22 day lead' the panel described; the posting lag ran 7-25 days from 2021 through 2025 and only fell to 1-2 days in 2026.
verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: No data vendor sells Great Lakes port-level ore loadings and no academic or practitioner study links LCA loadings to Cleveland-Cliffs earnings or returns (two web searches: 'Lake Carriers iron ore shipments Cleveland-Cliffs analyst earnings preview pellet loadings Silver Bay Marquette' and 'Great Lakes iron ore shipments dataset vendor OR study Cleveland-Cliffs stock OR earnings'). What exists: trade press republishes the LCA release within days, and not only the headline: Skillings Mining Review's May 2026 piece (https://www.skillings.net/great-lakes-iron-ore-shipments-rise-8-4-in-may-2026/) quotes port-level tonnage (Marquette 1.04M, Cleveland 447,139), and MarineLink, Professional Mariner, Marine Log, FreightWaves, SteelOrbis, Steel Market Update and AMO carry the monthly release. Argus Media (https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2669980-cliffs-to-idle-minn-iron-mine-cut-pellet-making) and the Star Tribune (Jan 2026) cover the Minorca idling (still idle) and Hibbing's partial idling (2.7Mt pellets in 2025 vs 5.2Mt in 2024, further cuts Feb 2026), which confirms the port mix is driven by pre-announced production decisions. Mechanism evidence from my own TESTED HERE backtest (port table from the PDFs, shipments from EDGAR): sign agreement between CLF-port loadings YoY and CLF steel-shipment YoY in 4 of 11 quarters; the Silver Bay collapse of 2022 (-69% in Oct) and recovery in 2023 are the Northshore idle/restart, both announced by CLF beforehand.

verifier.changes: No criterion changed from the panel median (A=5 L=5 S=2 C=3 U=1 H=2 G=5). Evidence reviewed per criterion: A: all five record sources answered structured or range-served (TESTED HERE), plus a daily bulk zip at download.open.fda.gov (206) not in the record; confirms 5. L: EDGAR 8-K item 2.02 dates (TESTED HERE) give Q3-2026 leads of 29-35 days at the day-5 measurement (AMRX 34-5=29, PRGO 30, AMPH/ANIP 31, HROW 35) and Q2-2026 leads of 25-36 (AMRX Jul 30 = 25, the only 4-band case); typical reading is 28+, so 5 stands with AMRX flagged borderline. S: endpoint is presentation-level (package NDC) with 227 molecules, 824/1586 rows bulk 'Reverified' (all six Amphastar rows re-stamped 11/06/2026), ~25-55 'New' entries per month across the whole list, and ASPE 2025 reports median injectable shortage duration 4.6 years, so transitions are rare and persisting entries are in guidance; ANIP and PRGO have zero shortage rows as suppliers, so beneficiary exposure must be inferred via NDC label counts; this supports 2, not a change. C: one vendor/literature search found no company-mapped shortage-exposure product (USP Medicine Supply Map and Vizient sell provider-side risk analytics; Yale RFI notes IQVIA sells investor-targeted data); series known, ours more granular -> 3 confirmed. U: 5-7 names confirmed -> 1. H: new evidence that Resolved rows are purged after ~3 months (59 rows, update_date 2026-07-31 to 2026-11-04) and the posting-year histogram is survivorship-shaped (2024: 11 rows, 2019: 20) means the shortage leg cannot be backfilled for exits at all; ANDA leg has decades; web.archive.org is denied here; 'forward collection with partial backfill' = 2 stands (a 1 would ignore the ANDA leg). G: openFDA terms/license pages linked in every response, government data -> 5.
verifier.refutation: The signal cannot be validated for at least four quarters and may never be backtested on the event it actually trades. The openFDA shortages endpoint is current-state only and, as measured here, purges Resolved rows after roughly three months (59 Resolved rows, all stamped 2026-07-31 to 2026-11-04); the posting-year histogram (2024: 11 rows, 2019: 20) shows most historical entries are gone. The hypothesis trades NEW competitor entries in the last eight weeks of a quarter that are still open at quarter end; the short-lived entries that produce the sharpest spot-price effects are exactly the ones already deleted, so any in-sample result today is survivorship-biased and web.archive.org is denied from this container. Second, the list is dominated by persistent entries (ASPE median injectable shortage 4.6 years; 824 of 1,586 rows are bulk 'Reverified'), and new entries run 25-55 per month across 227 molecules, so per covered company the count of relevant molecule-level events per quarter is in the low single digits, below the resolution needed to beat consensus dispersion for a company with dozens of products. Third, coverage is 5-7 names and two of them (ANIP, PRGO) have no shortage rows as suppliers at all, so their 'exposure' is inferred from NDC label counts, which the record itself admits is not market share. Fourth, the beneficiaries are capacity-limited and sell under GPO contracts, so a competitor's entry adds price on spot volume only, and management already flags shortage upside on the prior call; USP, Vizient and ASHP publish the same shortage facts to the people who set hospital demand. Fifth, the lead time is solid for the typical name but AMRX's Q2 print (Jul 30, day 30) leaves only 25 days at the day-5 measurement. A signal with U=1, H=2, S=2 and a mechanism no paper has tested belongs outside the top ten regardless of its clean accessibility and legal scores.
verifier.release_schedule_check: Source schedule: openFDA drug shortages docs (https://open.fda.gov/apis/drug/drugshortages/) state 'Frequency of API updates: Daily'; api.fda.gov/download.json shows export_date 2026-11-11 and meta.last_updated 2026-11-11 (TESTED HERE). Drugs@FDA data files page (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/drugsfda-data-files) states files are 'updated each morning, Monday through Friday' (TESTED HERE). So the quarter's status/approval reading is final on the first business day after quarter end (Oct 1 for Q3); the hypothesis measures day 5. Earnings timing from EDGAR 8-K item 2.02 filings (TESTED HERE): Q3-2026 AMRX Nov 3 (day 34), PRGO Nov 4 (35), AMPH Nov 5 (36), ANIP Nov 5 (36), HROW Nov 9 (40) -> lead at day-5 measurement 29, 30, 31, 31, 35 days. Q2-2026: AMRX Jul 30 (day 30 -> lead 25, the 4-band), PRGO Aug 5 (31), AMPH Aug 6 (32), ANIP Aug 7 (33), HROW Aug 10 (36). Q1-2026: May 6-11 (days 36-41 -> 31-36). Q4: late Feb to early Mar (57+ days). Typical lead 29-36 days = anchor 5; AMRX Q2 is the one sub-28 case; the record's 25 is the AMRX Q2 worst case, not the typical value.
verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: Vendor search (one WebSearch): no vendor sells a company-mapped FDA-shortage exposure index for equity investors. Adjacent products: USP Medicine Supply Map (shortage-risk prediction; USP 2025 report claims 98% of sterile-injectable shortages flagged high-risk in advance) and Vizient shortage analytics, both sold to providers; the Yale CRRIT RFI response (2023) notes IQVIA sells investor-targeted pharma data but does not name a shortage product. ASHP/University of Utah list is free and watched by hospital pharmacists. Literature search (one WebSearch): Yurukoglu, Liebman and Ridley, NBER w17987 'The Role of Government Reimbursement in Drug Shortages' (reimbursement cuts -> more shortages, fewer manufacturers; no stock-return or beneficiary-revenue analysis); Galdin, NBER conference paper 2024 'Resilience of Global Supply Chains and Generic Drug Shortages' (offshored injectables 13% more shortage-prone; structural pricing model); Stomberg NBER chapter (descriptive). ASPE/HHS 2025 data brief 'Drug Shortages 2018-2023': median injectable shortage lasts 4.6 years versus 1.6 for orals, i.e. status transitions are rare and persistent entries dominate. No paper found testing competitor shortage entry -> beneficiary revenue surprise or abnormal returns, so the mechanism is uncovered in the literature (supports C not below 3) but also unvalidated. rows.name: Package-download and repo-activity velocity for open-core developer tools

justifications.text: A: npm downloads API (range endpoint), GH Archive bulk, GitHub search API and pypistats are all DATA (Phase 0), keyless, with a free PAT lifting GitHub search limits; L: record measurement window runs to T-1 (lead_time_days 1); S: record signal_noise 2, downloads dominated by CI, mirrors and re-installs, revenue driven by enterprise expansion invisible in registries; C: no institutional vendor found packaging download velocity (record UNKNOWN after search), only VC-side indices and one non-peer-reviewed event study (CommitTrader, null result), record crowdedness 4; U: record ~2-3% (25-35 names); H: npm daily counts from 2015-01-10 and GH Archive hourly events from 2011-02-12, both point-in-time (record), while the Docker Hub and Homebrew legs flagged forward-only by the critic are demoted to live-only secondary features; G: npm public documented API, GH Archive public dataset, GitHub REST API used within its documented limits.
justifications.lead: QTD weekly npm downloads measured through T-1; reading final 1 trading day before the release -> 1 day.

justifications.text: A: npm downloads API is keyless and serves daily history (TESTED HERE range endpoint returns daily counts from 2015-01-10), GH Archive hourly bulk files and GitHub issue search (free PAT lifts limits) are DATA; L: the feature is quarter-to-date downloads measured 1 trading day before the print, so the reading is final at T-1 (record lead 1 day; the QTD-to-T-1 window even straddles the next quarter), although the data would permit a quarter-end variant final ~1 day after quarter end; S: downloads are CI-, mirror- and bot-inflated and dominated by re-installs, revenue is enterprise contract expansion invisible to registries, guidance embeds management telemetry and the one public event study (CommitTrader) found no abnormal returns -> indirect with heavy confounders; C: no institutional vendor packages download velocity (Two Sigma Ventures index, market.dev and Common Room are VC/GTM tools), a few papers on open-source value, informal watching by analysts -> niche, not in sell-side models; U: 25-35 names, ~2-3%; H: npm daily counts since 2015-01 and GH Archive since 2011-02 are immutable point-in-time series; package-mapping survivorship is a design discipline rather than a data gap; Docker Hub, Homebrew and pypistats legs are live-only secondaries; G: official public APIs and datasets (npm, GH Archive, GitHub API with PAT).
justifications.lead: As specified: QTD weekly npm downloads measured at T-1 -> lead 1 day (record lead_time_days 1). Data-permitted alternative (not the spec): npm daily counts are complete ~1 day after the fiscal quarter ends; open-core software names print 3-6 weeks after quarter end (REASONED), so a fiscal-quarter window would lead by 20-41 days. Scored on the record's T-1 spec.

justifications.text: A: npm downloads API is keyless JSON with daily counts from 2015-01-10, GH Archive hourly gz from 2011, GitHub search API and pypistats all probe DATA (Phase 0), a free PAT lifts limits; L: measured 1 trading day before earnings (record), overlapping N09 whose 1-day claim the facts sheet flags; S: downloads are CI-, mirror- and bot-dominated re-installs, enterprise expansion is invisible, and the CommitTrader event study found no abnormal returns, record S=2; C: GitHub and npm series are widely known and used informally by quant funds and software analysts, Thinknum tracked GitHub (REASONED), three studies exist (Emery et al. 2025, Aksoy-Yurdagul and Shah 2025, CommitTrader), ours is free and more granular, the known-series anchor; U: 25-35 names REASONED with 11 named and caps to verify, the 13-60 band; H: npm daily history since 2015 and GH Archive since 2011 are immutable, but the package-to-company mapping and renames carry a hindsight caveat (record) and the Docker Hub, Homebrew and pypistats legs are snapshot-only; G: npm and GitHub APIs are documented and public with rate-limit terms, the Docker Hub v2 endpoint is undocumented (mild flag)
justifications.lead: QTD weekly downloads through T-1; the reading is final 1 day before the release → anchor 1.

concerns: data-engineer: History is deep but the package-to-company mapping must be fixed point-in-time to avoid hindsight selection and rename survivorship; GH Archive backfill is ~70 MB per hour-file. Overlaps N09; the ranking step keeps the higher scorer.

quant-pm: Overlaps N09 (ranking step keeps the higher scorer); the secondary Docker Hub/Homebrew legs are forward-only per the facts sheet. Phase 1 confidence is 10% and the only public test of repository activity found nothing. A quarter-end window redesign would raise L substantially without changing the weak mechanism.

skeptic: The only public event study on repository activity is null; download series are heavily autocorrelated; management guidance already embeds internal telemetry; overlaps N09 (the Docker Hub and Homebrew legs are forward-only per the facts sheet).

rows.name: Earnings-triggered early lock-up release clauses in 424B4 prospectuses

justifications.text: A: EDGAR getcurrent 424B4 feed 200 with a declared User-Agent (TESTED HERE by vetter), daily form index and Form 3/4/5 bulk data DATA, but each prospectus must be fetched and its lock-up section regex-parsed from HTML, the Nasdaq calendar carries a robots flag (facts sheet: use EDGAR-derived dates as primary) and the CBOE delayed-quotes endpoint is snapshot-only; L: the clause and releasable-shares/ADV are fixed at the 424B4 and the earnings date is confirmed ~30 days ahead (record lead_time_days 30), but the critic's adjustment states N39's lead describes filing-day news whose earnings-window residual is reasoned not shown, and the disclosure was public and priced at IPO and sits in Bloomberg lock-up fields, so the lead over undisclosed information is near zero; S: record signal_noise 3, mechanical supply event confounded by price-conditional clause selection and IV embedding; C: Renaissance Capital IPO Pro, IPO Boutique and Bloomberg lock-up expiration fields are standard IPO-desk and trader inputs (record crowdedness 2); U: record ~2-4% (25-50 IPO names a year); H: 424B4 filings enumerable from the daily index (archive to 1994) with the clause era 2020-2026 giving ~6 years and 150-250 point-in-time events, but the hypothesis's pre-event implied-move control has no free history (CBOE snapshot only); G: EDGAR is public, mild flags from the Nasdaq calendar robots entry (legal-amber list) and the undocumented CBOE endpoint.
justifications.lead: Clause and releasable-shares/ADV known from the 424B4 months before; earnings date confirmed ~30 days ahead -> inputs final >=30 days before the release; but the 424B4 itself was public and priced at IPO, so the lead over undisclosed information is ~0 and the post-earnings residual is reasoned, not shown.

justifications.text: A: EDGAR daily form index plus 424B4 full text require HTML/text regex of the lock-up sections, the getcurrent 424B4 feed answered 200 with a declared User-Agent (SEC UA not yet set globally, trivial), the Nasdaq calendar carries a robots flag so release dates should come from EDGAR 8-Ks, CBOE delayed quotes are a snapshot -> fetchable with parsing; L: unconditional clauses are known at the 424B4 months ahead and the earnings date ~30 days ahead (would be 28+), but many clauses are price-conditional (X% above IPO for N of M days) and the record only flags an event when the condition is met 5 trading days (~7 calendar days) before the print, and the facts sheet flags that the claimed lead is over filing-day news whose earnings-window residual is reasoned, not shown -> 7-13 band; S: releasable shares over ADV with a dated trigger is a direct measure of a supply event and fixed-date lock-up expirations carry documented -1% to -3% returns with volume, but it targets the post-event path rather than the surprise, price-conditional clauses select post-IPO winners and recent-IPO option IV may already embed the supply -> clear mechanism, moderate confounders; C: Renaissance Capital IPO Pro and Bloomberg lock-up fields carry these dates, IPO desks track them, Cooley and Kelly-Lv-Twite document the provisions -> commonly used by traders and sold by several vendors, with only the clause-level ADV ratio as a wrinkle; U: 25-50 IPO names a year, ~2-4%; H: 424B4 archive back to 1994 and the earnings-conditional clause era 2020-2026 gives 150-250 point-in-time events (the implied-move control is snapshot-only, a minor control caveat); G: SEC official, but the record still lists the Nasdaq calendar flagged by the facts sheet as legal amber -> mild flag.
justifications.lead: Clause flag and releasable shares/ADV known at the 424B4 (typically 3-9 months before the triggering earnings release). Earnings date confirmed ~30 days ahead (record). For unconditional clauses the reading is final >=30 days before the print; for price-conditional clauses (the common form per Cooley/Renaissance) the record evaluates the condition 5 trading days (~7 calendar days) before the print, so the final reading is 7 days ahead. Facts sheet: the 30-day figure describes filing-day news that was priced at the 424B4 and is on Bloomberg lock-up fields; the earnings-window residual is reasoned, not shown. The event itself is T+1 to T+5, inside the program's hold window.

justifications.text: A: the EDGAR 424B4 feed answered 200 with a declared User-Agent (record TESTED), the daily form index is DATA, prospectus HTML must be fetched and regex-parsed, CBOE delayed quotes are DATA, and the Nasdaq calendar carries a robots flag (facts sheet) so dates must come from EDGAR 8-Ks; L: the clause and releasable-shares/ADV are public in the 424B4 from IPO day and the facts sheet says N39's lead time describes filing-day news whose earnings-window residual is reasoned, not shown, so the anchor's filing clause applies; S: releasable shares over ADV is a direct measure of potential supply but selling is discretionary, price-conditional clauses select winners and implied volatility may embed the overhang, record S=3; C: Renaissance Capital IPO Pro and Bloomberg carry lock-up dates, IPO desks track clauses, and the lock-up expiration literature is established (Field-Hanka 2001, Kelly-Lv-Twite 2024), record C=2; U: 25-50 IPOs a year above $500M with options (record REASONED) of which only a subset carry earnings-conditional clauses, the 13-60 band; H: 424B4s 2020-2026 from the daily index give six-plus years of point-in-time prospectus text with 150-250 events REASONED, but the regex parse and condition-state reconstruction are not demonstrated; G: SEC EDGAR is public, the CBOE delayed-quote endpoint is undocumented (mild), and the Nasdaq calendar must be replaced per the facts sheet
justifications.lead: Clause flag and releasable-shares/ADV are known at IPO (months ahead) and the earnings date is confirmed ~30 days ahead, so the nominal lead is 30+ days. But the content is a public filing from IPO day and the Phase 1 critic required treating it as filing-day news whose earnings-window residual is unshown → anchor 1.

concerns: data-engineer: This is an announcement-window overlay, not an earnings-surprise nowcast (record vet change 1). The implied-move control needs a daily CBOE archive that starts today, so the full backtest as specified cannot be run on free history. Examples in the original candidate were partly wrong (Snowflake/DoorDash were time-based); every clause must be verified per prospectus.

quant-pm: Fails program criterion (a): it is a post-announcement supply overhang, not a nowcast of the quarter, so Phase 1 reclassified it as an overlay (stand aside on longs or defined-risk put spreads when implied move is not elevated). Puts may already price the supply; 25-50 high-vol events a year give little power after costs; underwriter early-release waivers move the event date. Use EDGAR 8-K dates, not the Nasdaq calendar.

skeptic: Fails program criterion (a) per its own vet (an overlay, not a surprise predictor); puts are expensive if IV embeds the overhang; 25-50 noisy events a year; the Field-Hanka and Bradley et al. citations were not re-verified; underwriter waivers move event dates.

rows.name: FAA aircraft-registry diffs as a Textron Aviation delivery nowcast

justifications.text: A: FAA ReleasableAircraft.zip probe_status DATA (nightly, comma-delimited MASTER/ACFTREF/DEREG), EDGAR submissions DATA, no key; L: count final ~QE+7 calendar days, Textron prints QE+22 to +29 (Q3 2026: ~Oct 7 vs Oct 29) = 15-22 days, 14-27 band; S: registry is a direct US-delivery count but exports invisible, cert-issue lag shifts quarter-end units, Aviation only ~40-45% of revenue (record vet 3); C: JETNET/AMSTAT sell fleet data and the free Flycraft monthly registry-delta report (updated 2026-10-09, before the Oct 29 print) plus Aviation Week already count deliveries (record vet lowered to 2); U: TXT only; H: current snapshot only, backfill reconstructed from CERT ISSUE DATE/YEAR MFR with survivorship (resale overwrites cert date), Wayback blocked, true nightly archive starts now; G: FAA public government registry, record legal_risk 1.
justifications.lead: Nightly snapshots; quarter count final ~5 business days (~7 calendar days) after quarter end for cert-issue lag and pending rows. Textron prints QE+22 to QE+29 (Q3 2026: data final ~Oct 7, print Oct 29 = 22 days; Q1/Q2 prints ~Apr 23 / Jul 24 = +23/+24 → 16-17 days). Lead 15-22 calendar days.

justifications.text: A: FAA ReleasableAircraft.zip is free structured text with probe DATA, EDGAR submissions DATA; L: count by cert-issue date is taken 5 business days after quarter end (~Oct 7) vs the TXT Q3 2026 print on Oct 29 (AIN, LITERATURE) = 22 days, typical 16-24 (anchor 14-27); S: a direct count of US Citation/turboprop registrations, but only ~65-75% of deliveries are US (REASONED), cert-issue lag pushes late-quarter units into the next count and Aviation is ~40-45% of TXT revenue (vet signal_noise 3); C: Flycraft/Radar publishes a free monthly registry-delta delivery count (updated 2026-10-09, before the Oct 29 print), Aviation Week counts monthly from the registry, JETNET sells fleet data and an Apify feed exists, so the series is public and sold and our nightly version adds no pre-print timing edge; U: TXT only, one name (single-site physical family); H: a 6-8 year series rebuilt from CERT ISSUE DATE in a single current snapshot with survivorship bias (resold airframes overwrite the cert date), clean nightly archive only from now; G: FAA public government data, no scraping conflict.
justifications.lead: Quarter ends Sep 30; registry count by certificate-issue date taken 5 business days after quarter end (~Oct 7). TXT printed Q3 2026 on Oct 29 (LITERATURE, AIN) = 22 calendar days; TXT typically prints 23-29 days after quarter end, so the lead is 16-24 days. Caveat: cert-issue lag means units delivered in the last weeks of the quarter are not yet in the T+7 count, so the 'final' reading is a truncated read of the quarter, and the free Flycraft monthly report lands ~9 days after month end, also before the print.

justifications.text: A: FAA ReleasableAircraft.zip is a free nightly comma-delimited dump with probe DATA (Phase 0 list) and EDGAR submissions DATA, so 5; L: the record's own window (count settles ~5 business days after quarter end; TXT printed Q3 2026 on Oct 29) gives ~22 calendar days, and Q1/Q2/Q4 prints 24-30 days after quarter end give 17-25, so 4; S: a direct count of US registrations but only ~65-75% of Citation deliveries are US (REASONED in record), certificate-issue lag pushes quarter-end deliveries into the next quarter, and Aviation is ~40-45% of TXT revenue, so 3; C: Flycraft/Radar publishes a free monthly registry-delta delivery count, Aviation Week counts monthly deliveries from the registry, JETNET sells fleet data and Apify sells a registry feed (vet_vendors_found), so 2; U: TXT only (~0.1%), so 1; H: no archived nightlies exist and the ~6-8 year series is reconstructed from CERT ISSUE DATE in a single snapshot with a stated survivorship bias (record), so 3; G: FAA public registry, US government data, no terms conflict, so 5.
justifications.lead: Count treated as settled ~5 business days (~7 calendar days) after quarter end for pending entries and certificate lag (REASONED in record); Textron prints 24-30 days after quarter end (Q3 2026: Oct 29 = 29 days after Sept 30; AIN citation in record) -> 17-25 days; candidate's 16 'trading days' equals ~22 calendar days.

concerns: data-engineer: One name, four events a year: no statistical test possible. A free monthly registry-delta report already publishes the count before the print, so the pre-earnings read is not unique. Backfill is a reconstruction with survivorship, not point-in-time; the FAA owner-redaction programme could hide manufacturer-registered inventory, which the exclusion rule depends on. The zip is ~200 MB nightly (REASONED), manageable.

quant-pm: One name, four events a year: no hit rate can be distinguished from noise for the life of the programme. The free Flycraft/Radar monthly report already delivers the quarter's registry count before Textron prints, so the nightly diff adds nothing on timing. The gap is built against guidance-implied seasonality, not consensus. The only unpriced component (late-quarter delivery slips) sits exactly where the cert-issue lag is worst. Growing FAA owner redaction threatens the manufacturer-registrant exclusion. Q3 2025 was an EPS beat on a revenue miss driven by Bell and Industrial, which the registry cannot see.

skeptic: One name with four events a year; the record's own red team calls any backtest anecdote. The gap is built against guidance-pro-rated deliveries, not consensus, which undercuts the 'not in consensus' claim. The press (Aviation Week, Flycraft) already counts registrations monthly, so the level is public; only the late-quarter slip remains and that is where certificate-issue lag is worst. FAA privacy redaction is growing and could hide the manufacturer-registered inventory the exclusion depends on. Q3 2025 precedent in record: EPS beat on a revenue miss driven by Bell and Industrial, invisible to this signal.

verifier.changes: L 4 -> 2: the panel's arithmetic assumes the quarter count is final ~5 business days after quarter end. TESTED HERE on the 2026-11-10 snapshot: Citation CERT ISSUE DATE lags AIR WORTH DATE by a median 36 days (p25 19, p75 91; 57% >30 days, only 12% within 7 days), and of airframes with an airworthiness date inside each Textron fiscal quarter only 18-64% (Q1-25 0.18, Q2-25 0.56, Q3-25 0.33, Q4-25 0.49, Q1-26 0.52, Q2-26 0.42, Q3-26 0.64) had a certificate by QE+7; the share by the print date was barely higher (e.g. Q1-25 9 of 22, Q3-25 20 of 33). As of Nov 10 (FQE+38, print+12) only 14 Citations with Q3-2026 airworthiness dates are registered against 51 reported deliveries, and 31 of the 38 jets with Q3 cert dates were built in Q2 or earlier. The full-quarter reading is therefore never final before the release; what exists at QE+7 is roughly half of the quarter smeared with the prior quarter's tail, so the strict anchor is 1 and I give 2 for the partial read. Also the panel measured from Sep 30; Textron fiscal quarters end on Saturdays (Apr 4, Jul 4, Oct 3, 2026 per EDGAR reportDate) and prints land 24-26 days after fiscal quarter end (Apr 30, Jul 28, Oct 29, Jan 28; 2025: Apr 24, Jul 24, Oct 23, Jan 22). S 3 -> 2: TESTED HERE, snapshot cert-date count of non-Textron Citations by fiscal quarter vs reported jets: 17/31, 25/49, 24/42, 48/49, 41/37, 28/40, 38/51 (ratio 51%-111%), and the Q1->Q2 2026 move had the wrong sign (registry -13 vs reported +3); the turboprop leg captures 5-10 per quarter against 32-44 reported (15-25%), and the YEAR MFR = cert-year-or-prior filter admits resales of year-old airframes as deliveries. Heavy confounders with sign ambiguity fits the 2 anchor. A, C, U, H, G kept at the panel median: zip serves on GET (HEAD returns 503, a monitoring footnote), FAA page confirms nightly 11:30 pm CT refresh; Radar/Flycraft free CC BY 4.0 monthly report with CSV (12-month window only, now dated Oct 30 2026, i.e. after the Oct 29 print) plus JETNET, AMSTAT, Apify and ai-analytics.org resell the registry, so C=2 stands; no archived nightlies exist (FlightAware forum: FAA does not archive; Wayback blocked), so H=3 for a snapshot-reconstructed series stands.
verifier.refutation: The signal's premise, that the registry gives a near-final US delivery count within a week of quarter end, is false on the data itself. The FAA registration certificate is issued when the Aircraft Registration Branch processes the paperwork, not when the airframe is handed over; new aircraft fly for up to 90 days on the applicant's temporary copy. Measured on the Nov 10 snapshot, the certificate date trails the airworthiness date by a median 36 days for Citations, only 12% within a week, so at QE+7 roughly half of the quarter's US deliveries are missing and the count is padded with the prior quarter's tail; 38 days after Q3 2026 ended and 12 days after Textron printed, only 14 of the quarter's Citations were on the register against 51 reported. The late-quarter slip, the one thing not in consensus and the only reason to trade this, is exactly the portion the registry cannot see in time. Even the snapshot's cleanest version of the count (all certs dated inside the quarter) tracks reported jets at an unstable 51%-111% ratio across seven quarters and got the Q1-to-Q2 2026 direction wrong; the turboprop leg captures 15-25% of reported units and is useless; the YEAR MFR filter counts resales of year-old airframes as deliveries; and there is no point-in-time archive to calibrate any of this, so the trailing-8-quarter scaling ratio the hypothesis relies on cannot be estimated without survivorship bias. On top of that the mechanism is a single name with four observations a year, Aviation is 40-45% of revenue, the Q3 2025 print moved on Bell and Industrial, sell-side already models deliveries from backlog (Jefferies estimates are quoted in the trade press), Radar publishes free model-level registry counts monthly under CC BY, and JETNET, AMSTAT, Apify and ai-analytics resell the same file. A $0-budget overlay that reads half a quarter, mis-signs direction, cannot be backtested and covers 0.1% of the universe does not belong in the top ten.

(3) The panel's 'EIA outage CSV 200 TESTED HERE' is wrong in form: TESTED HERE the URL https://www.eia.gov/nuclear/outages/data/outages.csv returns text/html (the dashboard page, 54 KB), not a CSV; the dashboard's JSON endpoint only serves a config object (firstDate 2007-01-01, lastDate 2026-11-10). This only affects the crowding cross-check, but it was cited as evidence by all three scorers. The NRC primary files themselves are clean: 365-day file 200 text/plain, 365 consecutive dates with no gaps, 95 units; yearly PowerStatus.txt for 1999, 2010, 2015-2026 all 200 text/plain (2015-2019 use a date-only M/D/YYYY CRLF format; trivial to parse). L kept at 5: EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 dates (TESTED HERE via data.sec.gov submissions) give Q3 leads of 30-37 days for all six names, all >= 28. S kept at 3 (panel already lowered from 5), but the backtest evidence below argues it sits at the low end of 3: the one qualifying Talen event in seven years produced no negative EBITDA surprise. C kept at 2 (critic cap, EIA repackaging since 2007, Kpler/Montel/Genscape/Platts sell outage monitoring). U 1, H 5, G 5 unchanged (NRC robots.txt disallows only ads.txt/autodiscover/search for user-agent *; EIA robots.txt allows /nuclear/).
verifier.refutation: The signal cannot be validated and the one test case failed. Parsing the NRC yearly files (TESTED HERE, 2020-2026 plus 1999) gives Susquehanna combined lost unit-days in non-refueling Q3 quarters of 0.8, 7.7, 3.1, 2.5, 6.7, 8.3 and 3.2: the hypothesis's 10-EFPD unplanned trigger never fired in a Q3 in seven years. Outside Q3 the large readings (U1 Q2 2020 41.1, U1 Q2 2022 39.4, U2 Q2 2025 67.8, U1 Q4 2023 10.9) are refueling quarters where separating 'unplanned' from planned needs the company's disclosed outage duration, which the record has no source for; at most two to four qualifying events in seven years, roughly one every two to three years, on a single merchant name. The clearest case, Q2 2025 (~30 extra days), was disclosed by management as a deliberate uprate investment, Adjusted EBITDA rose year over year and guidance was reaffirmed, so even the biggest event did not produce the predicted negative surprise. Dollar scale is also small: 10 EFPD at ~1,300 MW is ~310 GWh, roughly $12-16M at a $40-50/MWh margin, against quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of $90-363M, inside normal consensus dispersion, and hedge buy-backs can cut either way. The remaining five names are regulated with fuel riders (near-zero EPS effect, as the record itself says), so U is honestly 1. The data are repackaged daily by EIA since 2007 and sold by Kpler, Genscape, Platts and others, so the outage is priced the same morning; what is left is a 'consensus has not moved yet' conditioning that requires point-in-time consensus EPS and PJM LMPs, neither of which the record has an accessible source for. A rank of 1 of 59 rests on A, L, H and G, which are genuinely excellent, while the two things that make a signal tradable, sample size and effect size, are close to zero. At best this is a veto rule for long-into-earnings positions on one name, which does not justify the top slot.

concerns: data-engineer: No as-of vintages exist: a backtest built on today's file sees late and amended returns that were not visible at T-5; start weekly snapshots now. quant-pm: Month 3 is after the print for nearly every name, so the read is two-thirds of the quarter. The alcohol-only, Texas-only residual can be wrong-signed against the national traffic trend consensus already holds from card panels and Placer. The backtest carries look-ahead from untimestamped late and amended filings until weekly as-of archiving has run for several quarters. Coverage is likely closer to 8-12 names than 20 once the 20-unit and permit-class filters apply. skeptic: The coverage claim is contradicted by the record's own test; after the 20-unit cut the verified universe is four names. The only tradeable read is 2 of 3 months (Aug posts ~Oct 7, +20 to +30 days before Sept-quarter prints); a two-thirds-quarter proxy that omits the most recent month, with the ~38-40-day completeness inferred from a single snapshot and the refresh cadence UNKNOWN (no agency schedule exists; only the 20th-of-following-month filing due date is published), is band 2, not 3. U 2 -> 1. verifier.refutation: The signal's headline virtue (tax-filed, location-level dollars) is real, but the thing the program trades, the quarter the company is about to report, is not in the file when it matters: for the Sept-2026 quarter every covered name printed before the Nov 7 refresh that completed September, and the same pattern holds in the March and June quarters; only the December quarter (printed mid/late February) and off-cycle KRUS (too few units) give a genuine full-quarter lead. What is actually available at T-5 is two months of alcohol-only receipts (10-35% of sales) from one state (10-25% of units), with the mixed-beverage sales tax inside the numbers, no filing timestamps (so the backtest cannot reproduce what was knowable, and late/amended returns are silently revised), and a ~38-40-day completeness rule inferred from a single snapshot on a portal with no published refresh cadence. Coverage is 8-10 names under 1% of the universe even after adding Darden, so a year yields roughly 30-40 events, far too few to separate a 3-point alcohol-receipts residual from Texas weather, oil-economy and alcohol-incidence noise, while consensus for these chains already embeds national card-panel and foot-traffic trends that drive the surprise. A signal whose full-quarter read is usually final after the print, that covers under 1% of names, and whose history cannot be made point-in-time, does not belong in the top ten of 59.

verifier.changes: L 4 -> 5. The panel's 4 rested on the record's own "25 days" and the vet text's "25-30", not on arithmetic. The primary-leg price series are final at quarter end: ams_2843.pdf TESTED HERE is "Report for 11/10/2026" and the MARS public feed shows it published 2026-11-10 07:57 MST (same day); AMS_3646.pdf (Weekly National Chicken Report) is published Friday for Mon-Fri of the same week. So the full-quarter reading for both primary names is final 31-53 days before the release, above the 28-day bar in every quarter checked. Secondary names (TSN/HRL) that need the slaughter report (final 12 days after the week: ams_3658.pdf dated Nov 5 for Oct 18-24, marked Final) get 20-29 days, but the hypothesis is defined on CALM and PPC only. H 5 -> 4. The USDA legs are deep (ESMIS Broiler Hatchery archive 184 pages back to 1991, Chickens and Eggs back to 1950, TESTED HERE), but (a) the keyless PDF archive of the Daily National Shell Egg Index (Cornell x346g071r) holds only 2025 onward (16 pages, TESTED HERE) and its MARS depth is REASONED, not shown; and (b) the hypothesis is defined against point-in-time consensus revenue, and the record's only consensus source returns nothing for CALM (api.nasdaq.com earnings-forecast: quarterlyForecast null, "Quarterly Earnings Forecast is not available", TESTED HERE) and EPS-only with 1-2 estimates for PPC, no revenue. The backtest as written cannot be run from the named sources; a YoY or sequential-price variant can, so this is a caveat, not a 3. A, S, C, U, G kept at panel medians: A because the MARS v3.1 public endpoints answer keyless JSON (listPublishedReports 200, 69 reports; listPublishedReport/2843 200) and the MARS and QuickStats keys are verified in the facts sheet; S because Cal-Maine's conventional eggs are formula-priced off Urner Barry/Expana quotations, not the AMS index, and specialty plus prepared foods were 44.4% of FY2026 net sales (LITERATURE, 10-K/earnings coverage), which is exactly a proxy with moderate confounders; C because the facts sheet caps at 3 and the panel's 2 already reflects daily sell-side use; U and G unchanged.
verifier.refutation: The hypothesis as written is not runnable from the record's sources: it compares the quarterly USDA price average with 'final consensus revenue', and the only consensus source named returns null for CALM and EPS-only with one or two estimates for PPC (TESTED HERE). With one or two analysts, 'consensus' is a single broker's number and the 'stale consensus' edge is indistinguishable from noise; there is no point-in-time consensus history to backtest, so any staleness result would have to be inferred from forward collection. Second, the mapping is weaker than 'one step removed': Cal-Maine's conventional eggs are formula-priced off Urner Barry/Expana, not the AMS index, and 44.4% of FY2026 net sales were specialty and prepared foods whose prices do not follow the index at all; PPC's cutout exposure is diluted by Mexico, Europe and prepared foods. Third, the inputs are the most-watched numbers in protein, published daily, and CALM's share price tracks the egg price through the quarter, so by the time the 31-53 day lead window opens the revenue direction is already in the price; the earnings-day move is driven by the dividend formula, feed cost and guidance tone, which the signal does not observe. Fourth, the universe is two tradable primary names (U=1), so even a correct signal gives perhaps eight events a year, too few to grade within the program's horizon, and the two names share one macro driver (HPAI/feed), so the events are not independent. A signal whose comparison variable is missing, whose mapping covers under 60% of revenue for its best name, and which yields eight correlated events a year does not belong above broader rows in the top ten.

Both primary names clear 28 days in every quarter checked (minimum 31). verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: Vendor: Expana (formerly Urner Barry) is the industry benchmark for egg and chicken quotations, and Cal-Maine's own filings and releases say most conventional shell eggs are sold at formula prices tied to Urner Barry quotes (LITERATURE: Cal-Maine Q3 FY2023 release via quantisnow; 10-K excerpts via capedge/docoh). That means CALM revenue tracks a paid Expana index, and the free AMS National Shell Egg Index is a correlated but different series (negotiated FOB loose, not the Midwest Large carton quote). Also LITERATURE: FY2026 specialty shell eggs plus prepared foods were 44.4% of net sales (feedstuffs.com), so under half of revenue is a commodity-index mapping today versus 20% specialty in FY2015. Literature on the hatchery leg: no academic paper found testing chicks-placed as a price or earnings predictor; USDA ESMIS describes the weekly report's primary use as forecasting production, and Farm Bureau (2017) notes placements misalign with output when bird weights change. Searches for a sell-side or academic nowcast of CALM/PPC revenue from USDA price series returned only earnings previews (Zacks, Barchart, Dow Jones/FactSet) quoting EPS consensus with 1-2 estimates; no vendor sells the specific quarterly-average-versus-consensus product, consistent with the record's claim, but the inputs are universally quoted.
