justifications.text: A: NCEI SWDI nx3hail JSON, SPC hail CSVs and Storm Events CSVs all 200 (record TESTED HERE), Census key verified in the facts sheet; L: the index uses trailing quarters excluding the current month so it is final by quarter end, OC reports ~22-29 days later and CSL ~22-24, record claims 25, all inside 14-27; S: clear hail-to-reroof mechanism but asphalt pass-through, pricing, roofer labour and roofing's partial share of OC EBIT are moderate confounders (record's own 3); C: storm demand is the most-discussed swing factor, sell-side surveys already cite hail/wind reports (Baird 2016), Verisk and CoreLogic sell hail analytics and the NOAA data is free to everyone, so commonly used; U: 3-4 names (OC, QXO, CSL, ROCK optional); H: SWDI counts to 2008 and SPC files to 2010 confirmed in the record, Storm Events to 1950, near-real-time with no vintage problem; G: NOAA and Census official data.
justifications.lead: Hail index covers the trailing two to three quarters excluding the current month, so it is final no later than quarter end. OC Q3 release ~Oct 22-29 → 22-29 days; CSL ~Oct 22-24 → 22-24; Beacon historically ~Oct 30-Nov 5 (QXO cadence unverified) → 30-36. Shortest typical ~22 → 14-27 band → 4.

concerns: data-engineer: Smallest universe in the batch. SWDI tile queries over many bounding boxes and years are slow and should be cached locally; nx3hail counts are radar-signature cells, not hail size, so the size threshold in the mechanism needs the MESH value field or SPC cross-check. ACS housing-unit weights are annual, fine for this purpose.

quant-pm: Sign is in consensus every quarter; only the magnitude of the rooftop-weighted index is new, and the one-to-nine-month lag structure is the whole model and untested. Two primary names give a sample of about 70 prints since 2008 for OC alone. MESH signatures versus ground-truth damage and the housing-unit weighting are untested calibration choices.

skeptic: The sign is in consensus; only the magnitude is tested, and that needs OC roofing-segment volumes and ARMA comps. Three names give few events. MESH radar signatures over-detect relative to ground truth and the housing-unit weighting must avoid double-counting population bias.

verifier.changes: A 5->4: TESTED HERE 2026-11-11, the record's primary instrument (NCEI SWDI web service, swdiws/json|csv/nx3hail) returned HTTP 500 'An error occured' on all 14 calls, including the two URLs the record marks TESTED (tilesum:-97,33 for June 2025 and count for June 2008), periodOfRecord, nx3hail:inv, and the service's own documented example queries; only parameter-validation errors returned anything else, so the app layer is up and the database behind it is not. The web search found no published outage notice. A fallback the record does not name does work: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/database-csv/v2/ serves per-signature gzipped CSVs (yearly 1995-2025, monthly from 2026-01, columns ZTIME,LON,LAT,WSR_ID,CELL_ID,RANGE,AZIMUTH,SEVPROB,PROB,MAXSIZE), which is free, structured and code-fetchable, but it requires downloading 2-175 MB files and doing the tile aggregation oneself, and the pre-aggregated hail-tiles-* files carry a header that reads 'count of Vaisala NLDN lightning strikes', an unresolved integrity question. Reachable-but-via-undocumented-fallback-with-an-outage-on-the-primary is the 4 anchor, not the 5. L 4->5: all three scorers used stale OC release dates (Oct 22-29, Apr 23). TESTED HERE via OC's own IR notices: OC has reported Q3 in early November since 2024 (Nov 6 2024, Nov 5 2025, Nov 4 2026) and its 2026 cadence is Feb 25 (QE+56), May 6 (QE+36), Aug 5 (QE+36), Nov 4 (QE+35). QXO Q2 2026 was Aug 13 (QE+44) and Q3 2026 is Nov 12 (QE+43; preliminary sales 8-K on Nov 9, QE+40). CSL Q3 2026 was Oct 28 (QE+28). The bulk monthly file for October was written Nov 5 (QE+5) and the November file written Nov 11 holds data through Nov 9, so the full-quarter reading is final at about QE+5. Lead = 30-51 days for OC, 38-39 for QXO, 23 for CSL. The two primary names sit in the 28+ band on every print; only secondary CSL falls to 14-27. S, C, U, H, G kept at the panel median: H confirmed stronger than the panel assumed (raw signature files back to 1995, with the 2008 yearly file written 2016 and 10.4M rows, so vintages are frozen); C confirmed at 2 by the vendor search (see vendor_and_literature_check); S kept at 3 but see the refutation on lag sign.
verifier.refutation: Five arguments. (1) Crowded and formulaic: the exact construction (NOAA hail counts x Census housing stock) is published free by a roofing-marketing blog, L.E.K. sells a NOAA-based weather index to roofing investors, Verisk, Cotality, Cape, Canopy and HailTrace sell hail-exposure layers, Baird's survey has cited hail and wind reports since 2016, and OC and QXO narrate storm demand on every call and at mid-quarter conferences; the sign is in consensus, and the panel's own C=2 implies the magnitude edge is small. (2) The lag may be wrong-signed: the only quantitative treatment found (L.E.K. WISE) reports the roofing boost in the same quarter as the weather and a larger decline two quarters later, while the vet's design excludes the current month and weights the prior one to two quarters, which is exactly where L.E.K. finds payback; the trailing two-to-three-quarter blend therefore mixes a positive and a negative term, and the record's REASONED one-to-nine-month claims-to-reroof lag has no test behind it. (3) Coverage is two names and both are diluted: OC's roofing is one of three segments and asphalt pass-through and price often dominate volume; QXO now consolidates Kodiak (from Apr 2026) and TopBuild (from Jul 2026), so roofing is a shrinking share and year-over-year comps are broken for the backtest and the next several prints; CSL is commercial single-ply membranes where hail-driven replacement is a weaker mechanism than shingles (REASONED). (4) Infrastructure fragility: the primary API answered 500 on every query today, the fallback files are labelled 'experimental', the hail-tiles aggregate carries a lightning-strike header, KNOWN_ISSUES records past gaps backfilled later, and MAXSIZE was once rounded to integers, which matters for a 1.5-inch threshold. (5) A short holding window around earnings is a poor way to monetise a slow, widely known demand pull: with a 30-50 day lead the information is in sell-side storm-comp adjustments and distributor commentary well before T-1, so the T-1 to T+2 residual the hypothesis targets may be near zero even if the fundamental link is real. Weighted score is unchanged at 3.55 after A down and L up, so the rank-6 placement is not obviously wrong, but items (2) and (3) are the ones that could make it wrong.
verifier.release_schedule_check: NOAA publishes no release calendar for SWDI; the lag is read from file timestamps (TESTED HERE): hail-202611.csv.gz written 2026-11-11 holds signatures through 2026-11-09 (about 2 days), and hail-202610.csv.gz was written 2026-11-05, so a calendar month, and hence a quarter, is final at about QE+5 in the bulk files (the API, when it works, is near-real-time). Earnings dates (TESTED HERE by web search of the companies' own notices): Owens Corning 2026 cadence from its IR notices at s21.q4cdn.com/855213745/files/doc_news/ (Owens-Corning-to-Announce-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-on-February-25-2026.pdf, ...-First-Quarter-...-May-6-2026.pdf, ...-Second-Quarter-...-August-5-2026.pdf, ...-Third-Quarter-...-November-4-2026.pdf): Feb 25 (QE+56), May 6 (QE+36), Aug 5 (QE+36), Nov 4 (QE+35); Q3 was Nov 6 2024 and Nov 5 2025 (businesswire.com/news/home/20241009854936 and 20251015787087), so the panel's 'Oct 22' date is at least two years stale. QXO: Q2 2026 release Aug 13 2026 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001236275/000162828026056734/qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm, QE+44); Q3 2026 full results Nov 12 2026 with a preliminary sales 8-K on Nov 9 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001236275/000162828026071846/qxoq3-26preliminaryresults.htm, QE+40/43). Carlisle: Q3 2026 release Oct 28 2026 after close (s22.q4cdn.com/386734942/files/content_files/3Q26-Earnings-Announcement.pdf, QE+28). Lead from a QE+5 final reading: OC 30-51 days, QXO 35-39 days (to the prelim), CSL 23 days. Primary names are in the 28+ band on every print; CSL alone falls to 14-27.
verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: Vendor search (TESTED HERE, web search): L.E.K. Consulting's WISE index (lek.com/insights/ind/us/ei/wise-approach-weather-related-services-demand) is built from NOAA severe-event counts plus degree days and is explicitly marketed to roofing providers 'and their investors'; its regression finds roofing shipments rise in the same quarter as the weather and show a larger decline two quarters later. PipelineOn (pipelineon.com/blog/roofing-storm-demand-statistics-2026/) publishes a free storm-demand formula of severe hail and wind events x exposed housing stock x roof value / contractor density built from NOAA, Census and BLS, which is essentially this signal's formula. Insurer- and contractor-facing hail products: Verisk Respond and 'State of America's Roofs' (hail >= 1 inch the dominant roof threat; cat hail about 33% of roof claims in 2025), Cotality (CoreLogic) 2026 Severe Convective Storm Risk Report, Cape Analytics Hail Intelligence, Canopy Weather, HailTrace, Flash Weather AI hail forecast tool, GAF WeatherHub. Trade literature: Roofing Contractor and Freedonia tie shingle demand to severe-weather reroofing; the Baird 2016 survey already cited hail and wind reports. No academic paper linking hail to building-products earnings surprises or returns was found (two searches). Net: the mechanism is commonly sold and at least one consulting index targets investors directly, so C=2 holds and could be argued to 1; the L.E.K. lag finding is adverse to the record's design (see refutation).

justifications.text: A: all MSHA zips HEAD 200 keyless in record (Violations, Mines, MinesProdQuarterly 54 MB last-modified 2026-11-10), ControllerOperatorHistory.zip TESTED HERE HEAD 200, 4.5 MB, last-modified 2026-11-11; L: record 10 days blends an orders leg visible within a week of issue and a 7000-2 leg that posts the first Friday of month 2 (QE+37, ~97% complete at QE+40) which is 0-7 days before or after early-November prints; S: record signal_noise 3, tons mined differ from tons sold, met-coal earnings are price-driven, aggregates hours track weather; C: record 3, MSHA Mine Data Retrieval System is public and mining sell-side reads it for safety and cost, no vendor sells an equity signal; U: record ~2%, 20-25 names; H: Violations 2000+ (REASONED from definition file), MinesProdQuarterly 2000Q1-2026Q3 DATA, controller history now verified for point-in-time mapping, but the quarterly file is a rolling snapshot with no archived vintages so the 7000-2 leg carries a fill-in look-ahead caveat; G: MSHA government open data.
justifications.lead: Orders leg: last qualifying order at QE, Violations.zip refreshes weekly, so visible by QE+7; coal and metals releases ~QE+30-45 gives 23-38 days. 7000-2 leg: file posts QE+37 and is ~97% complete at QE+40 against the same releases, giving -10 to +8 days (negative for late-October reporters). Record's blended 10 days reflects the orders leg's 5-trading-day cutoff rule.

justifications.text: A: MSHA Violations.zip, Mines.zip and MinesProdQuarterly.zip HEAD 200 on 2026-11-11, keyless CSV in zip, index and schedule pages 200; L: the primary orders leg requires an issue date at least 5 trading days before the release so the window closes about T-7 calendar days (record's 10 days), while the 7000-2 leg posts the first Friday of month 2 (QE+36, Nov 6 for Q3) and was only ~97% complete at QE+40 TESTED HERE, which is 0-4 days before or after MTX (~QE+23), BTU (~QE+30), EXP/USLM (~QE+28-30) prints, so that leg is band 1 and the signal sits in 7-13; S: a 103(k)/104(d)/107(a) order at a mine with 20%+ of a controller's output is a direct physical cut to tons, but tons mined differ from tons sold, met-coal P&L is price and freight driven, aggregates hours track weather, and operators 8-K big orders, as the vetter's 4-to-3 cut states; C: MSHA's Mine Data Retrieval System is public and read by mining sell-side, mine-level production is republished by data vendors, no equity-signal vendor exists, so a known series with a cheaper, more granular framing; U: 20-25 names, about 2%; H: Violations and 7000-2 back to 2000 with issue dates preserved, but the files are current snapshots (orders vacated or modified, posting history of 7000-2 rows not preserved), a minor look-ahead caveat; G: MSHA government data.
justifications.lead: Orders leg: weekly file, window closes T-5 trading days (~T-7 calendar); events can land QE-90 to T-7. 7000-2 leg: posts QE+36 (first Friday of month 2), ~97% complete at QE+40; releases MTX ~QE+23, EXP/USLM ~QE+28-30, BTU ~QE+30, AMR/HCC/METC/CEIX/HNRG/KNF/CDE/HL/MP ~QE+35-40, so lead -13 to +4 days for that leg. Record claims 10.

justifications.text: A: Violations.zip, Mines.zip and MinesProdQuarterly.zip HEAD 200 keyless (record TESTED HERE); L: the orders window ends 5 trading days (~7 calendar) before the release by construction, 107(a) orders are also 8-K Item 1.04 disclosures within 4 business days, and the 7000-2 leg posts the first Friday of month 2 (Nov 6 for Q3) which is -9 to +6 days versus coal/metals releases, so the composite sits in 2-6 despite the record's 10; S: a closure order is a direct physical disruption for one mine but tons mined differ from tons sold, hours are weather-confounded for aggregates and earnings are price-driven (record's own 3); C: MSHA data is public and read by mining sell-side for safety/cost commentary, no vendor sells the controller-level nowcast, so a known series with a more granular version; U: 20-25 names ≈ 1.5-2% on the orders leg, roughly half on the 7000-2 leg; H: files run from 2000 but are current snapshots where contested orders are modified or vacated and controller mappings change (ControllerOperatorHistory UNPROBED), a minor look-ahead caveat; G: federal regulator open data.
justifications.lead: Orders leg: weekly Violations posting; measurement window ends 5 trading days (~7 calendar days) before the release by construction, and 107(a) imminent-danger orders must be filed on 8-K Item 1.04 within 4 business days. 7000-2 leg: posts first Friday of the second month after quarter end (Nov 6, 2026 for Q3); typical coal/metals releases Oct 28-Nov 12 → -9 to +6 days. Record claims 10; lower of record and arithmetic → 2.

concerns: data-engineer: Weekly 121 MB Violations.zip and 54 MB quarterly file downloads are fine but the quarterly file's last-modified history must be archived from now on to make the 7000-2 leg point-in-time. Material closure orders are usually 8-K'd within days, so the lead over the company's own disclosure may be near zero for the events that matter. Rare events (handful per year across ~25 names).

quant-pm: Qualifying orders at material mines are rare (a handful a year across ~25 names); the record's own kill criterion is fewer than ~40 events since 2015, which is likely. Material orders are 8-K'd within days and priced then. Commodity price, not volume, drives these prints. The 7000-2 leg is mostly look-ahead for early reporters.

skeptic: Qualifying orders at mines that are 20%+ of a controller's output are rare (record expects possibly fewer than 40 since 2015) and material shutdowns are press-released within days, so the earnings-day residual is unlikely to survive the order-day return control. The 7000-2 leg is look-ahead for roughly half the names.

verifier.changes: S 3->2 and C 3->2; A, L, U, H, G kept at the panel median. S (TESTED HERE): the primary orders leg passes the record's own 40-event gate (156 qualifying orders at mines with >=20% of a controller's prior-year hours/tons, open 7+ days, 108 distinct controller-quarters since 2015), but 141 of the 156 (and 781 of 819 long-open orders of the three types at covered controllers) are 103(k) accident-control orders, which withdraw miners from the accident area and are routinely modified to let the rest of the mine run while the order stays open for the investigation; the file has no scope field (NO_AFFECTED is 0 for every one of the 781 long-open 103(k) orders, so it cannot be used to size them). Example: Warrior Mine No. 7 (0101401, 50-90% of Warrior's hours) carried 103(k) orders open 213 days (2017), 90 days (2022) and 84 days (2024) in quarters when it was Warrior's main producer. So 'order open 7+ days at a 20% mine' is not a measure of lost tons; the sign is ambiguous for the event that carries 90% of the sample, which is anchor 2 (indirect proxy with sign ambiguity), not anchor 3. The 7000-2 leg additionally reports hours only (no output) for the ~half of names that are metal/nonmetal. C (search TESTED HERE): S&P Global Platts/Market Intelligence runs a standing quarterly series of MSHA mine-level production notes published within days of each posting (e.g., 'IB Q3 output totals 16.8 million st, up 19.6% on quarter: MSHA' 2020-11-13; 'US coal production is trending lower year over year' 2026-09-18 citing H1 2026 MSHA reports), i.e. a major vendor republishes the exact series and coal sell-side already reads it; the same 104(d)/107(a)/103(k) order counts are mandatory issuer disclosures in every 10-Q Exhibit 95 (Dodd-Frank 1503) and 107(a) orders must be 8-K'd under Item 1.04 within 4 business days (EDGAR TESTED HERE: BTU 2026-10-16, AMR 2026-05-15, CNR 2026-05-19, HNRG 2026-06-03, ARLP 2026-04-07 all filed Item 1.04 8-Ks). That is anchor 2 (commonly used by sell-side, republished by a vendor); the controller-level roll-up is a trivial transformation, not a granularity that matters, and the facts sheet already directs not to score standard sell-side inputs above 3 without a stated reason. L kept at 3 but on different arithmetic than the record: the 7000-2 leg is band 1 in Q2 and Q3 (14 of 15 names reported on or before the Nov 6, 2026 posting; same pattern Nov 7, 2025 and Aug 7, 2026), band 2-3 in Q1 (4-10 days for ~10 names) and band 3-5 in Q4 (6-34 days for 10 of 13 names); the orders leg's full-quarter reading is final at the first Friday posting after QE (max issue date in the Nov 6 file was Nov 5, so ~1-7 day lag) versus releases at QE+26 to QE+40, i.e. band 4; the blend lands at 3. H kept at 4: 2000Q1-2026Q3 verified, ControllerOperatorHistory has CONTROLLER_START_DT/END_DT (point-in-time mapping possible), but the quarterly file is a rolling snapshot with no vintages, and the 'weekly fill-in' the record assumes could not be observed (2026Q3 row count unchanged at 22,433 between the Nov 10 and Nov 11 probes; inner file stamped Nov 6).
verifier.refutation: The signal is two legs stapled together, and neither leg does what the rank-8 score assumes. The 7000-2 leg has zero or negative lead in two of four quarters for essentially every covered name (Q3 2026: 14 of 15 names reported on or before the Nov 6 posting; Q2 2026: 14 of 15; TESTED HERE from EDGAR 8-K dates) and the record's list of names that 'report around or after' the posting is wrong for seven of nine; the only quarter where it reliably leads is Q4, and there the exact mine-level tonnage is republished by S&P Global within days and already sits in coal sell-side models, while the file is a rolling snapshot with no vintages, so a backtest cannot know what was posted on the first Friday versus later (and this probe found no fill-in at all between Nov 6 and Nov 11, which also undercuts the 'weekly fill-in' story). The orders leg, which the record promoted to primary to rescue the lead time, has enough events (156 qualifying orders, 108 controller-quarters since 2015) but 90% of them are 103(k) accident-scene orders that keep a mine's unaffected sections running while the order stays open for the investigation; the file carries no scope field (NO_AFFECTED is zero on all 781 long-open 103(k) orders), and Warrior's main mine carried such orders open 213, 90 and 84 days in normal production years, so 'open 7 days at a 20% mine' is not a measurement of lost tons and the sign of the volume surprise is unknown. The subset that does imply withdrawal of the whole workforce, 107(a) orders, must be 8-K'd within four business days and all order counts appear in every 10-Q Exhibit 95, so the issuer's own disclosure, not MSHA's weekly file, is the first public print; the one event study on these disclosures found no return effect. Add that the names trade on met-coal and metals prices rather than volumes, that hard-rock names (CDE, HL, MP) pre-release production, that tons mined are not tons sold, and that the universe is 15-20 names at 1-2% coverage, and what remains is a free, well-documented safety dataset that is a standard sell-side input, with a thin, sign-ambiguous residual for a 2-10 day earnings trade. On adjusted scores (A5 L3 S2 C2 U2 H4 G5) it belongs in the middle of the list, not the top ten.

verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: Vendor (search TESTED HERE): S&P Global Platts / Market Intelligence publishes a standing quarterly series of MSHA-derived mine-level and basin-level production notes within days of each posting (e.g., 'Northern Appalachia Q2 coal production tumbles to over 25-year low: MSHA' 2020-08-13, 'IB Q3 output totals 16.8 million st, up 19.6% on quarter: MSHA' 2020-11-13 naming individual mines such as CONSOL Bailey at 3.05 million st, and 'US coal production is trending lower year over year' 2026-09-18 citing H1 2026 MSHA reports totaling 101.4 million st), so the 7000-2 tonnage series is republished by a major vendor and read by coal sell-side; no vendor selling an MSHA-derived equity signal was found; data.gov catalog republishes the raw set. Issuer disclosure of the same orders is mandatory: Dodd-Frank 1503 / Reg S-K Item 104 Exhibit 95 tables in every 10-Q and 10-K count 104(d), 107(a) and other orders by mine, and Form 8-K Item 1.04 requires 107(a) imminent-danger orders and pattern notices within four business days (SEC small entity compliance guide sec.gov/files/rules/final/2011/33-9286-secg.htm; White & Case and Crowell alerts); EDGAR TESTED HERE shows Item 1.04 8-Ks from BTU (2026-10-16), AMR (2026-05-15, 2025-09-19), CNR (2026-05-19, 2026-05-04, 2026-01-12), HNRG (2026-06-03, 2026-03-27), ARLP (2026-04-07, 2025-02-07), HCC (2025-08-01), HL (2024-10-03). concerns: data-engineer: Large campaigns are priced on the filing day and often quantified by the company then, so the anchor-1 lead clause arguably applies to the events big enough to move gross margin; scored on the record's quarter-tally timing. Daily archiving of the flat file from now on would remove the POTAFF-amendment look-ahead. The remedy-cost classifier is the whole signal and has no ground truth.

The record's own kill criterion is fewer than ~60 qualifying firm-quarters since 2015. Overlaps S24 in the merge step.

verifier.changes: Changed U from 2 to 1. Evidence (TESTED HERE, FLAT_RCL_POST_2010 parsed 2026-11-11): matching the record's 16 self-filing names (THO incl. Jayco/Keystone/Airstream/Tiffin/Heartland/Dutchmen/Entegra/Cruiser RV, WGO incl. Newmar/Grand Design, LCII, PATK, PII incl. Indian/GEM, HOG, REVG incl. E-One/Spartan/Collins/Champion/Ferrara/Goshen, BLBD, OSK incl. Pierce/JLG/McNeilus, WNC, RIVN, LCID, FOXF, GT, DORM, SMP) gives 2,078 campaigns but PATK and SMP have zero self-filed campaigns, FOXF has 2 and DORM 3 since 2010, so only 13-14 names have any filing activity (1.0-1.1% of 1,300) and only 9 tickers (THO, HOG, WGO, PII, LCII, GT, DORM, BLBD, RIVN) have ever had a firm-quarter with 25k or more hardware-remedy units since 2015, which is what the signal needs to fire; 9 active names is under the 12-name floor for U=2. All other criteria kept at the panel median: A=5 confirmed (every data endpoint 200, structured tab-delimited or JSON, keyless, daily last-modified 2026-11-11); L=4 confirmed by arithmetic (tally public by about QE+8 to QE+10 given RCDATE-to-DATEA lag p50 1 day, p90 3 days; releases PII QE+27, HOG QE+29, WGO FQE+53, THO FQE+53, so median lead about 19-20 days); S=2 kept (per-unit cost unobservable, and only 8 of 359 covered firm-quarters exceed 100k hardware units, so the proxy is dominated by a handful of outliers); C=3 kept (no vendor sells an accrual nowcast but the recall series is tracked by Newscatcher, Apify, BizzyCar, Recall Masters, api.ai-analytics.org and several published event studies); H=4 confirmed and the look-ahead caveat quantified (flat-file POTAFF differs from the campaign's first-quarter INVOLVED figure in 4.3% of 12,024 campaigns and from the latest in 0.5%, so amendments touch about 4% of records; no vintages, web.archive.org denied); G=5 kept.
verifier.refutation: The signal fails the record's own go/no-go gate before any trading test is run. The vet instructions say to count qualifying firm-quarters since 2015 and abandon if under about 60. TESTED HERE on the full post-2010 flat file: the 16 named filers produce 359 firm-quarters with at least one campaign since 2015, but the 1%-of-consensus-quarterly-revenue trigger needs on the order of 40k-160k hardware-remedy units in a quarter (HOG ~$1.1B quarterly revenue at $150-300 per unit, THO ~$2.4B), and only 19 firm-quarters reach 50k hardware-class units, 35 reach 25k, 8 reach 100k, and 1 reaches 250k. The realistic qualifying count is 15-25 events in eleven years, concentrated in THO (9 at 25k+), HOG (7) and WGO (6), with PII, LCII, GT, DORM, BLBD and RIVN contributing one to four each and PATK, SMP, FOXF, WNC, OSK, REVG and LCID contributing none. A 20-event sample cannot resolve a 50 bp gross-margin effect against the controls in the hypothesis, and the largest single event (THO 2017Q4, 1.47M units) would dominate any regression. Second, the lead is over information that is already public and, for campaigns this large, press-released and often quantified by the company at filing, so the earnings-day residual is reasoned not shown, exactly the pattern the Phase 1 critic flagged for N27 and N39. Third, the two names with the longest leads and most events, THO and WGO, have fiscal quarters (ending Oct/Jan/Apr/Jul and late Nov/Feb/May/Aug) that do not align with NHTSA's calendar-quarter completion reports, so the completion leg is unusable for them and lands 0-8 days before the prints of the calendar-quarter names, adding no lead. Fourth, per-unit remedy cost is unobservable and the corrective-action text is amended in place (no vintages, archive blocked), so the proxy's estimation error is larger than the effect being tested. With free data (A=5) and clean terms (G=5) carrying the score, this is a well-sourced dataset without a tradable event frequency; a signal that cannot produce 60 historical events should not sit above candidates that can.
verifier.release_schedule_check: Source schedule (TESTED HERE via https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/49/573.6 and https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/49/573.7; ecfr.gov and www.nhtsa.gov are blocked from this IP): 49 CFR 573.6(b) requires the Part 573 report within 5 working days of the defect determination; 49 CFR 573.7(d) requires the quarterly completion report on or before the 30th day after each calendar quarter (Apr 30, Jul 30, Oct 30, Jan 30). Measured publication lag in the flat file (TESTED HERE, covered names, 2020+, n=895): RCDATE to DATEA p50 1 day, p90 3 days, max 6. So a decision on the last day of a quarter is filed by about QE+7 and visible in the flat file by about QE+8 to QE+10; the full-quarter campaign tally is final about QE+10 at worst. Measured completion-report submission lag (TESTED HERE, 2025-3 to 2026-3): p50 20-23 days, p90 28-30 days after quarter end. Release dates confirmed by web search (TESTED HERE): PII Q3-2026 on Oct 27 (QE+27, lead ~17 days), HOG Q3-2026 on Oct 29 (QE+29, lead ~19), WGO FQ4-2026 on Oct 21 (fiscal quarter ended ~Aug 29, FQE+53, lead ~43), THO FQ4-2026 on Sep 22 for the quarter ended Jul 31 (FQE+53, lead ~43; note the data-engineer scorer's 'Oct-31 FY' for THO is wrong, Thor's fiscal year ends July 31 and its quarters end Oct/Jan/Apr/Jul). Panel-reasoned dates for the rest (WNC ~QE+22-24, DORM/SMP/OSK ~QE+28-30, LCII/RIVN/LCID/FOXF/GT ~QE+35, BLBD ~QE+50, REVG Oct-FQ ~FQE+40) give leads of 12-40 days. Median lead across the 16 names is about 19-20 days, inside the 14-27 band, so L=4 holds. The completion-report leg (due QE+30, typically filed QE+20-23) lands 0-8 days before the calendar-quarter names' prints and is misaligned with THO, WGO and REVG fiscal quarters entirely, so it adds essentially no lead.
verifier.vendor_and_literature_check: Vendor search (TESTED HERE, two web searches): no institutional alt-data vendor sells a recall-accrual or warranty nowcast. What exists is raw-series repackaging and monitoring: Newscatcher 'NHTSA vehicle safety recalls tracker' (newscatcherapi.com), an Apify 'nhtsa-recalls-tracker' actor, BizzyCar quarterly recall-volume reports (Q1 and Q2 2026), Recall Masters (dealer-facing recall marketing data), api.ai-analytics.org CC0 repackaging of the completion file (from the record), data.gov 'Recalls Data' catalog entry (updated Apr 2026). One recall-API vendor's marketing claims investors use recall data for auto shorts, a vendor claim only. Literature search (TESTED HERE): event studies on recall announcements are plentiful: a 2,576-recall US 2010-2021 study finding negative announcement reactions; a 201-recall 1980-2016 study finding insignificant CARs in (-5,5) and (-2,2) windows (RePEc globus 2018); Rupp 2004 (Review of Industrial Organization) on indirect versus direct recall costs; a 1992 SMJ study finding more negative returns for replace-versus-repair remedies; a 2024 CEO-specialist study; Astvansh, Ball and Josefy (MSOM 2022) on recall timing and process; a 2026 poster pairing NHTSA recalls for six large automakers with daily returns and noting that ~80% of consequence summaries carry boilerplate 'increasing the risk of a crash' text, so keyword severity classification misfires. No paper links Part 573 filings or completion counts to warranty-accrual or gross-margin surprises at earnings. Conclusion: the input series is well known and widely monitored (C no higher than 3), the specific accrual mapping is novel, and the only literature support for a lagged effect remains the JFR post-recall-drift manuscript cited in the record.

justifications.text: A: California DocQNet is a single-page app whose search requires form interaction (headless or reverse-engineered POST) TESTED HERE, Minnesota CARDS reachable but PDF access UNPROBED, Indiana PDF availability UNKNOWN, Wisconsin unreachable (000 twice), and extraction is pdfplumber on large or scanned PDFs; L: FDDs are due 120 days after fiscal year end (Apr 30 for December filers) and posted by states days to weeks later, so the Q1 print (Apr 25-May 10) is led by -15 to +10 days and otherwise the Q2 print by 65-100 days, matching the record's 10 for the first affected release; S: Item 20 history duplicates the 10-K unit counts already public for weeks, projected openings are legally conservative, the incremental Item 19 and state-level terminations are annual and about four months stale, and PDFs are scanned, per the vetter's 2; C: FRANdata sells FDD-derived data (resold by Research and Markets) and franchise specialists and restaurant analysts read Item 19; U: about 30 franchisors, ~2.5%; H: multi-year PDFs on CA/MN portals are REASONED not verified and history must be reconstructed from ~350 filings; G: state public records, but SPA automation with no documented API is a mild flag.

justifications.text: A: California DocQNet is a single-page app whose search needs form interaction (headless or reverse-engineered POST), Minnesota CARDS and Indiana are reachable but no FDD PDF retrieval was demonstrated and Indiana PDF availability is UNKNOWN, Wisconsin unreachable from the container, so free but needs headless or manual download; L: FDD renewals post in late April to May while Dec-FY franchisors report Q1 in late April to early May, giving a lead of negative to ~20 days or a jump to the Q2 release, record claims 10, inside 7-13; S: annual data four months stale at posting, Item 20 duplicates 10-K unit counts, projected openings are legally conservative and PDFs are often scanned (record's own 2); C: FRANdata sells FDD-derived data and franchise specialists and restaurant analysts read Item 19/20 (vet_vendors_found), so sold and used; U: ~30 names claimed at 2.3% but EWCZ, LOCO, DENN and XPOF sit at or below the $500M floor, leaving ~25 ≈ 1.9%; H: multi-year PDFs on the state portals are REASONED not verified and history must be reconstructed from archived filings; G: state government public records with a mild flag for SPA scraping or a reverse-engineered POST on a government portal.
justifications.lead: FDD renewal due 120 days after FYE (Apr 30 for Dec FY); state posting days to weeks later (May). Dec-FY Q1 releases: DPZ ~Apr 28, CHH/WH ~Apr 29-May 1, WING ~Apr 30-May 7, WEN ~May 2, HRB (Jun FY) ~May 7, PLNT/PZZA ~May 8, JACK (Sep FY) ~May 14 → lead from negative to ~20 days; when posting misses Q1 the next release is Q2 at ~60-90 days. Record claims 10 → 7-13 band → 3.

concerns: data-engineer: Accessibility is unproven end to end: no FDD PDF has been fetched by code from any of the three portals, CARDS is blocking this IP today, and DocQNet needs form automation. Extraction from scanned or very large PDFs is error-prone. Annual data gives ~1 observation per name per year; the 350-observation backtest depends on portals holding and serving ten years of PDFs, which is REASONED only.

quant-pm: Annual conditioning screen, not an event signal: one observation per name per year, four months stale by posting, duplicating the 10-K on the parts the market cares about. Extraction cost is high relative to a $0 budget and the portals' history depth is unverified. Fine as a franchisee-distress filter, not as a trade.

skeptic: An annual conditioning screen, not an event signal; one observation per name per year. The market has the 10-K unit counts weeks before the FDD posts. Extraction from scanned PDFs is error-prone and no PDF was actually pulled during vetting.

rows.name: openFDA MAUDE device-event report velocity per manufacturer

justifications.text: A: openFDA device event endpoint 200 in record (needs curl -g for brackets), 510(k) 200, recall endpoint DATA, openFDA key verified per facts sheet for higher rate limits; L: record 14 days, months 1-2 of the quarter are complete at ~QE+7 (30-day MDR lag plus ~1 week publication, TESTED in record last_updated 2026-11-04 with date_received through 2026-10-30) and covered medtechs report 16-30 days later, the full-quarter month-3 reading is final ~QE+37 after most prints; S: record signal_noise 2, MDR velocity is dominated by installed-base growth, summary-report batches, duplicates and litigation filings; C: record 3, no vendor sells a MAUDE equity signal, recall-prediction papers exist (West J Emerg Med 2025, GWU thesis) and Innolitics offers an alerts tool, sell-side cites spikes anecdotally; U: record ~2-3%, 25-35 names; H: 1991 onward per openFDA (REASONED) with date_received allowing a point-in-time cut, but ~a third of MDRs filed late (UNVERIFIED in record) and the weekly snapshot's revisions are a minor look-ahead caveat; G: openFDA official API.
justifications.lead: Months 1-2 reading final ~QE+7. Releases: ITGR ~QE+23, NVST/ATRC/IART ~QE+28-30, DXCM ~QE+30, PEN ~QE+29, TNDM/GMED ~QE+36, PODD ~QE+37. Lead = 16-30 days for the two-month reading; record states 14. The full-quarter reading (month 3 complete) lands ~QE+37, after most releases.

justifications.text: A: openFDA device/event TESTED HERE 200 (curl -g), 510k 200, recall endpoint DATA, openFDA key verified for rate limits; L: MDRs are due 30 days after awareness and openFDA publishes weekly (TESTED HERE last_updated Nov 4 with date_received through Oct 30), so the months-1-2 reading is final ~QE+7 and medtech prints run ~QE+25-40 (DXCM/GKOS ~QE+30, PODD/TNDM ~QE+36), lead 18-33 days with the record's 14 at the floor and the unverified claim that a third of MDRs file late eroding completeness; S: MDR velocity is driven by installed base, summary-reporting batches, duplicate root-cause reports and litigation, the cost channel to gross margin is negligible until a recall that is priced on its own day, and the vetter demoted it to a conditioning flag at 2; C: MAUDE spikes are cited anecdotally by sell-side and routinely by short sellers, two recall-prediction papers exist (West J Emerg Med 2025, GWU thesis) plus an Innolitics alerts tool, no equity-signal vendor, so a known series with a cheaper normalized version; U: 25-35 names, ~2-3%; H: openFDA from 1991 with date_received, but publication dates are not preserved and late filings are backfilled into the snapshot, a minor look-ahead; G: openFDA government open data.
justifications.lead: Month-2 MDRs due by end of month 3, published within ~1 week: reading final ~QE+7. Typical release QE+30-36. Lead ~23-29 days (18-33). Record claims 14.

justifications.text: A: openFDA device event, recall and 510(k) endpoints 200 (record TESTED HERE with curl -g) and the openFDA key is verified in the facts sheet; L: months 1-2 are complete ~37 days after month-2 end (30-day MDR deadline plus ~1 week openFDA publication, record TESTED HERE last_updated Nov 4 with date_received through Oct 30), giving 21-34 days before typical medtech releases, record claims 14, both in 14-27; S: MDR velocity is dominated by installed-base growth, summary-reporting batches, duplicates and litigation filings, and the cost channel is nil until a recall that is priced on its own day (record's own 2); C: MAUDE is public and cited anecdotally by sell-side, two recall-prediction papers and tooling (Innolitics alerts) exist, no vendor sells the equity version, so a known series with a finer version; U: 25-35 names ≈ 2-2.7%; H: data from 1991 but late-filed MDRs and openFDA record updates make an as-of reconstruction by date_received only approximately point-in-time; G: openFDA official API.
justifications.lead: Month-2 (Aug) events must be reported within 30 days (by Sep 30); openFDA publishes weekly with ~1 week lag → months-1-2 reading ~Oct 7. Q3 releases: DXCM ~Oct 30 (23d), TNDM ~Nov 5 (29), PODD ~Nov 6 (30), GKOS/INSP/IRTC/PEN/NVST ~Oct 28-Nov 6 (21-30). Record claims 14 → 14-27 band → 4; the unverified claim that about a third of MDRs file late means the reading keeps moving after the cutoff.

concerns: data-engineer: Product-code to company mapping and installed-base normalization are the real engineering work; event_type filtering is needed to strip summary-report batches. Late MDR filings mean the historical file is more complete than the real-time view was, so backtests should drop reports whose date_received is after the measurement date and accept a residual bias.

quant-pm: The literature supports recall prediction, not an earnings-day channel; the recall-day move likely absorbs the effect. Reporting mechanics (summary batches, installed-base growth) dominate the series. Useful as a put-sizing conditioning flag only. Overlaps S24 in the merge step.

skeptic: Demoted by the record to a sizing flag; no literature supports an earnings-day channel. Manufacturer-name normalization in MAUDE is messy (subsidiaries, contract manufacturers). Two months of signal per quarter with a 50% threshold on counts that batch and duplicate.

rows.name: Earnings-date scheduling behaviour versus the firm's filing history

justifications.text: A: EDGAR daily index and latest-8-K atom feed DATA, Business Wire and PR Newswire RSS TESTED 200 in record, Yahoo calendarEvents DATA via anonymous crumb, Alpha Vantage key verified (25 calls/day shared per IP, one call covers the calendar), Nasdaq calendar DATA but demoted to cross-check, SEC User-Agent not yet set but trivial; L: record 7 days, the EDGAR delay feature fires only once the firm's prior-two-year median filing date plus 5 days has passed so the release follows within 0-20 days, and late confirmers are by definition under 10 days; S: record signal_noise 3, literature-backed timing behaviour (Bagnoli-Kross-Watts 2002, Johnson-So 2018) with vendor-estimate noise; C: Wall Street Horizon and FactSet sell date revisions, published since 2002 and used by quant funds, record crowdedness 1; U: record ~100%, all ~1,300 names for the EDGAR leg; H: EDGAR daily indexes give point-in-time 8-K Item 2.02 dates back to 2004 for the delay leg, but the confirmation leg is 'recent items only; build forward' (RSS) and 'forward-looking only' (Yahoo), so half the feature set has no history; G: EDGAR clean, Nasdaq api robots Disallow / (critic amber, EDGAR dates primary), Yahoo quoteSummary is an undocumented crumb handshake, Alpha Vantage prohibits redistribution, newswire RSS terms unread.
justifications.lead: Delay feature: flag = no 8-K by (prior-two-year same-quarter median filing date + 5 days); the release then lands 0-20 days later, typically under 10. Confirmation feature: companies confirm 14-28 days ahead, but the 'late' class is confirmed fewer than 10 days before the event. Record states 7.

justifications.text: A: EDGAR daily index and 8-K atom DATA, Business Wire and PR Newswire RSS TESTED HERE 200, Yahoo calendarEvents DATA, Alpha Vantage key verified, SEC User-Agent a trivial header; L: the delay feature fires at the prior-two-year median 8-K date plus 5 days and a late filer's print follows days to two weeks later, the late-confirmation feature is by definition announced fewer than 10 days before the event, and the record's 7 sits in the 7-13 band; S: a behavioural timing proxy backed by Bagnoli, Kross and Watts 2002 and Johnson and So 2018 but small, loading on small and distressed firms already visible via NT 10-Q, with free calendar dates being vendor estimates rather than confirmations; C: Wall Street Horizon DateBreaks and FactSet sell date revisions, the effect has been published since 2002, Deltix/TABB replicated it and quant funds use it, so the record's own phase-1 crowdedness of 1 stands; U: all ~1,300 names for the EDGAR delay feature; H: EDGAR 8-K dates are point-in-time to 2004 for the delay feature, but the confirmation-lateness feature is forward-only with no free point-in-time history; G: facts sheet legal amber for N35 because the Nasdaq calendar API (robots Disallow: /) is kept as a cross-check, the Yahoo anonymous crumb is undocumented and Alpha Vantage prohibits redistribution, so clean only if EDGAR and newswire RSS are the sole sources.
justifications.lead: Feature (a): final at prior-two-year median 8-K date +5 days; late filer's print typically 5-15 days later. Feature (b): final at confirmation, which is <10 days before the print by definition. Record claims 7.

justifications.text: A: EDGAR daily index and 8-K atom feed are free and keyless (User-Agent trivial), Business Wire and PR Newswire RSS 200 (record TESTED HERE), but the confirmation feature needs free-text parsing of RSS items and Yahoo's undocumented crumb handshake, Alpha Vantage key verified, Nasdaq calendar robots-disallowed and treated as absent; L: the EDGAR delay feature is only known once the firm passes its median-plus-5-day date, typically 1-7 days before the actual release, and the late-confirmation feature is known at T-10 at the earliest, record claims 7, lower of the two legs sits in 2-6; S: a timing signal with benign causes (acquisitions, auditor changes, calendar shifts), small effect and vendor-estimate noise, an indirect proxy with sign ambiguity; C: Bagnoli-Kross-Watts 2002 and Johnson-So 2018 published, sold by Wall Street Horizon and tracked by FactSet, used by quant funds (record's own text), so heavily published and sold; U: ~1,300 names for the EDGAR feature; H: EDGAR 8-K filing dates point-in-time to 2004 for the delay feature while the confirmation leg is forward-only; G: EDGAR and newswire feeds are public but Yahoo quoteSummary is an undocumented endpoint behind a crumb handshake and Nasdaq's robots.txt disallows everything (facts sheet amber), so ambiguous.
justifications.lead: Delay feature: fires when no 8-K Item 2.02 has been filed by the firm's prior-two-year median filing date plus 5 days; the actual release then typically follows within 1-7 days → 2-6 band. Confirmation feature: 'confirmed fewer than 10 days before the event' is determinable at T-10 at the earliest → 7-13 band. Record claims 7; lower of the two legs → 2.

concerns: data-engineer: Effect is published for two decades and sold by vendors, so expect it to be priced for liquid names; its value here is as a conditioning variable. The confirmation leg needs a daily RSS archive built from scratch. Alpha Vantage's 25/day shared-IP quota must be reserved for the one calendar call.

quant-pm: Heavily published and sold since 2002; assume priced for liquid names, with any residual in sub-$5B names small relative to the costs of a sub-$10k options account. Keep strictly as a conditioning variable. Drop the Nasdaq calendar to clear the robots conflict.

skeptic: The confirmation leg has no history and must be built forward from RSS archives. Priced for two decades in liquid names; whatever remains loads on small, thinly covered firms already flagged by NT 10-Q filings. Transaction costs on a sub-$10k account dwarf the documented effect; useful only as a conditioning variable.

rows.name: Mid-quarter non-earnings 8-K items as a negative-surprise flag

justifications.text: A: EDGAR submissions API (items field, acceptanceDateTime), latest-8-K atom feed, daily index and Form 3/4/5 bulk data all DATA in the working-sources file, FDA warning letters page 200, keyless with a declared User-Agent under 10 req/s; L: anchor-1 clause applies, the 8-K is itself the public disclosure and the record says the filing-day move is priced (Lerman-Livnat 2010), critic notes the earnings-window residual is reasoned not shown, so lead over public disclosure is 0 even though filings arrive 10-70 days before earnings; S: record signal_noise 2, 2.05/2.06 have no sign prior, 4.01 dropped, residual after the filing-day return is the open question; C: record 2, sec-api.io and Audit Analytics sell 8-K item and restatement data, quant funds parse items in-house; U: record 100% of ~1,300 names; H: 8-K item codes since Aug 2004 with acceptanceDateTime in the submissions API and daily index from 1994, point-in-time by construction; G: SEC public data, User-Agent and rate rule only.
justifications.lead: Filings are public within 4 business days of the event and the record's window closes 5 trading days before the release, so the last qualifying filing is 7+ calendar days ahead and typical flags arrive 10-70 days ahead. But the measured object is the filing itself, which is priced on its filing day; lead over public disclosure = 0 days, per the anchor's explicit clause.

justifications.text: A: EDGAR submissions API items field and acceptanceDateTime DATA, 8-K atom feed, daily index and Form 345 bulk all DATA with only a declared User-Agent under 10 req/s; L: the window closes 5 trading days (~7 calendar) before the print by construction and filings are public within 4 business days of the event, but the facts sheet flags that this lead is over a filing priced on its own filing day with the earnings-window residual reasoned not shown, which the anchors treat as the 0-1 day case, so 2 as the blend; S: 4.02, 2.04, 3.01 and CFO/CAO departures are real EPS-risk disclosures, but Lerman and Livnat 2010 show an efficient filing-day reaction, Audit Analytics shows positive post-restatement drift, and the flag loads on size, momentum and distress, per the record's 2; C: sec-api.io sells 8-K item search, Audit Analytics restatement and officer-departure datasets are widely used, quant funds and news-analytics vendors parse items in-house, and the literature is published; U: 100% of the ~1,300 names (the negative flag fires for 2-4% of firm-quarters); H: 8-K item codes since August 2004 via the point-in-time daily index; G: SEC public data with the User-Agent rule.
justifications.lead: Last qualifying 8-K accepted up to T-5 trading days (~T-7 calendar); events public within 4 business days and typically 10-70 days before the print. Lead over public disclosure is zero (the 8-K is the disclosure); lead over the print is ~7 days at the window close. Record claims 20.

justifications.text: A: EDGAR submissions API returns JSON with 8-K item codes and acceptanceDateTime, free and keyless, only a declared User-Agent needed (facts sheet: not yet set, trivial); L: the anchor's explicit case applies, the predictor is a public 8-K filing priced on its filing day (Lerman and Livnat 2010 in the record) and the facts sheet flags N27's lead as filing-day news whose earnings-window residual is reasoned not shown, so the 10-70 day gap to the earnings 8-K is not a lead over public disclosure; S: item flags are structured and direct but as predictors of the earnings-day residual they are indirect with sign ambiguity (impairments excluded from adjusted EPS, kitchen-sink then relief, Audit Analytics positive post-restatement drift); C: quant funds and news-analytics vendors parse 8-K items, sec-api.io sells item search with published Item 4.02 CARs and Audit Analytics sells restatement and CFO-departure datasets, so commonly used and sold by several vendors; U: every filer in the ~1,300-name universe; H: 8-K item codes since August 2004 with acceptance timestamps and daily-index point-in-time backfill; G: SEC public data.
justifications.lead: Items are public within 4 business days of the event and 10-70 days before the Item 2.02 8-K under the record's window (which ends 5 trading days before the release). But the predictor is itself a public filing priced on its filing day (Lerman and Livnat 2010; sec-api.io Item 4.02 CARs), so by the anchor the lead over public disclosure is 0 → 1.

concerns: data-engineer: Scored L=1 strictly on the anchor text and the critic's N27 note; if the ranking step treats the earnings-day residual as the target, the record's 20-day figure would put it at 4, so this criterion drives the spread for this signal. Data engineering is the cleanest in the batch (structured, keyless, timestamped, universe-wide); the 5.02 CFO/CAO text classifier is the only build cost. Best use is as a control for the other signals.

quant-pm: The earnings-day residual after the filing-day move may be zero or positive (kitchen-sink quarter then relief); 25-50 events a quarter across the universe but few per name. Best used as a control and conditioning flag for the other signals rather than a standalone 2-10 day trade. Overlaps S31 in the merge step.

skeptic: The earnings-day residual after controlling for the filing-day return may be zero or positive. The negative-flag set fires for only 2-4% of firm-quarters (25-50 events a quarter) and loads on size, momentum and distress. Best use is as a control for the other signals, which the record already concedes.

rows.name: Retailer promotional-email cadence and depth index

justifications.text: A: mailbox-only after Milled dropped (milled.com and /terms 403, robots disallows /search and /sites/); IMAP fetch is codeable but subscribing two persona mailboxes to ~150 retailer lists is manual form work and emails are unstructured, rules-parsed text, UNPROBED by nature; L: vet_changes (2) defines the score as last 14 days of the fiscal quarter over weeks 1-10, so the reading is final at quarter end +1, 20-35 days before specialty-retail prints, which contradicts the record's lead_time_days=1 (that is only the measurement point); S: record signal_noise 2, one mailbox sees one personalized treatment, promotions follow planned calendars, heavy promo can accompany strong demand (sign ambiguity); C: MailCharts sells promotion-rate-vs-last-year per brand, Hedgeye counts promo emails, sell-side runs weekly promo checks on large names (record vet_changes 6); U: ~60 tradable mid-caps = 4.6% of 1,300 (100 collected including large-cap controls); H: history_depth 'From subscription date forward; no backfill', facts sheet lists N48 as forward-collection-only with no lawful backfill; G: own-mailbox data is lawfully obtained and Milled is dropped, mild flag for persona mailboxes and unread retailer email terms.
justifications.lead: Score = promo intensity in the last 14 days of the fiscal quarter / weeks 1-10 average (vet_changes 2), so the full-quarter reading is final the day after fiscal quarter end. Specialty apparel/footwear/home quarters end ~Oct 31-Nov 1 and prints land ~Nov 19-Dec 5 (REASONED typical: 19-35 days). Lead ~20-34 days. The record's lead_time_days=1 reflects 'final reading the day before earnings' and is a measurement point, not when the information is final.

justifications.text: A: own IMAP mailbox is free and parseable but requires manual subscription to ~150 retailer lists with two personas each, is UNPROBED by design, and the Milled backfill was dropped (403, robots Disallow, paid Pro archive); L: the hypothesis scores the last 14 days of each retailer's fiscal quarter against weeks 1-10, so the reading is final at fiscal quarter-end, 19-34 days before typical specialty-retail prints (REASONED); the record's own 1-day figure is the trade date, not data finality; S: record lowered to 2 for personalization (one mailbox sees one treatment), planned promo calendars already in guidance, and heavy promo accompanying strong demand; C: MailCharts sells per-brand 'promotion rate vs last year', Milled, EDITED and DataWeave sell promo/markdown data, Hedgeye counts promo emails and sell-side runs weekly promo checks on large names (record vendors); U: ~60 mid-cap names after excluding large caps used as controls = 4.6% of the universe; H: forward collection only with no lawful backfill per the context list; G: receiving broadcast email one subscribed to is clean, mild flag for persona accounts and unread retailer email terms.
justifications.lead: Reading is final at fiscal quarter-end (all quarter emails received). Specialty retailers with Oct-31 quarter ends print ~Nov 20 to Dec 5 (REASONED typical): 20 to 35 days. Calendar-quarter DTC names print ~Nov 5-12: 35-42 days. Record claims 1 day because it measures at T-1; by data finality the lead is 14-27+ days, so L=4 (not 5 because the Oct-quarter names cluster at 20-27).

justifications.text: A: free IMAP mailbox but requires manual subscription of ~150-300 retailer lists (two personas each) and HTML-email parsing; nothing probed (record: UNPROBED, user-side); L: reading is finalized the day before earnings by design (facts sheet flags the 1-day claim); S: indirect proxy with sign ambiguity (heavy promotion accompanies strong demand), personalization and planned calendars per the record's own red team; C: MailCharts sells 'promotion rate vs last year' per brand, Hedgeye counts promo emails, sell-side runs weekly promo checks on the large names; U: ~60 tradable mid-caps (~4.6%), at the top of the 13-60 band; H: forward collection only, Milled backfill dropped (403, paid archive, robots disallow); G: Milled dropped but terms of ~150 retailers' email programs unread and persona subscriptions are ambiguous (Phase 1 legal 2).
justifications.lead: Promo-intensity index is computed daily through T-1; the full-quarter (last-14-day escalation) reading is final 1 day before the print for every covered name. 0-1 day band.

concerns: data-engineer: Record is internally inconsistent on lead time (lead_time_days 1 vs the vet-defined quarter-end score). No history can exist until a year of own collection; the hypothesis cannot be backtested today. The task's read-only/no-forms constraint means the subscription step must be done by the user, not by code from here. Personalization detection via two personas halves usable names further.

quant-pm: Four quarters of own history before any YoY read; first live use is cross-sectional with ~60 names and no backtest, so it cannot be graded for at least a year. Personalization drift (two-persona divergence test) may shrink the usable set. Record's 1-day lead claim is inconsistent with its own hypothesis window; scored on the hypothesis. Milled archive is a paid, robots-restricted product and must stay out. Edge, if any, is confined to thinly covered mid-caps where XRT-relative moves on margin are modest.

skeptic: Same single-mailbox mechanism family the critic flagged for S21/N33 (one treatment of a segmented program). No lawful backfill exists, so the YoY version cannot be tested for a year and the cross-sectional stand-in is untested. Coverage counts ~100 collected names but only ~60 are tradable after removing large caps used as controls.

rows.name: Securitization-trust 10-D monthly servicer reports (CarMax, CNH)

justifications.text: A: EDGAR company-search atom PROBED 200 with declared UA, submissions API and daily index DATA; TESTED HERE: the UNPROBED ABS-EE atom for CarMax Auto Owner Trust 2020-3 (CIK 0001814294) returned 200 (15 KB) listing monthly ABS-EE filings on ~15th of each month (2023-09-15 through 2024-06-17 on the first page), so loan-level EX-102 XML is real; servicer reports are PDF/HTML exhibits needing parsing and the SEC User-Agent string is not yet set (trivial); L: CarMax month-3 10-D ~15th of the following month gives 4-26 days before its prints, median ~8-9, Harley month-3 10-D ~27 days after month-end lands on the print, CNH timing UNKNOWN; S: record signal_noise 3, securitized pools are selected seasoned subsets, management pre-guides provision direction, KMX reaction driven by comps/GPU; C: ABS desks and rating-agency surveillance read 10-Ds monthly, sec-api.io sells an ABS-EE dataset, but nobody maps it to the parent's equity print (record), so our version differs in alignment; U: KMX, CNH, HOG = 3 names (<1%); H: history_depth 'CarMax and Harley trusts since 2006' on EDGAR with daily-index filing timestamps (point-in-time by construction), ABS-EE since Nov 2016 (TESTED HERE monthly filings for 2020-3); G: SEC EDGAR public with fair-access limits and declared UA, no scraping conflict.

justifications.lead: TESTED HERE: CarMax Auto Owner Trust 2020-3 10-Ds filed 2023-09-15 (Aug), 2023-12-15 (Nov), 2024-03-15 (Feb), 2024-06-17 (May); CNH Equipment Trust 2021-C filed 2025-10-15 (Sep), 2026-01-15 (Dec). L kept at 4 despite the openings leg alone supporting 5 (median ~30 days from Q-end+7 to the 8-K 2.02 date, TESTED HERE via data.sec.gov): the 'net' count the hypothesis uses is not final until expirations post (~Q+38), which puts the composite at roughly -8 to +21 days; 4 is the honest blend. A, U, H, G kept: all primary endpoints answered 200 with structured JSON/CSV/XLSX; 13 names listed (~1%); Florida new-license files FY2016-17 onward with approval dates plus TABC original_issue_date back to 1937 but only latest status (closure history partial); state open data is clean but the record still carries the Nasdaq calendar leg. Record corrections: the Florida fiscal-year file is closed at June 30 (not 'updated continuously'); the live file is newfood.csv at /sto/file_download/extracts/, and the record's xlsx path (/hr/licensing/newfood_2526.xlsx) returns the site home page as HTML; the pending dataset's earliest submission is 2024-09-11, not March 2026.
verifier.refutation: The data are real, free, daily and historical, but the measured quantity is empty for the names it is supposed to cover. Matching TABC original licenses to the chains' actual operating entities (TESTED HERE) gives a Q3 2026 Texas count of 2 for Texas Roadhouse, 1 each for Kura Sushi and LongHorn, and zero for Chili's (3 originals since January 2024), Cheesecake Factory (none since July 2025), BJ's (none since May 2024), Outback (none since February 2025), First Watch, Portillo's and Dave & Buster's; Florida's live file adds 0-2 per chain since July. A quarter's 'net new TX+FL licensed units' is therefore an integer in {0,1,2,3}, so the hypothesis' 10% shortfall against guided pace is unresolvable: a single license is 33-100% of the reading, and the timing noise the record itself concedes (issue dates months before or after openings) swamps it. The only entity with real volume, Casey's (21 Q3 originals, 12 pending), is converting acquired Pak-A-Sak stores, so its license count tracks M&A, not organic growth, and the 'new license' label would read as unit-growth upside when it is not. The closure leg is worse: 34k of 129k TABC licenses sit in 'Expired - Original Required' and the status change posts a median 31 days after expiration, so the net count is not final until about Q+38, after most prints, and lapses (renewal timing) are indistinguishable from closures; the Florida 'closure' extract is sanitary emergency closures (roach activity), not business closures. Meanwhile every covered chain reports its own quarter-end unit count and development guidance in the same press release the trade targets, and sell-side already tracks 'coming soon' pages. The record also overstates the Florida leg (the fiscal-year file is a closed archive, its listed path returns HTML, and the pending-dataset history starts 2024-09 not 2026-03). Several cheap vendors already sell the raw TX filings. With S at 1 and C at 2 the signal has free, verifiable data attached to a quantity too sparse to trade; it should sit below the top ten.

verified.vendor_and_literature_check: One search (WebSearch, 'nuclear outage monitoring data vendor traders Genscape Yes Energy Platts NRC reactor status equity earnings surprise unplanned outage study'). Vendors found: EIA 'Status of U.S. Nuclear Outages' dashboard built on NRC data (daily since 2007 per its JSON config, TESTED HERE); S&P Global/Platts outage coverage; Genscape (now Wood Mackenzie) nuclear outage calls for NYISO (power-eng.com); Kpler blog on tracking live unplanned nuclear outages for trading; Montel on how desks fold outage data into dashboards. Literature: Stockholm University/IAEE extended abstract on unplanned outage drivers across 541 reactors 2003-2023 (capacity study, not equity); EIA Today in Energy pieces on summer nuclear outages. No paper or vendor product found that maps NRC unit-days to a utility earnings surprise; the record's Rothwell (1989) and TMI JFQA event studies are accident studies, not routine-outage earnings studies. Mechanism check from a second search on the one qualifying Talen event: Q2 2025 Susquehanna Unit 2 extended outage (~30 extra days, ~$30M incremental maintenance per management) coincided with Adjusted EBITDA of $90M, up $3M YoY, and 2025 guidance reaffirmed (ir.talenenergy.com Q2 2025 release), i.e. no negative surprise from the largest lost-EFPD quarter in the seven years of NRC data parsed here.
verified.refutation: The signal cannot be validated and the one test case failed. Parsing the NRC yearly files (TESTED HERE, 2020-2026 plus 1999) gives Susquehanna combined lost unit-days in non-refueling Q3 quarters of 0.8, 7.7, 3.1, 2.5, 6.7, 8.3 and 3.2: the hypothesis's 10-EFPD unplanned trigger never fired in a Q3 in seven years. Outside Q3 the large readings (U1 Q2 2020 41.1, U1 Q2 2022 39.4, U2 Q2 2025 67.8, U1 Q4 2023 10.9) are refueling quarters where separating 'unplanned' from planned needs the company's disclosed outage duration, which the record has no source for; at most two to four qualifying events in seven years, roughly one every two to three years, on a single merchant name. The clearest case, Q2 2025 (~30 extra days), was disclosed by management as a deliberate uprate investment, Adjusted EBITDA rose year over year and guidance was reaffirmed, so even the biggest event did not produce the predicted negative surprise. Dollar scale is also small: 10 EFPD at ~1,300 MW is ~310 GWh, roughly $12-16M at a $40-50/MWh margin, against quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of $90-363M, inside normal consensus dispersion, and hedge buy-backs can cut either way. The remaining five names are regulated with fuel riders (near-zero EPS effect, as the record itself says), so U is honestly 1. The data are repackaged daily by EIA since 2007 and sold by Kpler, Genscape, Platts and others, so the outage is priced the same morning; what is left is a 'consensus has not moved yet' conditioning that requires point-in-time consensus EPS and PJM LMPs, neither of which the record has an accessible source for. A rank of 1 of 59 rests on A, L, H and G, which are genuinely excellent, while the two things that make a signal tradable, sample size and effect size, are close to zero. At best this is a veto rule for long-into-earnings positions on one name, which does not justify the top slot.

Three specific problems: (1) the measured quantity is dominated by the vendor's own release cadence, since npm's own methodology note says mirrors and disposable-CI builds re-pull every new version and a release produces a burst, so quarter-over-quarter share-of-registry moves with how many versions a vendor shipped, which is unrelated to customer consumption; (2) under the vet-restricted primary spec the cross-section is nine tickers, several of which only listed in 2020-2021 (CFLT, BRZE, AMPL, FROG), leaving roughly 150-200 name-quarters for a test that must control for consensus revisions, size, momentum and NRR, so even a true small effect would be statistically invisible and a null result would be uninformative; (3) the npm series has permanent registry-wide holes (nine unfilled zero days in 2025, three inside Q3 2026, five in Oct-Nov 2026), and the 2025 holes appear in the registry totals but not in the twilio package series, so the share-of-registry ratio is undefined or distorted on those days unless carefully day-matched, which adds another analyst degree of freedom. Add that a real vendor (TickerTrends) already sells exactly this series with multi-year history to investors and commodity scrapers exist, so whatever information survives is unlikely to be unpriced. The honest description is a nearly free null test, not a top-ten candidate on expected value; at U=1 the weighted score falls to about 3.45, and any signal with S=2 and C=3 should be ranked below candidates whose mechanism is a direct driver even if their plumbing is worse.

verified.vendor_and_literature_check: Vendor search (TESTED HERE, web search): L.E.K. Consulting's WISE index (lek.com/insights/ind/us/ei/wise-approach-weather-related-services-demand) is built from NOAA severe-event counts plus degree days and is explicitly marketed to roofing providers 'and their investors'; its regression finds roofing shipments rise in the same quarter as the weather and show a larger decline two quarters later. PipelineOn (pipelineon.com/blog/roofing-storm-demand-statistics-2026/) publishes a free storm-demand formula of severe hail and wind events x exposed housing stock x roof value / contractor density built from NOAA, Census and BLS, which is essentially this signal's formula. Insurer- and contractor-facing hail products: Verisk Respond and 'State of America's Roofs' (hail >= 1 inch the dominant roof threat; cat hail about 33% of roof claims in 2025), Cotality (CoreLogic) 2026 Severe Convective Storm Risk Report, Cape Analytics Hail Intelligence, Canopy Weather, HailTrace, Flash Weather AI hail forecast tool, GAF WeatherHub. Trade literature: Roofing Contractor and Freedonia tie shingle demand to severe-weather reroofing; the Baird 2016 survey already cited hail and wind reports. No academic paper linking hail to building-products earnings surprises or returns was found (two searches). Net: the mechanism is commonly sold and at least one consulting index targets investors directly, so C=2 holds and could be argued to 1; the L.E.K. lag finding is adverse to the record's design (see refutation).
verified.refutation: Five arguments. (1) Crowded and formulaic: the exact construction (NOAA hail counts x Census housing stock) is published free by a roofing-marketing blog, L.E.K. sells a NOAA-based weather index to roofing investors, Verisk, Cotality, Cape, Canopy and HailTrace sell hail-exposure layers, Baird's survey has cited hail and wind reports since 2016, and OC and QXO narrate storm demand on every call and at mid-quarter conferences; the sign is in consensus, and the panel's own C=2 implies the magnitude edge is small. (2) The lag may be wrong-signed: the only quantitative treatment found (L.E.K. WISE) reports the roofing boost in the same quarter as the weather and a larger decline two quarters later, while the vet's design excludes the current month and weights the prior one to two quarters, which is exactly where L.E.K. finds payback; the trailing two-to-three-quarter blend therefore mixes a positive and a negative term, and the record's REASONED one-to-nine-month claims-to-reroof lag has no test behind it. (3) Coverage is two names and both are diluted: OC's roofing is one of three segments and asphalt pass-through and price often dominate volume; QXO now consolidates Kodiak (from Apr 2026) and TopBuild (from Jul 2026), so roofing is a shrinking share and year-over-year comps are broken for the backtest and the next several prints; CSL is commercial single-ply membranes where hail-driven replacement is a weaker mechanism than shingles (REASONED). (4) Infrastructure fragility: the primary API answered 500 on every query today, the fallback files are labelled 'experimental', the hail-tiles aggregate carries a lightning-strike header, KNOWN_ISSUES records past gaps backfilled later, and MAXSIZE was once rounded to integers, which matters for a 1.5-inch threshold. (5) A short holding window around earnings is a poor way to monetise a slow, widely known demand pull: with a 30-50 day lead the information is in sell-side storm-comp adjustments and distributor commentary well before T-1, so the T-1 to T+2 residual the hypothesis targets may be near zero even if the fundamental link is real. Weighted score is unchanged at 3.55 after A down and L up, so the rank-6 placement is not obviously wrong, but items (2) and (3) are the ones that could make it wrong.

verified.refutation: The signal's headline virtue (tax-filed, location-level dollars) is real, but the thing the program trades, the quarter the company is about to report, is not in the file when it matters: for the Sept-2026 quarter every covered name printed before the Nov 7 refresh that completed September, and the same pattern holds in the March and June quarters; only the December quarter (printed mid/late February) and off-cycle KRUS (too few units) give a genuine full-quarter lead. What is actually available at T-5 is two months of alcohol-only receipts (10-35% of sales) from one state (10-25% of units), with the mixed-beverage sales tax inside the numbers, no filing timestamps (so the backtest cannot reproduce what was knowable, and late/amended returns are silently revised), and a ~38-40-day completeness rule inferred from a single snapshot on a portal with no published refresh cadence. A signal whose full-quarter read is usually final after the print, that covers under 1% of names, and whose history cannot be made point-in-time, does not belong in the top ten of 59.

S (TESTED HERE): the primary orders leg passes the record's own 40-event gate (156 qualifying orders at mines with >=20% of a controller's prior-year hours/tons, open 7+ days, 108 distinct controller-quarters since 2015), but 141 of the 156 (and 781 of 819 long-open orders of the three types at covered controllers) are 103(k) accident-control orders, which withdraw miners from the accident area and are routinely modified to let the rest of the mine run while the order stays open for the investigation; the file has no scope field (NO_AFFECTED is 0 for every one of the 781 long-open 103(k) orders, so it cannot be used to size them). Example: Warrior Mine No. 7 (0101401, 50-90% of Warrior's hours) carried 103(k) orders open 213 days (2017), 90 days (2022) and 84 days (2024) in quarters when it was Warrior's main producer. So 'order open 7+ days at a 20% mine' is not a measure of lost tons; the sign is ambiguous for the event that carries 90% of the sample, which is anchor 2 (indirect proxy with sign ambiguity), not anchor 3. The 7000-2 leg additionally reports hours only (no output) for the ~half of names that are metal/nonmetal. C (search TESTED HERE): S&P Global Platts/Market Intelligence runs a standing quarterly series of MSHA mine-level production notes published within days of each posting (e.g., 'IB Q3 output totals 16.8 million st, up 19.6% on quarter: MSHA' 2020-11-13; 'US coal production is trending lower year over year' 2026-09-18 citing H1 2026 MSHA reports), i.e. a major vendor republishes the exact series and coal sell-side already reads it; the same 104(d)/107(a)/103(k) order counts are mandatory issuer disclosures in every 10-Q Exhibit 95 (Dodd-Frank 1503) and 107(a) orders must be 8-K'd under Item 1.04 within 4 business days (EDGAR TESTED HERE: BTU 2026-10-16, AMR 2026-05-15, CNR 2026-05-19, HNRG 2026-06-03, ARLP 2026-04-07 all filed Item 1.04 8-Ks). TESTED HERE on the full post-2010 flat file: the 16 named filers produce 359 firm-quarters with at least one campaign since 2015, but the 1%-of-consensus-quarterly-revenue trigger needs on the order of 40k-160k hardware-remedy units in a quarter (HOG ~$1.1B quarterly revenue at $150-300 per unit, THO ~$2.4B), and only 19 firm-quarters reach 50k hardware-class units, 35 reach 25k, 8 reach 100k, and 1 reaches 250k. A 20-event sample cannot resolve a 50 bp gross-margin effect against the controls in the hypothesis, and the largest single event (THO 2017Q4, 1.47M units) would dominate any regression. Second, the lead is over information that is already public and, for campaigns this large, press-released and often quantified by the company at filing, so the earnings-day residual is reasoned not shown, exactly the pattern the Phase 1 critic flagged for N27 and N39. Third, the two names with the longest leads and most events, THO and WGO, have fiscal quarters (ending Oct/Jan/Apr/Jul and late Nov/Feb/May/Aug) that do not align with NHTSA's calendar-quarter completion reports, so the completion leg is unusable for them and lands 0-8 days before the prints of the calendar-quarter names, adding no lead. Fourth, per-unit remedy cost is unobservable and the corrective-action text is amended in place (no vintages, archive blocked), so the proxy's estimation error is larger than the effect being tested. With free data (A=5) and clean terms (G=5) carrying the score, this is a well-sourced dataset without a tradable event frequency; a signal that cannot produce 60 historical events should not sit above candidates that can.

Second, the mapping is weaker than 'one step removed': Cal-Maine's conventional eggs are formula-priced off Urner Barry/Expana, not the AMS index, and 44.4% of FY2026 net sales were specialty and prepared foods whose prices do not follow the index at all; PPC's cutout exposure is diluted by Mexico, Europe and prepared foods. Third, the inputs are the most-watched numbers in protein, published daily, and CALM's share price tracks the egg price through the quarter, so by the time the 31-53 day lead window opens the revenue direction is already in the price; the earnings-day move is driven by the dividend formula, feed cost and guidance tone, which the signal does not observe. Fourth, the universe is two tradable primary names (U=1), so even a correct signal gives perhaps eight events a year, too few to grade within the program's horizon, and the two names share one macro driver (HPAI/feed), so the events are not independent. verified.refutation: This signal should not be in the top ten because almost every path to a tradeable, backtestable edge is blocked. (1) Universe: the facts sheet caps it at seven named tickers, so at most 28 earnings events a year, and the hypothesis further restricts to quarters where a more-than-15% site-days drop was NOT disclosed by 8-K or press before T-20; the record's own red team expects 10 to 20 usable quarters in the whole 2019-2025 window, which cannot distinguish a real coefficient from polygon overfitting. (2) The equity-relevant event is disclosed: a line down at CLF, SXC or CENX is an 8-K or press release within days and sits in consensus by T-1, so the undisclosed residual is a partial run-rate that a 375 m thresholded active-fire detection (near-binary per overpass) cannot resolve. (3) The mechanism physically covers only three of the seven names (CLF blast furnaces and EAFs, SXC coke ovens, EXP kilns); CENX aluminium potlines, OLN chlor-alkali cells, LXU ammonia reformers and TROX pigment reactors are enclosed processes that are weak IR emitters at VIIRS resolution (REASONED), so effective coverage is three names. (4) It is not uncrowded: VNF per-mill profiles for 1,000-plus steel mills including a US mill are published by Elvidge and the Payne Institute, the nightly data behind them is freely distributed by EOG, and Earth-i, SatVu, LaGrand, Kayrros and Wood Mackenzie sell plant thermal activity to traders; whatever edge remains is the REASONED claim that nobody bothers with sub-$5B single-site names. (5) Data continuity is worse than the record states: S-NPP FIRMS production ceased 2 November 2026, so the record's primary URL now returns nothing new, the 2012-2017 history is S-NPP only, and live collection must move to NOAA-20/21 with different overpass times; the backtest archive is standard processing that replaces NRT with a 2-5 month lag and differs in geolocation and granule completeness; and the Black Marble secondary is 9 days behind, not 1-2. (6) The lead time is genuine but ordinary (17 to 35 days) and the hypothesis fixes T-20, no better than several higher-coverage physical signals. A signal with one-percent coverage, a near-binary noisy residual, published mechanism, vendor competition, and a sensor transition in the month it would go live does not belong above signals that trade dozens of names each quarter.
