verified.refutation: The signal cannot be validated for at least four quarters and may never be backtested on the event it actually trades. The openFDA shortages endpoint is current-state only and, as measured here, purges Resolved rows after roughly three months (59 Resolved rows, all stamped 2026-07-31 to 2026-11-04); the posting-year histogram (2024: 11 rows, 2019: 20) shows most historical entries are gone. The hypothesis trades NEW competitor entries in the last eight weeks of a quarter that are still open at quarter end; the short-lived entries that produce the sharpest spot-price effects are exactly the ones already deleted, so any in-sample result today is survivorship-biased and web.archive.org is denied from this container. Second, the list is dominated by persistent entries (ASPE median injectable shortage 4.6 years; 824 of 1,586 rows are bulk 'Reverified'), and new entries run 25-55 per month across 227 molecules, so per covered company the count of relevant molecule-level events per quarter is in the low single digits, below the resolution needed to beat consensus dispersion for a company with dozens of products. Third, coverage is 5-7 names and two of them (ANIP, PRGO) have no shortage rows as suppliers at all, so their 'exposure' is inferred from NDC label counts, which the record itself admits is not market share. Fourth, the beneficiaries are capacity-limited and sell under GPO contracts, so a competitor's entry adds price on spot volume only, and management already flags shortage upside on the prior call; USP, Vizient and ASHP publish the same shortage facts to the people who set hospital demand. Fifth, the lead time is solid for the typical name but AMRX's Q2 print (Jul 30, day 30) leaves only 25 days at the day-5 measurement. A signal with U=1, H=2, S=2 and a mechanism no paper has tested belongs outside the top ten regardless of its clean accessibility and legal scores.

verified.refutation: The signal's premise, that the registry gives a near-final US delivery count within a week of quarter end, is false on the data itself. The FAA registration certificate is issued when the Aircraft Registration Branch processes the paperwork, not when the airframe is handed over; new aircraft fly for up to 90 days on the applicant's temporary copy. Measured on the Nov 10 snapshot, the certificate date trails the airworthiness date by a median 36 days for Citations, only 12% within a week, so at QE+7 roughly half of the quarter's US deliveries are missing and the count is padded with the prior quarter's tail; 38 days after Q3 2026 ended and 12 days after Textron printed, only 14 of the quarter's Citations were on the register against 51 reported. The late-quarter slip, the one thing not in consensus and the only reason to trade this, is exactly the portion the registry cannot see in time. Even the snapshot's cleanest version of the count (all certs dated inside the quarter) tracks reported jets at an unstable 51%-111% ratio across seven quarters and got the Q1-to-Q2 2026 direction wrong; the turboprop leg captures 15-25% of reported units and is useless; the YEAR MFR filter counts resales of year-old airframes as deliveries; and there is no point-in-time archive to calibrate any of this, so the trailing-8-quarter scaling ratio the hypothesis relies on cannot be estimated without survivorship bias. On top of that the mechanism is a single name with four observations a year, Aviation is 40-45% of revenue, the Q3 2025 print moved on Bell and Industrial, sell-side already models deliveries from backlog (Jefferies estimates are quoted in the trade press), Radar publishes free model-level registry counts monthly under CC BY, and JETNET, AMSTAT, Apify and ai-analytics resell the same file. A $0-budget overlay that reads half a quarter, mis-signs direction, cannot be backtested and covers 0.1% of the universe does not belong in the top ten.

ranking_disputes: Rubric weights (implied A 0.20, L 0.20, S 0.20, C 0.15, U 0.10, H 0.10, G 0.05) give plumbing (A+L+H+G) 55% and tradability (S+U) 30%, and the rubric has no criterion for event frequency, so rows with S=2 and U=1 (N03, N22, G02, N09) and rows with one or two qualifying events every few years (N15: trigger never fired in a Q3 in seven years; N22: 15-25 events in eleven years against its own 60-event gate) occupy six of the top ten. The verifiers for N09, N03 and N15 each named this as a rubric artefact rather than evidence the signals work.

Four of the top ten carry verifier_stay=false (N18 at rank 1, N03 at 4, N22 at 6, G02 at 7): the verifiers argued each should leave the top ten, but their findings (missing consensus comparison variable, 3-4 usable permits, event count below the abandon gate, purged shortage history) landed on U or on unscored properties and moved W by 0 to 0.10, so the arithmetic kept them. N18 in particular rose to rank 1 on L moving 4 to 5 while the verifier showed the hypothesis as written cannot be run from the named sources.

The four-way tie at W 3.35 (S33, S04, S16, N55) was broken by an undocumented rule (not W_panel, not S, not H) that leaves N55 at rank 11 and S16 at rank 10. N55 has S=3 and U=2 (25-40 names, A=5, H=4); S16 has S=2 after a live check that was wrong-signed for two of three names. On the two criteria that measure whether a signal trades, N55 is the stronger row and should at least be carried as the first alternate.

Merges were executed on panel scores before verification, so S07 (final W 3.55) and N26 (final W 3.50) were folded into survivors that now score lower (N03 3.50, N22 3.40) and neither merged row was ever verifier-tested; this contradicts the facts-sheet rule of keeping the higher-scoring member. N26 (U=2, 25-35 medtech names, L=4, H=4) is arguably a better occupant of the N22 slot than N22 (U=1, nine active names) and should be re-opened if N22 fails its 60-event gate.

S33 (rank 8) and S04 (rank 9) entered the top ten only because four panel-top-ten rows were demoted, and neither received a verifier refutation pass; their S=3 and S33's U=3 are REASONED panel medians (coverage 'perhaps 120-150 names', '8-12 names with verifiably exclusive berths'), the only unverified scores in the top ten. Their ranks are therefore less certain than the rank-11 to rank-15 rows that were counted.

Seven of the ten carry U=1 (N18, N15, N50, N03, N09, N22, G02, plus S04 at U=1), so the arithmetic lets single-site family members with four events a year each (N18, N15, N03) outrank broad rows (N55 25-40 names, N32 20 names, N27/N35 universe-wide) on lead time and plumbing alone; the facts sheet's instruction not to inflate pooled-family coverage was followed per row, but the ranking still rewards the family's shared lead-time advantage ten times over.

Verifier texts reference stale ranks (N15 'rank 1 of 59', N50 'rank-6', N03 'rank-2', N09 'rank 4', N21 'rank-8', S16 'rank 5'), confirming the verifiers worked from panel ranks before cross-row adjustments; the final order was never seen by any verifier, so no one has checked the top ten as a set.
concerns: Shared unsolved dependency: five of the ten hypotheses (N18, N15, S33, N22, S16, and N09's controls) compare against or condition on point-in-time consensus, and no $0 source with history exists; Nasdaq returns null for CALM, Alpha Vantage is 25 calls/day shared per IP, FMP's consensus history is unverified, and the Nasdaq calendar carries a robots flag. Phase 3 must either start daily consensus snapshots now or Phase 4 must respecify every one of these rows against reported YoY/sequential or guidance-midpoint stand-ins.

Shared harness: every top-ten row needs the EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 release-date harness and the SEC User-Agent string, which the facts sheet lists as not yet set; it is trivial but blocks all ten at once, and S33 additionally depends on the intermittent efts.sec.gov full-text search.

Verifier coverage asymmetry: only the panel top ten were refuted; the demoted rows were replaced by S33 and S04 (and nearly N55), which were never refuted. Phase 3 should run a verifier pass on S33, S04 and N55 before sourcing effort is spent.

Forward-collection-only in the top ten: G02 is flagged forward_collection_only (shortage history purged after ~3 months; four quarters of daily snapshots needed before any trade) and S04's live leg is de facto forward-only (NOAA archive stops at 2024, 2025-2026 gap, aisstream must be self-archived from day one). Both collectors must start today or they lose history daily; neither can produce a backtestable trade inside the program's first year.

Keys and accounts outstanding: PJM Data Miner 2 (N15, not created), SEC User-Agent (all), api.data.gov/SAM key for S16's cross-check (DEMO_KEY 404), Google Cloud/BigQuery (N09 PyPI backfill, not created, optional); API Ninjas transcripts are premium-only per the facts sheet, so S33's transcript leg is dead and the record's source list is wrong on that point.

Infrastructure fragility found by verifiers: NCEI SWDI web service returned 500 on all calls (N50 must use the undocumented bulk CSVs and the hail-tiles aggregate carries a lightning-strike header); the EIA nuclear outages.csv URL returns HTML (N15 crowding cross-check); ECHO's DMR custom-data endpoint is unusable as called (N03 must use 264-645 MB annual zips); npm registry totals have permanent zero-day holes (N09).

Legal amber inside the top ten: S04 (aisstream has no terms page; G=3), S33 (Nasdaq calendar leg, use EDGAR-derived dates), N09 (npm terms silent on the downloads API, crawler policy permits <=1 req/s, pypistats is third-party). None is red, but S04's live source is the only top-ten source with no terms at all.

Statistical power: excluding S33's reasoned 120-150 names, the other nine rows together reach roughly 60-70 distinct tradeable names (about 5% of the 1,300 universe) at four events a year each, and the verifiers measured N15 at roughly one qualifying event every two to three years and N22 at 15-25 events in eleven years. Phase 4 should decide up front whether a pooled single-site-family harness counts as one specification or whether per-row event-count gates apply, because most of the top ten fail the latter.

Record bookkeeping: N18's verifier text says H 5 -> 4 but the panel median was already 4 (only L changed); N44's and N50's verifier texts contain record corrections (Florida file paths, OC release dates) that the compact records still carry wrong; Phase 3 should apply the verifier corrections to the records before sourcing.
critic.balance_note: Lens: four physical (N18, N15, N50, S04), four regulatory (N03, N22, G02, S16), one digital (N09), one second-order (S33); the facts sheet's single-site physical family contributes N18, N15 and N03 directly and N50 and S04 are single-berth or two-name physical rows in all but name, so half the top ten shares one test harness and one failure mode (four events a year per name). Sector: consumer staples protein (N18), merchant nuclear (N15), roofing (N50), single-site chemicals and pulp (N03), infrastructure software (N09), RV/powersports/truck OEMs (N22), generic injectables (G02), government services (S16), coal/fertilizer/LNG terminals (S04), and cross-sector thin-coverage customers (S33); no restaurant, retail, consumer-discretionary digital or universe-wide conditioning row survived, and eight of ten are physical-economy industrial, materials, energy or staples names. Coverage: seven of ten have U=1, only S33 (reasoned ~120-150) and S16 (15-20) exceed a dozen names. Forward-collection-only: G02 is flagged and S04's live leg is effectively forward-only; both collectors must start on day one. Shared-harness dependencies across all ten: the SEC User-Agent and EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 date harness, and a point-in-time consensus source that does not yet exist at $0.
critic.main_uncertainty: Whether Phase 4 treats the single-site rows (N15, N03, N22, N18) as specifiable despite single-digit qualifying-event counts, that is, whether a pooled family harness counts as a surviving specification or each row must pass its own event-count and consensus-comparison gates; per-row survival estimates (N09 0.65, N18 0.55, N50 0.55, S33 0.50, S16 0.45, G02 0.40, N15 0.35, S04 0.35, N22 0.30, N03 0.25) sum to about 4.4 expected survivors, and the unresolved point-in-time consensus dependency, which five hypotheses share, is the single factor most likely to push that below five.
